Measured on dev-georgios (62 GiB, MemAvailable about 18 GB while measuring) with a cell that allocates 64 × 1 GiB `Uint8Array`s (limits/runaway-64gib-cell-fails-cleanly): in a systemd scope with `MemoryMax=3G MemorySwapMax=0` the native-host runner was killed by the kernel before (signal 9 after 4.0 s, max RSS 3.14 GB) and after fails the cell with `Script stopped: the cell ran out of memory.` in 1.09 s at max RSS 1.60 GB and runs the next cell; `nanocode exec` in the same scope (output/cm-conf native-cli through a wrapper) died with no result before and reports the clean failure and the next cell after; with no limit both builds stop at djs's arena (max RSS 3.69 GB, 3.9 and 4.1 s). The cap is read once, so cellbench is unchanged by it. Conformance: limits/runaway-64gib-cell-fails-cleanly passes on all four hosts; the cap cases (oom-uncatchable-no-catch-no-finally, oom-keeps-earlier-output, oom-keeps-earlier-cells-store, oom-next-cell-runs, heap-cap-is-per-cell) now configure 32 MiB and run on every host instead of ts-workerd only, and oom-configured-cap runs on native-cli too (cli/run.ts passes cell_memory_bytes as NANOCODE_CELL_MEMORY); the native runner restores `cell_memory()` after a configured case instead of `usize::MAX`. Not solved: several runaway cells at once can still together take more than is available, since each has its own cap. Commands: as for the store() writes entry below, plus `cargo clippy --offline --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-cli -- -D warnings`. Files: crates/runtime/code-mode-engine/src/{memory.rs,cell.rs,lib.rs}, crates/runtime/code-mode/src/code_mode/mod.rs, crates/nanocode/src/tools.rs, bin/nanocode/src/{cells.rs,lib.rs}.

- fix(code-mode): `store()` throws a TypeError for a value nested deeper than serde_json reads, and a cell journal header reads each stored value with its own recursion budget (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 Code Mode conformance track: limits policy). serde_json reads a `RawValue` without counting depth but a `Value` to at most 127 levels of arrays, and the session map reaches `Value` in a cell journal header (`CellJournalHeader.stored`). So a value nested 128 levels or more was kept in memory and silently left out of a revived cell's header (`stored_json` drops what does not parse), and one nested 125 to 127 levels, which sits three containers deep inside a `CellJournalUpdate`, made the update unreadable: nanocode-ts failed the turn with `durability store failed: turn log state is invalid: cell journal update: recursion limit exceeded at line 1 column 538`. STORE now parses the value as a `serde_json::Value` before keeping it and throws `TypeError: Unable to store "key": recursion limit exceeded at line 1 column 128`, the limit and wording a nested tool input past it already gets (`invalid tool input: recursion limit exceeded`); `CellJournalHeader.stored` deserializes through `stored_values`, which reads the map as raw values and parses each one on its own, so the header's nesting no longer counts against a value (the field's type and the journal's bytes are unchanged). Conformance: limits/store-nested-past-json-limit-throws and limits/store-nested-past-json-limit-uncaught-fails-cell (128 levels) stored the value before and throw after on all four hosts; limits/store-deepest-value-survives-restart (127 levels, a timer crash and a restart) ended both ts-node backends with the error above before and passes after on all four hosts; limits/store-moderately-deep-roundtrips now nests 100 levels. Commands: as for the store() writes entry below. Files: crates/runtime/code-mode-engine/src/cell.rs, crates/runtime/code-mode/src/code_mode/replay.rs.

- fix(code-mode): a cell's `store()` writes reach the host as they are made and are kept however the cell ends (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 Code Mode conformance track: limits policy). The bootstrap kept a cell's writes in a JS map and returned them inside the cell's terminal JSON, so only a cell that completed or threw reported them; a cell that ran out of memory (host.rs sent `stored: HashMap::new()`), exceeded the CPU budget, was terminated through `wait` or was stopped by the host lost every write, although `store` promises a value "for later `exec` calls in the same session" and the cell's tool calls up to that point had happened. `store()` now passes the value's JSON to a new host function, `__nanocodeStore` (STORE in cell.rs), which keeps it in `ExecutionState.written`; the terminal JSON carries only its kind and message, and every end takes the writes from there: Done and Error through `send_terminal`, the out-of-memory and CPU-budget Error events, and a terminated or stopped cell through the new `EmbeddedHost::take_stored`, which `run_cell_actor` calls after the terminate (`CellTerminal::Terminated { stored }`) and merges into the session map and its journal sink (`keep_stored`) exactly as a completed cell's writes. Only a host failure or a replay divergence still drops them. `load` inside the cell still reads the JS map. output/cellbench (`sudo perf stat -e instructions:u`, (N 1200 − N 200) / 1000 per cell, two interleaved rounds that agree to 0.1%, base acf4a0b96 against this lane's four commits together, dev-georgios): empty cell 85.7k → 82.2k, `text('ok')` 101.0k → 97.3k, one tool call 226.2k → 222.3k, 16 sequential calls 1,133.3k → 1,126.4k, the agent cell 949.1k → 945.5k, 16 `store` calls 866.6k → 684.4k (the terminal no longer builds and parses a stored map). Conformance (output/cm-conf, cases renamed for what they now check): limits/oom-keeps-this-cells-store-writes and limits/cpu-exhausted-keeps-store-writes (all four hosts, with a configured cap or budget), limits/terminate-keeps-store-writes (native-host, native-cli), async/terminate-keeps-stores and output/store-terminated-kept (all hosts) read `undefined` in the next cell before and the stored value after. Commands: `cargo check --offline --locked --lib` and `cargo clippy --offline --locked --no-deps --lib -- -D warnings` for nanocode-code-mode-engine, nanocode-code-mode and nanocode, natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`. Files: crates/runtime/code-mode-engine/src/{bootstrap.js,code-values.mjs,cell.rs,host.rs}, crates/runtime/code-mode/src/code_mode/mod.rs.

- fix(code-mode): a nested tool whose handler panics fails that call with `aborted` and its cell goes on under LocalCells too, as in nanocode exec (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 Code Mode conformance track: CLI cell layer). `ToolRegistry::execute_nested` catches a panicking dispatch (`catch_unwind`; `panicked_tool_output` records the message on the tool span and answers `ToolOutput::error("aborted")`), but LocalTools has no catch, so under LocalCells the panic unwound through the cell's task: the cell died, the exec returned `Script failed` with `local code-mode cell ended before a result`, and the rest of the script never ran. `execute_nested_call` now runs each dispatched call (`Nested::Run`, nested or host) under `catch_unwind` and answers a panic with `embedded::tool_panicked()`, a new public helper beside `tool_not_available` that the registry's `panicked_tool_output` now returns too, so both layers answer from one definition; recovery (`recover_nested`) stays uncaught, as in the registry. Conformance with output/cm-conf and its native-toolhost engine (previous entry): new case tools/panicking-tool-fails-the-call (a `{"panic": m}` mock, new in the native runner; the ts runners throw m, so the case runs on native-host and native-toolhost) fails on native-host for both backends before and passes after, and passes on native-toolhost before and after; the whole suite after: native-host 1,194/1,194, native-toolhost 1,194/1,194, layers.ts 1,428 same, 0 differ. Commands: `cd output/cm-conf/native && cargo build --release --bin run`, `./target/release/run --backend both --engine cells --out results/native-host.jsonl`, the same with `--engine tool-host --out results/native-toolhost.jsonl`, `node output/cm-conf/layers.ts --a results/native-host.jsonl --b results/native-toolhost.jsonl`. Gates: `cargo check --locked --lib` and `cargo clippy --no-deps -- -D warnings` for nanocode-code-mode and nanocode-tool-host natively and for wasm32-unknown-unknown; rustfmt leaves the change as it is. Files: crates/runtime/code-mode/src/code_mode/mod.rs, crates/runtime/code-mode/src/embedded/mod.rs, crates/runtime/tool-host/src/runtime/execution.rs.

- fix(tool-host): a nested call to a host tool named `exec` or `wait` answers TOOL_NOT_AVAILABLE in nanocode exec, as it does under LocalCells (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 Code Mode conformance track: CLI cell layer). The registry leaves such tools out of the nested catalog (`Catalog::nested` filters `host_owned_name`, so ALL_TOOLS never lists them), but `execute_nested_inner` still found them in `by_name` and ran them, so a cell calling `tools.exec({})` in the CLI dispatched the host tool, while LocalCells (nanocode-ts, LocalTools, crates/runtime/code-mode/src/code_mode/local.rs) drops host-owned names from its tool list and answers TOOL_NOT_AVAILABLE; `recover_nested` likewise recovered such a call through the host tool instead of reporting its outcome unknown. Local dispatch and recovery now refuse host-owned names first, after hand routing, so a call addressed to another hand is still forwarded as LocalTools forwards it. Found by comparing the two layers: output/cm-conf/native (git-ignored) gains a second engine, `--engine tool-host` (host native-toolhost in result lines, matrix.ts and RUNNERS.md): a nanocode-tool-host `ToolRuntime::new_with_tools` built from `Tools::builder().without_defaults()` with CodeModeOnly exposure, the mocks as its builtin FunctionTools, `cell_journals` over the runner's generation-fenced in-memory sink and `cell_yield` from the case config, driven by `execute_code_owned_with_updates`, `wait_for_code_with_updates`, `recover_code` and `ToolRuntimeControl::cancel_turn`/`begin_turn` as crates/backends/claude/src/claude_tools.rs drives it, with crash and restart through those journals (a new ToolRuntime over the same sink; it adopts on its first exec, wait or recover, as `nanocode exec --continue` does); every case that runs on native-host also runs there, and output/cm-conf/layers.ts compares the two engines' result files case by case (pass, steps with wall time masked, tool calls with clock and random values masked, stored values, crash count). Before, of 1,426 case × backend results (1,192 run, the rest restricted to other hosts) the engines differed only in tools/host-owned-names-not-nested, which native-toolhost failed for both backends (`exec resolved`, `wait resolved`, two mock calls; native-toolhost 1,190/1,192) and native-host passed; after, it passes on both engines and the two engines' 1,428 results (with the case of the next entry) are identical, 1,194/1,194 each. Commands: `cd output/cm-conf/native && cargo build --release --bin run`, `./target/release/run --backend both --engine cells --out results/native-host.jsonl`, the same with `--engine tool-host --out results/native-toolhost.jsonl`, `node output/cm-conf/layers.ts --a results/native-host.jsonl --b results/native-toolhost.jsonl`. Gates: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-tool-host` and `cargo clippy --no-deps -p nanocode-tool-host -- -D warnings` natively and for wasm32-unknown-unknown; rustfmt leaves the change as it is. Files: crates/runtime/tool-host/src/runtime/registry.rs.

- fix(code-mode): a `wait` on a cell whose hand was lost answers the hand's unknown outcome instead of the fallback's `exec cell N not found` (2026-11-14, Georgios: repair the durable-cloudflare crash harnesses). `CodeModeExecutors::wait_routed` asks each place of `wait_route` in turn (the hands that hold the session's running cells, the selected executor, then the fallback) and returned the last place's answer. Since nanocode-ts installs its `LocalCells` as the fallback `local` of every hands session (`set_fallback`, 2026-10-28), a wait whose hand died in the middle of it (`… the dispatched operation has an unknown outcome and was not retried`) or whose hand came back as a new runtime (`NO_CELLS`, `… restarted or reconnected since the cell started, so the cell's outcome is unknown`) went on to `local`, which never ran the cell, and the model was told `exec cell N not found`: a known cell with an unknown outcome read as a cell that never existed. An error from a hand that the wait reached is now the answer unless a later place holds the cell, and the first missing-cell answer is kept over later ones. Found by durable-cloudflare `scripts/measure-hand-faults.mjs` (`reconnect` and `duplicate`), whose checks failed on nanocode-ts dddd1fb in 3 of 3 runs (`exec cell 11 not found` for the wait in flight and for the wait after the hand reattached, `exec cell 2 not found` for the displaced hand's cell); with this change packed into nanocode-ts dddd1fb's module the same checks pass in 3 of 3 runs, answering `runner disconnected; the dispatched operation has an unknown outcome and was not retried`, then `this hand has no cells for the session: it restarted or reconnected since the cell started, so the cell's outcome is unknown`, and for the displaced hand `another hand attached under this name; the dispatched operation has an unknown outcome and was not retried`. Checked: `cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-code-mode --lib` reports nothing in the changed file.
- fix(turnlog): a durable admission whose row does not commit is taken back out of the writer (2026-11-14, same harness). `OneLog::admit` pushes the `Admitted` record and the turn's `queued` event, which `Lease::push` applies to the fold and buffers, then commits; when the commit failed it returned the error (durable-cloudflare answers 503 `session operation failed`) and left both in the fold and the buffer. The pump then ran the refused turn from the fold, and the next commit that landed would have written its admission. `Lease::unadmit` removes both records from the buffer and the turn and its event from the fold (`Fold::unadmit`), and `admit` calls it before it returns the error. A buffered admission (`submit_buffered`) is unchanged: it was never acknowledged on its own. durable-cloudflare `scripts/measure-faults.mjs faults` (`admission`: every `INSERT INTO nanocode_log` refused while one turn is submitted, then resubmitted) counted 2 model calls for that turn on nanocode-ts dddd1fb in 6 of 6 provider runs and 1 in 6 of 6 with this change, and the whole harness passed 1,340 of 1,340 checks in 3 of 3 runs. Checked: `cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-agent --lib` reports nothing in the changed files, and SIM_RESULT.
- feat(python): Cython extensions run on the C API, and msgpack's C module (`msgpack._cmsgpack`, msgpack 1.2.4, Cython 3.3.0 output) is compiled into python3: `import msgpack` uses it and passes msgpack's own test suite, 154 passed and 7 skipped of 161, in python.wasm and natively (2026-11-14, Georgios: run the top compiled Python packages in plain wasm32 with a C API layer written in Rust, no Pyodide). Every extension is compiled with `-DCYTHON_LIMITED_API=1`, so Cython's generated C keeps to functions and stays off CPython's thread state, frame and type internals. New in crates/core/python-capi: c/spec.c, heap types from specs (PyType_FromMetaclass, FromModuleAndSpec, FromSpecWithBases, FromSpec, placing each slot by CPython's own Objects/typeslots.inc offset table, the `__weaklistoffset__`, `__dictoffset__` and `__vectorcalloffset__` members, ht_module), PyType_GetSlot/GetModule/GetModuleState/GetModuleByDef, Py_Version, PyOS_(v)snprintf and PyErr_WarnFormat; c/objects.c, Py_CompileStringExFlags and PyEval_EvalCode over builtins compile and eval, PyCapsule_Import, PyVectorcall_Call through tp_vectorcall_offset, and a datetime C API (PyDateTime_CAPI) built over the datetime module, published as `datetime.datetime_CAPI`; src/buffer.rs, the buffer protocol of C types: a type with bf_getbuffer gets an as_buffer slot whose PyBuffer holds the Py_buffer the type filled and calls bf_releasebuffer when the last share goes, and PyObject_GetBuffer/PyBuffer_Release call a C type's own procs directly (so memoryview(Packer) and Packer.getbuffer() share the packer's memory). Crossing objects: bytearray crosses as CPython's PyByteArrayObject (size, alloc, ob_bytes, ob_start, refreshed on each crossing) since Cython reads Py_SIZE; datetime, date, time and timedelta cross in CPython's PyDateTime_* layouts (data bytes, hastzinfo, fold, a borrowed tzinfo) once the datetime C API was imported, since Cython's datetime helpers read those fields with macros. Types: a C type with Py_TPFLAGS_BASETYPE is subclassable from Python; the type object of a Python subclass of a C type copies its C base's type object (size, alloc, new, dealloc, free, buffer and number methods) under its own header, name, base and flags, `__new__` passes the class it was called with (so C allocates the subclass's size and the instance comes back as the subclass), a C type based on PyType_Type maps to `type`, `__get__` comes from tp_descr_get, members named like the special offsets are not exposed, attributes go into the class's namespace with update_slot so dunders installed after creation take effect, and tp_bases and tp_dict point at a tuple proxy and the class's real namespace dict. `type.__dictoffset__` is a property. Modules: Py_mod_create, PyModule_GetDef/GetName/NewObject. PyTraceBack_Here pushes a traceback entry for the current Python frame onto the pending exception, as Cython's __Pyx_AddTraceback expects before __Pyx_GetException (a C-raised OverflowError caught inside the packer had no traceback, and Cython decrefed it). About 65 more functions in api.rs (attribute lookups, binary and in-place numbers, PyUnicode_Format, PyFloat_Pack/Unpack 4 and 8, exception info get and set, capsules, PyCMethod_New and PyCFunction_* through a map from function object to definition, PyImport_*, PyMemoryView_*, GC no-ops) and libc's strcmp, strncmp, strchr, strrchr, strstr, abs, labs, llabs and arpa/inet.h. rustpython-vm's `update_slot` and `AsBufferFunc` are public. Known limits: a metaclass passed to PyType_FromMetaclass is ignored; capsule destructors are not called; one interpreter per thread; a Python subclass of a C type keeps its dict on the Rust side. Checked on dev-georgios: msgpack's test/ (pytest replaced by a small runner, ~/rpw/hill/mp, tracemalloc's two leak tests skipped as RustPython has no _tracemalloc) 154 passed, 7 skipped, natively and in python.wasm (1.3 s); regex 101/101 and markupsafe's checks still pass. Benchmark (5,000 records of six fields, 393,509 bytes packed, best of 5 after a warm-up, ms, python.wasm then Pyodide 314.0.7 with its msgpack 1.1.2 wheel): C pack 30.4 and 33.6 vs 6.5, C unpack 44.6 and 35.0 vs 8.8; msgpack's pure-Python fallback on python.wasm 256 to 314 pack, 399 to 466 unpack. nanocode-ts bench/python/score.ts: compiled modules 2/274 to 3/274, packages 2/18 to 3/18, C API symbols 289/538 to 354/538, external crates 5, limits 4/4; python.wasm 28,211,778 to 28,410,545 bytes (+198,767). No interpreter path outside the C API changed. Commands: `cargo clippy --offline -p nanocode-python-capi -p nanocode-python --no-deps -- -D warnings` natively and for wasm32-unknown-unknown, `cargo build -p nanocode-python-cli`, `node scripts/check-dependency-boundaries.mjs`. Files: crates/core/python-capi/{build.rs,c/{objects.c,spec.c,typeslots.inc},include/libc/{stdlib.h,arpa/inet.h},ext/msgpack._cmsgpack/*,src/*}, crates/patches/rustpython-vm/src/types/slot.rs.
- deps(memchr): nanocode's own memchr (crates/core/memchr) gives the 17 crates that called memchr the API they call, over vector kernels in `nanocode_sys::memchr`, and memchr 2.8.3 leaves the registry (2026-11-14, agent 33). It takes the crates.io name at 2.8.3 through `[patch.crates-io]`, as itoa and once_cell do, in the root workspace and in psh's standalone one; the `alloc` feature that psh-pattern and six rustpython manifests asked for is no longer named, since the crate declares none. `cargo metadata --offline` still resolves 137 packages; third-party ones go from 15 to 14. The API is what the compiler found the callers use: `memchr`, `memchr2`, `memchr3`, `memrchr`, `memrchr2`, `memrchr3`, their `_iter` forms (double-ended; `memrchr*_iter` is `Rev`, and a one-byte iterator's `count` counts by vector, as memchr's does) and `memmem::{find, rfind, find_iter, rfind_iter, Finder::{new, find, find_iter, needle, as_ref, into_owned}, FindIter, FindRevIter}`. All of its unsafe is in nanocode-sys: one generic search per operation over a `Vector` trait (forward and reverse search for one to three bytes, unrolled by 4 vectors for one byte and 2 for two or three as memchr's loops are; a count; a scan for two bytes at two offsets), instantiated for AVX2 (detected at runtime, with popcnt for the count), SSE2, NEON and a u64 SWAR word for every other target (wasm32). Haystacks shorter than a vector take two overlapping u64 words (a byte loop below 8 bytes), which is 1.4 to 3 times faster than memchr's byte loop at 7 to 15 bytes. The two-byte scan runs in its own non-inlined kernel and returns each chunk with candidates to safe code that verifies them: verifying inside the vector loop through a closure made LLVM spill the loop's registers, 1.3 to 1.5 times slower on every long search. memmem picks the needle's rarest byte, and the rarest byte that differs from it, by a rank table measured over the repository's .rs, .py and .md files with each kind weighted equally (output/memchr-ranks/ranks.py at 18b2bef09), scans for both at their offsets, compares each candidate word by word, and falls back to Two-Way (std's `TwoWaySearcher` factorization and shifts, both directions, with the same scan between windows) once failed candidates have compared more bytes than the search has passed, so every search stays linear. Haystacks under 64 bytes take Rabin-Karp in `memmem::find` and `rfind`, the cutoff memchr 2.8.3's own one-shot functions use. Equality (output/memchr-harness, seeded): every function against crates.io memchr 2.8.3 over haystacks of 0 to 256 bytes (one round in 16 up to 4,096) at all 64 alignments, alphabets of 1 to 256 bytes with NUL and 0xff mixed in, needles of 0 to 33 bytes or up to the haystack's length cut from it, mutated or random, and interleaved `next`/`next_back`: 193.0M cases with AVX2 (48.3M of them after the last dispatch change), 6.0M with SSE2 only (`qemu-x86_64 -cpu Nehalem`), 6.0M with NEON (`qemu-aarch64`) and 6.0M with SWAR (wasm32-wasip1 under node), 0 differences; the SWAR run first found a count that divided SWAR's one set bit per lane by its 8 lane bits. Throughput (output/memchr-harness bench, AMD EPYC 9554 Hand pinned to one core at load 4 to 6, own against memchr, three interleaved rounds each the best of 3, three runs): Claude SSE lines with `memchr2` and the field's `memchr(b':')` 0.94 to 0.95, Codex lines with `memchr(b'\n')` 0.90 to 0.96, the Claude client's one-shot `memmem::find` of a key in 200-byte windows 1.03 to 1.05, rg line counting 0.87 to 0.94 and line iteration 0.85 to 0.95 over 32 MB of source, `memchr`, `memrchr` and `memchr3` of an absent byte over 32 MB 0.94 to 1.04, psh `Finder::find_iter` over 32 MB for six of seven literals 0.92 to 1.17, RustPython `str.find` on short strings 0.87 to 0.92, `str.rfind` 0.57 to 0.59, `str.count` 1.06 to 1.08, long `find` 0.88 to 0.97 and long `rfind` 0.05 (memchr's reverse search has no prefilter). Past 10%: psh's `" the "` at 1.32 and `"fn main"` at 1.11 to 1.17, needles whose rarest pair still matches every 370 and 1,000 bytes of Rust source, where each chunk with candidates costs a return from the kernel and a re-entry (about 5 ns) that memchr's inline verification does not pay; and RustPython's NUL check over 20,000 strings of 5 to 124 bytes, 0.96 to 1.21 across runs of a separate benchmark (output/memchr-harness/src/bin/nul.rs), within the Hand's noise.
- A systemd user unit that `nanocode_home::service` writes sets `OOMPolicy=continue` (2026-11-14). systemd's default for a service is `stop`: when the kernel's OOM killer kills any process in the unit's cgroup, systemd stops the whole unit. A Hand runs its commands in its own cgroup, so one build that ran the machine out of memory stopped the Hand and every other command it was running, and the Hand came back as a new runtime whose brain reported all their outcomes as unknown. On one 62 GB machine running a Hand for several agents at once, the Hand unit's journal showed eight such stops between 00:53 and 05:44 UTC, each `A process of this unit has been killed by the OOM killer` then `Failed with result 'oom-kill'`, with unit memory peaks of 17 to 44 GB, and each matched a burst of 10 to 20 calls the brain read as unknown. With `continue` the killed process ends alone and its call fails with its own exit status. If the OOM killer picks the service's main process, `Restart=on-failure` starts it again as before. An installed unit only gets the line when it is written again (`UserService::install`); `systemctl --user daemon-reload` applies it to the running service without a restart (checked on that machine: `systemctl --user show -p OOMPolicy` read `continue` with the same main PID). `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-home`, natively and for wasm32-unknown-unknown, passed.
- nanocode-http refuses a `content-length` that is not all decimal digits and a chunk-size line with anything but whitespace and a chunk extension after its hex digits; `nanocode-sim --scenario http_server` sends both and found them (2026-11-14). `content_length` (crates/core/http/src/wire.rs) parsed each comma-separated part with `u64::from_str`, which accepts a leading `+`, so `content-length: +5` framed a five-byte body where RFC 9112 allows only `1*DIGIT`; the chunk-size parser read the leading hex digits and ignored the rest of the line, so `5x` read as a five-byte chunk. Both are request-smuggling shapes: a front end that refuses or reads them differently from nanocode's server disagrees with it about where a message ends, and the egress proxy is such a server. The new `wire::decimal` takes only ASCII digits (after trimming), and the content-length readers use it (`content_length`, the server's `declared_length` for streamed replies, and the client's `Payload::new`); a chunk-size line passes only when its hex digits are followed by nothing, or by spaces and tabs and then `;` (`chunk-ext`). The scenario's malformed request is now one of three kinds: the head without a colon it sent before, `POST /broken` with `content-length: +5` (the server must fail on the head and call no handler), and a chunked `POST /broken` whose first chunk-size line is `5x` (the handler is called and reads its whole body, which must fail, and nothing after it is handled; its response is not checked). On the server before this change seeds 0..20,000 fail 701 times, 367 of them `SignedLength` ("the server handled 1 requests where the script allows 0 to 0": the head was accepted and the handler called) and 334 `ChunkJunk` ("the handler read a body of 5 bytes behind a malformed chunk size"), and none of another kind. The gate on the hosted Hand: `nanocode-sim --tidy` clean; `cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-http -p nanocode-sim` and `cargo check --locked --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p nanocode-http` report nothing in either crate; `cargo check --locked --workspace --all-targets` passes; with this change seeds 0..50,000 of `--scenario http_server` pass and 50,000..55,000 with `--twice`, the scenario's two mutations are caught by 210 and 258 seeds of 0..400, and seeds 7760000000000..+3,000 of `--scenario runtime` with `--store kv`, `--store memory`, `--store kv --twice` and `--store kv --wire http` pass, 12,000 of 12,000. The full runtime gate that the 42f3ae413 entry below ran short also ran, on 1490d4c4b (which contains it): seeds 7750000000000..+3,000 of `--store memory`, `--store kv --twice` and `--store kv` pass, 9,000 of 9,000.
- deps(trace): nanocode-trace's Instrumented no longer uses pin-project-lite; nanocode-sys's Scoped does the one pin projection (2026-11-14). What: nanocode-sys gains `Scope` (a value that can be entered, giving a guard) and `Scoped<T, S: Scope>`, a future that holds `Option<T>` pinned and its scope unpinned, enters the scope around every poll of T and around dropping T, and is Unpin exactly when T is; its two `unsafe` lines (`get_unchecked_mut` and `Pin::new_unchecked` on the inner future, which is never moved and is dropped in place) live in the one crate allowed unsafe code. nanocode-trace implements Scope for Span and makes `Instrumented<T>` an alias of `Scoped<T, Span>`; `Instrument::instrument` and `in_current_span` are unchanged. Why: TIGER_STYLE's dependency order and pin-project-lite's macro, which expands unsafe code into a crate that forbids it. Equal: output/trace-instrument (its own workspace, pin-project-lite =0.2.17's Instrumented as it was, beside Scoped over a scope that logs every enter and exit) compares 2,000,000 seeded cases (inner futures that yield 0 to 4 times, polled 0 to 6 times so that some are dropped before they finish, wrapped once or twice): 25,142,383 trace lines (enter, poll, exit, drop and ready, in order), 0 differing. Cost: none measured, wrapping and driving a future 0.27 ns either way (median of 7 interleaved runs of 2,000,000, release); no allocation, unlike boxing the inner future. Different: `Instrumented::span()` and `span_mut()` become `Scoped::scope()` and `scope_mut()`, its Debug prints `Scoped { inner, scope }`, and the type is named Scoped in errors; nothing in the workspace, tempoxyz/pyramid or tempoxyz/pyramid-core names Instrumented or calls those methods (`.instrument(...)` call sites, 80 of them, are unchanged). Checks: cargo check --locked --workspace --all-targets passes; wasm32-unknown-unknown cargo check --lib passes for nanocode-sys, nanocode-trace and nanocode-sync; clippy adds no warning in the changed files; rustfmt --check is clean on them. Packages: unchanged, 137 (15 third-party): pin-project-lite stays in the graph for tokio, which depends on it unconditionally. Downstream: none.
- nanocode-sim exercises the event clause of the turn log archive cut: `--event-bytes N` pads every scripted event with N deterministic letters, so the events of one snapshot exceed the 32 KiB window, and the new invariant `event_kept` checks that every event a committed turn log row held is still in `TurnLog::history` after each reopen and in the durable log at the end (2026-11-14, Georgios: close the gap the coldreads change left, where dropping the event clause passed 300 of 300 seeds). Why: the existing archive check in `SimHost::append_compacting` (each archive is a suffix of the snapshot it replaces with the same `Event` records) only fires when a snapshot's events start before the window floor, and the scripted events were a few dozen bytes. The client-seen oracle cannot serve as the reference for `event_kept`, since a client sees an event before the turn log commits it (temporary seqs): `Oracle::committed` records the events of each committed row when the tick commits instead. What changed: (1) `--event-bytes N` (`turns::emit`). (2) `event_kept`, checked in `Sim::start` for every scope it loads (`judge_history`) and in `judge_observed`. (3) Mutation `archive_drops_events`: `SimHost` replaces each archive the writer hands it with the window-only cut (the coldreads source mutation `while start > floor`), packed as an `a` row of raw deflate plus base64 and split at the row limit, after the archive check, so only `event_kept` can catch it. (4) `--reopen-row-limit M` opens every even incarnation with row limit M, so a snapshot written at one limit is archived at another. That is the only path that reaches the `rows.len() <= self.parts` guard of `Previous::archive`, and the writer then keeps the superseded snapshot, so the at-most-one-`s`-row invariant is off in that mode (`TurnLogPolicy::single_snapshot`). Results (sweep.sh, 4 jobs, `--scenario turns --policy turnlog --snapshot-rows 4 --state-bytes 40000`, seeds 0..2000): `archive_drops_events` fails 0 seeds without `--event-bytes`, 452 with 16384, 841 with 32768 and 1,781 with 32768 `--row-limit 16384`. Source mutations of crates/core/turnlog/src/writer.rs (each built and swept, then reverted): the coldreads `events_short` (`while start > floor`) fails 0 without the flag and 841 with `--event-bytes 32768` (archive check). `open_events_zero` (`TurnLog::open` passes 0 events to `Previous::of`) fails 0 and 704. `open_parts_one` (open counts 1 part) fails 0 with no row limit and 1,692 with `--row-limit 16384`. `dropped_ignored` (empty `dropped` range) fails 0 and 1,898 with `--row-limit 16384`. `parts_unchecked` (drop `rows.len() <= self.parts`) fails 0 with a fixed row limit and 1,313 with `--row-limit 65536 --reopen-row-limit 8192`. `bytes_unchecked` (drop `bytes < self.bytes`) fails 0 in every mode: an archive is a strict suffix of its snapshot and never packs larger here, so this guard is not reached. `snapshot_kept` fails 1,567 with `--event-bytes 32768`. Clean sweeps pass with 0 panics: 0..3000 `--twice --event-bytes 32768`, and seeds 0..2000 `--twice` with `--event-bytes` 16384 and 65536, `--event-bytes 32768 --row-limit 16384`, `--event-bytes 32768 --row-limit 65536 --reopen-row-limit 8192`, `--retain 0 --snapshot-rows 2 --event-bytes 32768`, `--calm --snapshot-rows 2 --event-bytes 32768`, plus the regressions `--twice`, `--twice --snapshot-rows 4 --state-bytes 131072`, `--twice --snapshot-rows 3 --row-limit 1024`, `--twice --event-bytes 32768` without the snapshot flags, and the reference policy with and without `--event-bytes 32768`. `nanocode-sim --tidy` is clean, `cargo +1.97.1 clippy -p nanocode-sim --no-deps -- -D warnings -A clippy::useless_conversion` passes, and rustfmt is clean on turnlog.rs and turns.rs. Not done: after a row limit shrinks across a reopen, the snapshot superseded at that point stays fat permanently, because the writer does not try to archive it again. Files: bin/nanocode-sim/src/{main,turnlog,turns}.rs.
- SLA.md records a rerun of live Codex on nanocode master 00c215b02 against Codex CLI 0.166.0, 20 sessions x 3 turns on gpt-6-luna and gpt-6.1-sol (2026-11-14). nanocode wins every p50 (990 against 1,814 ms on luna turn 1) and turn 1 p99, and loses p99 on turns 2 and 3 by 0.1 to 3.0 s. Traces put nanocode's own share of a later turn at 0.9 to 1.6 ms and match Codex's requests, and the slow sessions are slow on every turn under any request shape, so the p99 gap is backend-side. The levers left are a priority service tier, which costs more usage, and hedged duplicate requests, which would replay dispatched work. Neither is taken. Commands: nanocode-ts bench/sla/run.ts --live --lanes=live-nc-codex@master,live-codex --samples=20 --turns=3 on dev-georgios.

- fix(sim): nanocode-sim builds again: the code-mode cells it drives give their CellJournalHeader `started_at_ms: None` (2026-11-14). 412d181b2 (performance.now() continues across a restart) added `started_at_ms: Option<u64>` to nanocode-code-mode's CellJournalHeader, and bin/nanocode-sim/src/cells.rs, which builds headers for the cells its turns scenario drives, did not set it, so `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` failed on master (E0063 in cells.rs) from that commit on. None is what a header written before 412d181b2 decodes to (`#[serde(default)]`), so the simulated cells replay as such journals do, and it reads no wall clock, which the simulator's determinism rules forbid. Checks: cargo check --locked -p nanocode-sim --all-targets passes; nanocode-sim release --tidy is clean; sweep.sh 0 300 with 2 workers passes 300 of 300 with 0 panics for --scenario turns (which runs the cells) and --scenario runtime --store kv. Packages unchanged. Downstream: none.
- refactor: every `tokio::sync` site moves to nanocode-sync's own primitives (2026-11-14, tokio replacement step 2 of plan-22). 84 files swap `tokio::sync::{mpsc, oneshot, watch, broadcast, Notify, Semaphore, OnceCell}` (and `futures::Notified`) for `nanocode_sync::…`; inside nanocode-sync, `Signal`, `Actor`, `Mailbox`, `unbounded`, `wakes` and `lanes` use `crate::`. Three call-site changes beyond the import: `watch::Sender` gains `Default` as tokio's has; nanocode-sync gains `SetOnce` (`const_new`, `set`, `get`, `wait`, `SetOnceError`) for `FIRST_FRAME`, which master moved to tokio's `SetOnce` meanwhile: a `OnceLock` for the value and a lazily created `Notify` for waiters, with a SeqCst fence on each side so a `set` racing a `wait` cannot both miss; and a step 0 leftover `Instant` import in the sandbox's audit module goes. tokio's `sync` feature leaves every manifest. tokio leaves the manifests of nanocode-agent-core, nanocode-mcp, nanocode-types, nanocode-agent, nanocode-agent-config, nanocode-code-mode, nanocode-subagents, nanocode-store-jsonl, nanocode-observability and nanocode-backend-claude-tools. nanocode-backend-claude(-client), nanocode-backend-codex(-client) and nanocode-durability move their tokio to the native target section, since nothing on wasm32 used it. `cargo tree --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -e normal -i tokio --workspace` now lists only nanocode-sim (native-only) and nanocode-platform under RustPython's host-side proc-macro build, so tokio is out of every wasm32 library graph. Checks: `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo check --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` for platform, sync, agent-core, durability, backend-claude, backend-codex(-client), code-mode, subagents, http, mcp-http, websocket, types, mcp and agent-config are clean; `nanocode-sim --tidy` clean; release nanocode-sim seeds 1..150: `--scenario runtime --twice` 149/149 identical in 24 s, with the same crash, epoch and turn counts as on master; `--wire http` 149/149 in 23 s; `--store kv` 149/149 in 16 s; `--scenario websocket` 149/149. Wake order now follows registration (watch, Notify) and the runtime digests are unchanged across these seeds. Packages: `cargo metadata` unchanged (146); tokio itself leaves in steps 5 to 9. Files: 84 call sites and 30 manifests, crates/core/sync/src/{watch.rs,set_once.rs,lib.rs}.

- fix(claude): background Bash tasks take Claude Code 2.1.300's shape: `b` + 8 base-36 ids, an exit line at the end of the output file, and mid-turn notifications merged into the round's system message (2026-11-14, ~/hill/analysis/claude-parity.md L4). Measured in the parity mock (`~/wt/claude-bg-par`, `run3.py bg` and a new `bgx` scenario: a 1 s `timeout` moved to the background, plus a background `exit 3`, both ending during a foreground `sleep 4`). Stock's task id is `ck()`: the type letter (`local_bash:"b"`) then `randomBytes(8)[i] % 36` over `0-9a-z` (`b3978tou9`); nanocode used `<session uuid>-bash-N` (45 chars). Now `task_id()` draws the same from `nanocode_platform::fill_random` (an error is the call's error), retries an id the session already holds, and the cwd marker becomes `nanocode-{session}-{id}-cwd` so it stays unique across sessions. The output directory stays `/tmp/nanocode/<session>/tasks/` rather than stock's `/tmp/claude-<uid>/<cwd with - for />/<session>/tasks/`, which is about 60 chars longer in every start result, notification and Read. Stock's `Yrt` appends `\n[exited with code N]\n` (`unknown` with no code) or `\n[killed]\n` when a task ends, and TaskStop's `HV` appends `\n[killed]\n`; nanocode's files had no such line. Now `Job::close_output` appends the same once the writer has drained, for every task that reached the background (the watch and the exec-reported paths), and a deadline or the 5 GB cap counts as killed; the notification's inlined tail strips that line so `Output:` and "printed nothing" read as before. Files now match stock byte for byte (`bg-out\nbg-err\n\n[exited with code 0]\n`, `\n[killed]\n`, Read `4\t[exited with code 0]`). Mid-turn, stock queues the notification and renders it into the next system message as `J3e` (the `[SYSTEM NOTIFICATION - NOT USER INPUT]` preamble) + `<task-notification>…</task-notification>` + `\n\n` before `<total_tokens>`, one preamble per notification; nanocode steered it in as a second user message (`<system-reminder>` wrapped) followed by its own `<total_tokens>` message. Now direct headless root sessions use `Delivery::Merged`: a notification goes to `Jobs::round`, the agent's new `round_notices` hook drains it into the system message it writes after each tool round (`{notices}{update}<total_tokens>…`), and the turn hold steers whatever is still queued when the model ends its turn as the `<system-reminder>` user message stock sends then. Headless sessions that are not direct (exec cells) keep `Held`, and interactive sessions and subagents are unchanged. nanocode keeps its inlined `Output:` tail after `</task-notification>`, which saves the model a Read. Results with the release build: `bg` makes 8 requests (stock 8) and its last request has 22 messages (stock 22, before 23), 3357 chars of message text (stock 3667, before 3842); `bgx` makes 6 requests (stock 6) with both notifications in message 10, as stock does. `timeout`, `par`, `out`, `maxtok` and `edit` give the same requests as before once ids are normalized. Stock sends `is_error: false` only on Bash results (not on Read or TaskStop); the API reads an absent field the same way, so it stays omitted. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude` native and `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode`, `cargo build --locked --release -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode`.
- fix(release): the Linux container step of scripts/release-cli.sh installs BOLT again on rust:1.97-bullseye, without llvm.sh and without the bullseye-security source (2026-11-14, release lane). Since bullseye reached its end of life, deb.debian.org/debian-security still serves the bullseye-security index but no longer its packages, so any install that needs a security update 404s: `apt-get install -y lsb-release software-properties-common gnupg python3` (what llvm.sh needs) failed on libcap2, systemd, packagekit and python3-pkg-resources, and even `apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ca-certificates` fails on `pool/updates/main/c/ca-certificates/ca-certificates_20250419~deb12u1~deb11u1_all.deb`. The image already has gnupg 2.2.27, python3 3.9.2 (train-cli.py, order-cli.py, trim-cli.py), wget, xz-utils and ca-certificates, and apt.llvm.org still publishes llvm-toolchain-bullseye-21 (bolt-21 and llvm-21 21.1.5). The step now deletes the debian-security line from /etc/apt/sources.list, adds apt.llvm.org's key (`llvm-snapshot.gpg.key` dearmored into /usr/share/keyrings/llvm.gpg) and `deb [signed-by=...] https://apt.llvm.org/bullseye/ llvm-toolchain-bullseye-21 main` by hand, and runs `apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends bolt-21 llvm-21`: 8 packages (bolt-21, libbolt-21-dev, libllvm21, libpfm4, libz3-4, llvm-21, llvm-21-linker-tools, llvm-21-runtime), no 404s, giving llvm-bolt, merge-fdata, libbolt_rt_instr.a and llvm-strip in /usr/lib/llvm-21/bin. llvm-21 is there for build-cli.sh stripping with the llvm-strip beside llvm-bolt. The image stays bullseye so the glibc baseline stays: the published nanocode-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu and nanocode-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu need at most GLIBC_2.30 (`objdump -T <binary> | grep -o 'GLIBC_[0-9.]*' | sort -uV | tail -1`), and so do the new build's nanocode and nanocode-python. Building without the security updates changes nothing that ends up in the binaries: they link only glibc, which the image already carries at 2.31-13+deb11u14. Checked on dev-georgios, amd64 only (no qemu for arm64, whose lines are the same): the container command of release-cli.sh, as written, with `--memory 24g` added, run under `flock ~/dist-build.lock` at 884c2d387 ran through apt and `scripts/build-cli.sh nanocode-cli nanocode` with BOLT 21 (instrumented training, cdsort and the final layout) and printed /src/target/linux-amd64/cli/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/nanocode: 46,141,696 bytes, `nanocode 0.7.0`; nanocode-python 15,975,320 bytes beside it, which runs `print(6*7)` and whose SHA-256 the nanocode binary embeds. The linker script and trim-cli.py that origin added to the Linux lane later were checked in the same image: GNU ld 2.35.2 links a hello-world with `-T scripts/cli-eh-frame.ld` and the lane's flags (`.eh_frame` placed before `.eh_frame_hdr`), and trim-cli.py uses nothing past Python 3.9. release-cli.sh was not run whole (no macOS lanes, no --publish, nothing uploaded). Files: scripts/release-cli.sh.
- feat(sync): nanocode-sync's own `Notify` (`notify_one`, `notify_last`, `notify_waiters`, `notified`, `Notified::enable`), `watch` (`channel`, `Sender::new`, `send`, `send_replace`, `send_modify`, `send_if_modified`, `borrow`, `subscribe`, `closed`, counts; `Receiver::borrow`, `borrow_and_update`, `has_changed`, `mark_changed`, `mark_unchanged`, `changed`, `wait_for`) and `broadcast` (`channel`, `Sender::new`, `send`, `subscribe`, `downgrade`, `closed`; `Receiver::recv`, `try_recv` with `Lagged(n)`, `resubscribe`, `len`) with tokio's names, error types and text (2026-11-14, tokio replacement step 1b of plan-22). Nothing calls them yet; step 2 swaps the imports. `Notify` keeps the `notify_waiters` count, the stored permit and its waiters (FIFO by ticket in an `OrdMap`) in one `Atom`; each waiter has a state byte, and `notify_one` claims a waiter by moving that byte from waiting to notified before removing it, so a waiter dropped at the same moment either cancels first (and is skipped) or sees it was notified and forwards the notification to the next waiter or the permit, as tokio's does. A `Notified` made before `notify_waiters` completes even if it was never polled, as in tokio. `watch` keeps the value and its version together in one `Atom<Versioned<T>>`, so a borrow always sees a matching pair; versions come from a counter stepped by 2, so `mark_changed`'s odd version never equals a real one. A `Ref` holds an `Arc` snapshot instead of a read lock, so holding one while sending cannot deadlock. Two deviations from tokio's signatures, both met by every call site: `send_modify` and `send_if_modified` take `FnMut` (a racing send reapplies the change to the newer value), and `send_replace` needs `T: Clone` to return the old value while a `Ref` still shares it. Receivers wake in registration order, not tokio's random choice among eight `Notify`s (the 2026-11-13 InOrder entry traced simulator nondeterminism to that randomness). `broadcast` keeps its ring (tail, receiver count, closed flag and the slots as a persistent `Vector` of `Arc`'d values) in one `Atom`; receivers wait on a `Notify` that every send and the last sender's drop wake. Its one user, `wakes.rs`, sends a wake per lane, so the copy-on-write send is not hot. `Sender::len` and `is_empty` are left out (no caller). Checks: output/channel-equality's notify, watch and broadcast scripts (create, poll, enable and drop notifieds; send, replace, modify, conditional modify, borrow, mark, `changed` and `wait_for` polled and dropped, subscribe, clone and drop either side, `closed`; send, try_recv, recv polled and dropped, subscribe, resubscribe, drops) give 0 differences over 5 seeds x 300,000 scripts each against tokio::sync 1.52.3, comparing results, error text and which wakers woke. A mutation that keeps the stored permit after a waiter takes it gives 89 differences in 2,000 notify scripts, and one that inverts `has_changed` gives 671 in 2,000 watch scripts. `channel-equality bench2` watch 1 sender to 64 receiver threads, 2,000 sends, median of 7 interleaved rounds: 203.2 vs 189.3 us per send (1.07). `cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-sync` native and wasm32 report nothing in the new files. Files: crates/core/sync/src/{notify.rs,watch.rs,broadcast.rs,lib.rs}.

- perf(sync): nanocode-sync's `Semaphore` keeps its permits, its closed flag and a drainer lock in one atomic word, and its waiters in nanocode-sys's lock-free MPSC queue, so acquiring and releasing touch one word unless someone waits (2026-11-14, tokio replacement plan-22, before step 2 moves bounded channels onto it). The first version kept everything in one copy-on-write `Atom` with an `OrdMap` of waiters, which made every acquire and release allocate: bounded(64) mpsc cost 126 to 298 ns per message on one thread against tokio's 22 to 26. Now `try_acquire` is one compare-and-swap and a release one `fetch_add`; a release that sees queued waiters, an enqueue, a drop and `close` call `drain`, which takes the DRAINING bit (or sets AGAIN for the holder) and so is the queue's one consumer. The drainer keeps the queue's `Consumer` and the head it is filling in an `AtomicBox` it alone takes while it holds the bit. Each waiter node has an atomic word for its assigned permits, GRANTED, CANCELLED and SHUT: the drainer takes permits from the semaphore word and adds them to the head node by compare-and-swap, handing them back if the node was cancelled meanwhile; a dropped acquire sets CANCELLED and returns what it was assigned, or all its permits if it was already granted. That is tokio's partial assignment to the oldest waiter, with the same answers: after `close`, queued acquires fail and their assigned permits come back when they drop. Checks: output/channel-equality, 0 differences over 5 seeds x 300,000 scripts for Semaphore, bounded and unbounded mpsc, oneshot and OnceCell against tokio::sync 1.52.3; stress 10M messages 4P1C and 16P4C bounded(64), no loss or reorder. `channel-equality bench2`, 7 interleaved rounds against tokio at load 13 to 15, median ns per op (ratio ours/tokio): bounded(64) 1P1C across threads 234.0 vs 258.5 (0.91), bounded(64) 4P1C 804.8 vs 661.4 (1.22, p90 1,024.9 vs 1,651.2), `try_acquire` and drop 4.8 vs 8.6 (0.56), 4 threads contending for 2 permits 28.3 vs 35.4 (0.80); bounded(64) on one thread 19 to 43 vs 20 to 29 in the 3-round bench. `cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-sync` native and wasm32 report nothing in semaphore.rs. Files: crates/core/sync/src/semaphore.rs.

- fix(claude): a tool_use cut by max_tokens stays in the history as Claude Code 2.1.300 keeps it, `{"__unparsedToolInput":{"raw":…,"len":…}}`, answered by the InputValidationError tool_result, and the turn goes on as after any tool call, without a continuation message (2026-11-14, ~/hill/analysis/claude-parity.md H1 and L2). nanocode's client replaced such a block, whether its content_block_stop came or not, with assistant text `Incomplete tool input for Bash (toolu_01) was not executed because the output token limit was reached. Issue a fresh complete call if needed.`, and the agent then appended `Output token limit hit. Resume directly …` and counted it as one of the 3 continuations, so a model that was cut twice in text and then once mid-call failed the run where stock went on. Stock builds the unparsed input in `cXt` for every stop reason (`raw` = the first 2048 UTF-16 units, `len` = the whole input's length), runs the tools of any response that has a tool_use, and its next turn resets `maxOutputTokensRecoveryCount` (`guards:{...kt,...qs}`, `qs` spreads `vr`), so only text-only cuts are continued and counted (`wr=3`). Now `BlockAccumulator::finish` no longer takes `truncated`: a ToolUse whose fragments do not parse gets the unparsed input on every stop reason, the path the bad-JSON fix already answers in durable.rs, and an unstopped ToolUse at a max_tokens message_stop is finished the same way, as an unstopped Text already was; the agent's tool branch continues on `ToolUse | MaxTokens` with `output_continuations` reset, so the continuation message goes only after a cut with no tool call. thread.rs's `stored` already treats a max_tokens response that ends in a tool_use as not stored, which now applies. Measured with a private copy of the parity mock (~/wt/claude-maxtok-p3: mock3.py gains maxtok3, two text cuts, a cut tool_use, three more text cuts, then DONE, and maxtok4, a complete Bash call plus one cut mid-input with a non-ASCII character in one response), stock Claude Code 2.1.300 against nanocode-6c44fe5 and a release build of this tree, every request's messages compared exactly (text, tool_use id/name/input, tool_result text and is_error): maxtok 4 of 4 requests identical after (before: the cut call became text and a second continuation followed), maxtok3 7 of 7 and exit 0 after, as stock (before: exit 1 after 4 requests, `output token limit exhausted after 3 continuations`), maxtok4 3 of 3 after (`You sent (first 33 of 33 bytes)` as stock), maxtok5 4 of 4 and exit 1 before and after, as stock. Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude-client -p nanocode-backend-claude` native and `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode`, `cargo build --locked --release -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode`, `NC=… python3 run3.py maxtok,maxtok3,maxtok4,maxtok5 nc-claude`. Files: crates/backends/claude/client/src/lib.rs, crates/backends/claude/src/agent.rs.
- deps(macros): nanocode-tools-macros and RustPython's derive macros parse and generate over proc_macro through nanocode-macro-support, so syn, quote and proc-macro2 leave the workspace (2026-11-14). What: nanocode-macro-support (the crate behind our serde_derive since 2367c144e) gains the item grammar both macro crates need: items (fn, impl, trait, struct, enum, union, mod, use, const, static, type, macro and extern blocks with their impl and trait items), signatures, function arguments and receivers, blocks, patterns (ident, paren, reference, tuple-struct, wild) and an expression tree for literals, paths, groups and unary operators, beside the derive input, generics, paths, types, literals, punctuated lists and quote! it already had. nanocode-tools-macros (#[derive(JsonSchema)] and #[tool]) and rustpython-derive with rustpython-derive-impl (FromArgs, pyclass, pyexception, pymodule, pystruct_sequence, pystruct_sequence_data, py_compile, py_freeze, PyPayload, Traverse) take proc_macro::TokenStream and nanocode-macro-support's types instead of syn's, and RustPython's syn_ext helpers (meta parsing, nested metas, attribute lookup) are written over them. Why: DEPENDENCIES.md's goal of nothing outside the async baseline; these two macro crates were the last users of syn, quote and proc-macro2 once our serde_derive landed. Equal: every macro invocation in the workspace expands to the same tokens. The check instrumented both implementations (a wrapper around each proc-macro entry point that writes the invocation's input and its output's `TokenStream::to_string()` to a file keyed by a hash of the input) and ran `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` on master and on this change with buildcache off: 1,720 invocations each (derive_from_args 274, derive_json_schema 20, py_compile 3, py_freeze 3, pyclass 931, pyexception 158, pymodule 81, pypayload 124, pystruct_sequence 14, pystruct_sequence_data 14, pytraverse 96, tool 2). After pairing the 112 nested invocations whose input is an outer macro's output (their inputs differ only in that output's spacing), 1,671 outputs carry the same tokens (1,408 byte-identical; in the rest syn and quote re-emit `||`, `?;`, `*x` and `std::io` as `| |`, `? ;`, `* x` and `std :: io`, where proc_macro keeps the source's spacing), 46 pyclass outputs register the same getset blocks in another order and 3 py_freeze outputs hold the same frozen modules in another order (equal lengths: 9,374,141, 217,531 and 81,574 bytes), because both implementations collect those in a std HashMap with a random hasher (GetSetNursery's map, and py_freeze's read_dir into a HashMap), so the old macros were not deterministic there either. No other difference. Different: the spans and wording of errors for malformed macro input come from nanocode-macro-support's parser instead of syn's. Checks: cargo check --locked --workspace --all-targets passes; cargo clippy on nanocode-macro-support, nanocode-tools-macros, nanocode-tools and nanocode-python adds no warning in a changed file; rustfmt --check finds no new difference in a changed file; rustfmt --check is clean on every changed file (the vendored rustpython-derive and rustpython-derive-impl files it touches are formatted whole, which also reformats 78 lines of upstream code there); a Python smoke (output/macros-equality/smoke.py: builtins, f-strings, json, re, collections, itertools, functools.lru_cache, datetime, hashlib sha256 and md5, base64, struct, textwrap, dataclasses, decimal, fractions, statistics, seeded random, heapq, bisect, unicodedata, enum, generators, exceptions, zlib, csv, difflib, html, urllib.parse, big integers and floats) run by this change's nanocode-python (the program psh's python3 runs, started as python3; a debug build, so with a 4 GB stack for its larger frames) prints the same 41 lines and digest as `nanocode psh-shell -c 'python3 smoke.py'` from a master release build. Packages: `cargo metadata --locked` 140 to 137 (third-party 18 to 15: syn, quote and proc-macro2; unicode-ident stays for rustpython-ruff_python_parser); `cargo tree -p nanocode-cli --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -e normal,build` 15 to 11 third-party (unicode-ident leaves that graph too).
- The local OTLP exporters' threads (nanocode-otlp-traces, nanocode-otlp-metrics, OpenTelemetry.Metrics.PeriodicReader) start after the TUI's first frame instead of during install (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 CLI performance track: the 1.3 ms first frame, earlydraw lane). `install` spawned all three on the main thread before the async runtime existed, and they ran beside it while it drew. Their channels need no reader yet (spans queue in the unbounded trace channel up to OTEL_BSP_MAX_QUEUE_SIZE, metrics are only exported by the reader thread or at shutdown), so install now records each spawn as a closure in `ExporterThreads` (an Arc'd `nanocode_sync::Slot`, taken once, lock-free); run_with starts them at once for every command but the TUI and resumed sessions, which start them from the task that waits for `app::FIRST_FRAME`, and `ObservabilityGuard::shutdown` starts any not yet started before it flushes, so an early exit still writes its spans. A failed spawn reports through the exporter's existing write-failure message instead of failing install. Measured as in the previous entries (60 and 61 runs): threads created before the first frame 5 to 2, other-thread samples 5 to 3, main-thread samples 43 to 42, first frame 2,573 to 2,292 us; perf stat to exit (9 each), which still includes the threads: user 9.06M both, kernel 11.78M and 12.11M, faults 855 and 867 (noise at this load).
