- fix(tls): a CPU without what graviola needs is a typed error instead of a panic (2026-11-14, TLS plan step 8). graviola asserts its CPU features on every public call, so on Intel before Broadwell, AMD before Zen, Atom-class chips, QEMU's default CPU or Rosetta 2 before macOS 15, every TLS connection and every egress certificate panicked. `nanocode_tls::cpu::check()` (45 lines) asks std's safe `is_x86_feature_detected!` and `is_aarch64_feature_detected!` for graviola's list (aes, pclmulqdq, bmi1, bmi2, adx, avx and avx2 on x86_64; neon, aes, pmull and sha2 on aarch64; bmi2 is the one its README adds to the asserts) and returns `io::ErrorKind::Unsupported` naming the missing ones. It runs first in `native_client_config`'s load, in the sandbox's `Tls::with_roots` (so `Tls::new` too), `Tls::from_ca` (as a `BadCa` of "this CPU") and `Tls::signed_by`, in store-sql's TLS config and in the MPP proxy's `CertificateAuthority::generate`. std caches the detection, so a check costs a few loads. Checked: output/tls-live's `cpu` binary (`native_client_config` then `egress::Tls::new`), built for x86_64-unknown-linux-musl because QEMU user mode on the Hand crashes reading /proc/self/maps for glibc's thread setup, run under `qemu-x86_64 -cpu`: before, Haswell panics with "graviola requires adx CPU support" and Westmere with "graviola requires bmi1 CPU support"; after, Haswell gives `Unsupported this CPU lacks adx, which nanocode's TLS cryptography needs` and Westmere `lacks bmi1, bmi2, adx, avx, avx2`, while `-cpu max`, Broadwell and the Hand's own CPU load both configs as before.
- A Codex turn that goes on after a host restart sends its whole input once and gets a new turn ID; both were looked at as possible defects of the resume path and neither is changed (2026-11-14). The input: over the Responses WebSocket a session continues with `previous_response_id` and the new items only, and with `store: false` (the default, see the entry on it) the response that ID names lives in the connection that produced it. A restarted host has a new connection, so the first request after the restart cannot name a previous response; a replayed model step therefore ends with `transport_continuation_valid` false and the next request carries the full input, after which the session continues with `previous_response_id` again. Measured on nanocode-ts build-7968b53 with a scripted Responses endpoint under local workerd, a six-cell turn killed in its fourth cell: requests 1 to 4 carried 5, 1, 1 and 1 input items, request 5 (the first after the restart) 13 items and no `previous_response_id`, requests 6 to 8 one item each with it; over HTTPS every request carries the full input, restart or not. The cost is one full-input request per restart, which the prompt cache can still serve; avoiding it would need stored responses, which the default rules out. The turn ID: `Agent::prompt` draws a UUID for every admission, and a backend with driver turn IDs (Codex) names the turn by it, so the part of a turn that runs after a restart carries a second turn ID and its prompt is accepted again as `<new turn ID>:prompt`, while Claude names a turn by its request ID and repeats `<request ID>:prompt` unchanged. A reader of the event stream that counts instructions or groups events by turn ID therefore sees one resumed Codex turn as two; the host's request ID is the same in both parts and is what such a reader has to group by. Keeping the first turn ID would mean storing it with the durable request and reading it back at admission, a change to the admission record that nothing but event readers would gain from, so it is left as documented behaviour.
- fix(claude, codex): a call that the hand never received is dispatched on recovery instead of being reported with an unknown outcome (2026-11-14). A host that dies after it committed the effect row of an `exec` or `wait` and before the frame reached the hand leaves a call the hand has never seen. On recovery the hand answers the resume frame with `NOT_RECEIVED`, the host's `recover` maps that to `CodeModeHostError::unsent`, and both backends turned every recovery error into `Tool execution interrupted by a host crash; outcome unknown. Do not assume it did not run or automatically repeat it.`, so the model was told not to repeat a command that had never run and the turn went on without it. Claude: `ClaudeTools`' recovery keeps the unsent case apart, `recover_tool` returns `Recovered::NotDispatched` for it, and the durable tool step (`durable_tool`) then calls the tool as a step that was never interrupted, including in the step where a recovered `exec` would otherwise be refused as `Code Mode admission was lost during recovery`. Codex: `execute_model_tool_call` asks `recover_code` before it builds the call's context, and an unsent error makes it run the call as a fresh one (the `PreToolUse` hook is not asked again, as for any recovered call). Every other recovery error, and a recovery that finds nothing (`None`: the hand restarted, or the host no longer holds the request), is still reported as unknown and nothing is dispatched: only the hand's own statement that it never received the request proves that the command did not run. For the hand to be asked at all the host has to know the request it sent, which is the host's business: nanocode-ts recorded a hand request only while it sent the frame, after the effect row, so a kill between the two left the row without any record and the hand was never asked; that window was the usual one (its fix is nanocode-ts's entry of the same day, which records the request before the row). Measured on nanocode-ts d6d0578 under local workerd with the hand nanocode-cli-3f97ab0, a scripted model and SIGKILL 3 ms after the model answered with the third cell of a six-cell turn, 5 runs per shape (Claude, gpt-6-luna over HTTPS, an unknown gpt model): before, 3 of 15 runs lost the third command (session log row written, the command never started, the model read `outcome unknown`; in 1 of the 3 the host had recorded the request and the hand answered that it never received it, in 2 the host had no record of it and the hand was not asked); with this entry and nanocode-ts's, 0 of 15, and in the 6 runs that hit the window the hand answered `NOT_RECEIVED`, the command ran once after the restart and the turn asked its 8 model requests. With 10 more runs before and 12 more after on each of the two gpt shapes: 9 of 35 runs lost the command before (the host had recorded the request in 1 of the 9), none of 39 after, of which 12 hit the window (3 on Claude, 9 on the gpt shapes) and ran the command once. No command ran twice in any run.
- fix(code-mode): recovering a call waits for the hand its host awaits, so a restored subagent takes up its running cell instead of reading an unknown outcome (2026-11-14). The subagent runtime resumes restored children as soon as the root agent is built (the restore task that `Registry::adopt_journal` spawns). A host that attaches hands after that, such as nanocode-ts (the module's `init` builds the runtime, then the host attaches each hand, then drives the turn, which places it), had no hand and no placement for the child's session at that moment: `CodeModeExecutors::recover` found no route and answered `None`, and the child's backend reported `Tool execution interrupted by a host crash; outcome unknown` for a cell that kept running on the hand and whose reply the hand still held, while the root's own cell, recovered only once the host drove its turn, was taken up. `CodeModeExecutors::recover` now resolves the session through `ready_placement`, as `exec` does: it waits while the host has said `await_replacement(true)`, the session and its root have no selection, and no default hand is connected. `select` and `select_prompt_hand` wake the waiters, which they did not. `CodeModeHost::recover_with_local_tools` (new; default `adopt`, then `recover`) is what `ToolRuntime::recover_code` calls, and `CodeModeExecutors` implements it as wait, adopt, recover, so the cell tools are adopted on the hands attached by then and not on the none attached before. A host that awaits no hand answers at once, as before. The smallest design that makes a child resume as a parent does is this wait: a child's recovery already runs the same durable step recovery as a root's (`recover_tool`, then the hand's resume frame); only its timing differed. What a host has to do is say that it awaits hands while it opens a session that uses them and stop saying so once a turn is placed (nanocode-ts: `await_replacement(true)` in `open`, `false` in `place` and when it drives background work). Left as it is: the child still gets the runtime's restart notice as a steer on the recovered turn (`RESUME_MESSAGE`, harness.rs `subagent-recovery:`), whose words say that a call running at the restart is not shown and may or may not have taken effect; with the call recovered that sentence is no longer true for it, and making the notice depend on what recovery found is a change to model-facing text that belongs to the subagent runtime's owner. A child of a child whose cell waits in a brain tool is not measured. Checked with output/resume-recovery `placement`: a child's `recover_with_local_tools` stays pending with no hand, stays pending once the hand is attached and the root is not placed, and returns the hand's recovered execution, adopted first, once the root is placed; a host that awaits nothing answers at once; 4 of 4 pass, and the first fails with the wait removed. End to end: the numbers of the entry above (the three kill lanes 0 of 5 before, 5 of 5 after), where the child's requests after the kill are its `wait` on the recovered cell, its `submit_result` and its final message, and no tool result says `outcome unknown`.
- fix(code-mode): a remote cell that a new runtime recovers answers the brain tools it calls, and settles like a cell this runtime started (2026-11-14). `RemoteClient` kept the tools and the context that answer a cell's callbacks only for cells whose `Execute` it had sent (`request`), so after a host restart a callback the hand had held while the brain was away, or one the cell made later, was answered `brain callback tool `<name>` unavailable` and the script failed: a parent's cell blocked in `tools.wait_agent` lost its child's result, and the turn went on without it. `RemoteTransport::adopt` (new, default empty; `RemoteCodeModeHost::adopt` forwards to it, and `exec`, `wait` and `recover_code` already call the host's `adopt` with the session's cell tools) registers them in the client per session (`Adoption::Held`, without the call's history). A callback whose origin the client did not start waits for its session's adoption (`Adoption::Awaited`, a `Signal`) and is then answered by the adopted tool, under its own call ID and in the adopter's turn. It waits instead of failing because the hand sends its held callbacks again right after the resume frame, before the agent's recovery has adopted anything; the wait ends with the client's operation timeout when it has one (then `unavailable`, as before), with the session's `Cancel`, with the callback's `CallbackCancel`, or with the connection. Adoption is by session and not by call, because a recovered `wait` carries its own call ID, not its cell's, and `exec` adopts before `request` registers the same call. `RemoteTransport::delivered` (new, default empty), called by `RemoteCodeModeHost::recover` with the execution it recovered, settles the cell as `request` does when a reply ends it (`Client::settle`: recorded answers forgotten, callback state dropped, receipts carried by the recovered call). Without it the receipt of a `wait_agent` result was never carried, the subagent runtime saw a result nobody had read, and the root got a `subagent-completion` turn after the recovered turn had already used that result: one extra model request. A transport that wraps a client forwards both methods (nanocode-ts's `Recovering`). Not done: a recovered cell that is detached at the end of its turn gets no observer, since the client has no callback state of its own for it. Checked with output/resume-recovery (ignored; its own workspace, path dependency on nanocode-code-mode, a scripted `RemoteLink`): `adoption` asserts that a callback of an unknown origin stays unanswered until `adopt`, is then answered as its own call, that an unadopted tool is refused at once, that an `exec` under the adopted call ID is still dispatched and its own callbacks answered as before, that `Cancel` drops the adoption, and that a 300 ms operation timeout refuses after 300 ms; 8 of 8 pass, and 4 fail with the wait removed. End to end, on nanocode-ts d6d0578 built against nanocode b3816dc27 (before) and against b3816dc27 with this series and nanocode-ts's side of it (after), under local workerd (wrangler 4.151.1) with the hand nanocode-cli-3f97ab0, a scripted Messages endpoint and SIGKILL, 5 runs per lane: a root that spawns a child and waits for it in `tools.wait_agent`, the Worker killed while the child's cell runs, while the child's `wait` is out, and while the child's model is asked, completed correctly 0, 0 and 0 of 5 before and 5, 5 and 5 of 5 with this entry and the next (9 model requests asked and 9 answered, as without a kill; 10 asked when the killed request is asked again); without a kill 5 of 5 both times. With only this entry the root still read the child's result but the child read an unknown outcome for its cell. `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-code-mode` natively and the wasm32-unknown-unknown build of nanocode-ts pass; `cargo clippy --locked --lib -p nanocode-code-mode -p nanocode-tool-host -p nanocode-backend-claude -p nanocode-backend-codex` reports nothing in the files touched.
- fix(claude): a call stopped by quitting nanocode keeps its receipt and says so (2026-11-14, e2e BUG 10). Ctrl-C Ctrl-C while a Bash call ran was reported to the model on resume as "Tool execution interrupted by a host crash; outcome unknown", although nanocode stopped the call itself. Cause: the stopped call's receipt was written as a deferred journal write (a one-call batch completes at the next commit), and a closing session's settle releases the operation (`Release`) without a commit, so the receipt never reached the store and resume found the call begun with no result. Change: the session driver's `Release` persists deferred writes before it releases the claim, as finishing an attempt already does; and a call stopped because the session stopped answers "Tool execution stopped after <s>s because nanocode stopped this session (the user quit nanocode or the agent was closed); the call and the commands it started were stopped then. It may have partly run…" instead of the generic interrupted text. Verified with the real binary in tmux and the mock: a cell running `sleep 10; echo CC >> cc.txt`, Ctrl-C Ctrl-C after 5 s, `nanocode -c`: the model gets "Tool execution stopped after 5.4s because nanocode stopped this session…" (before: the host-crash text); kill -9 still gives the host-crash text, which is accurate. No sim scenario: the runtime scenario's close does not reopen the session without a crash. Files: crates/runtime/durability/src/session.rs, crates/backends/claude/src/agent.rs.
- fix(cli): a second process does not resume a session whose live owner runs a turn (2026-11-14, e2e BUG 12). A second `nanocode -r` of a session another live process was running took ownership (a new JSONL owner fence), saw the live turn as pending, re-ran it (the model was called twice for one turn, a running Bash call was told "interrupted by a host crash") and the first process died with "durability state owner was fenced" or "durability store failed". Taking over an idle session from another window stays as designed (OWNER_MOVED); taking over a turn in flight needs to know the owner is alive, which fences cannot say. Change: store-jsonl holds an exclusive file lock on `<session>.owner` beside the session journal from the first acquire until the process exits, with its pid inside (`std::fs::File::try_lock`, no unsafe; a crashed process's lock is released by the kernel, so the pid is only for the message), and `JsonlArchiver::live_owner` answers the pid when another process holds it. `open_session` refuses a session with pending turns whose owner lock is held elsewhere: "session <id> is running a turn in nanocode process <pid>; let that turn finish or stop it there, then resume". Verified with the real binary and the mock: A runs a 3 s Bash cell, B resumes 1 s later: B exits 1 with that message, A completes rc 0, one model call per request, one line in the file, and B's next resume after A finished works; after `kill -9` of a running exec the next resume continues the interrupted turn as before. Left: a process that took over an idle session while the first still holds its lock cannot take the lock, so a third process names the first one's pid. No sim scenario: the sim's stores are in memory and KV, the lock is the JSONL store's and the CLI's. Files: crates/integrations/store-jsonl/src/{sessions,lib}.rs, bin/nanocode/src/app.rs.
- fix(claude): the transcript keeps the turns a compaction summarized (2026-11-14, e2e BUG 7, Claude half). After /compact or an automatic compaction, resume and `nanocode sessions <id>` showed only the turns after it, and the summary as a "›" user prompt once a later turn moved it into the messages. Cause: the saved transcript is rendered from the checkpoint's model history, which compaction replaces. Change: `Conversation::compacted` keeps the messages a compaction drops (not the summary message), paged like `code_calls` (`PagedConversation::compacted`, an optional sequence, so older checkpoints load and the checkpoint stays O(new records)); it is never sent to the model. The format renders `compacted` then `messages` through the same prompt matching, skips summary messages (a compaction block or text starting with `COMPACT_CONTINUED`), and shows "Retained conversation summary" only for sessions compacted before this change. Memory: the dropped messages stay resident instead of being freed, bounded by the session's history, which the store keeps anyway. Verified with the real binary against the mock after an automatic compaction (`#tokens 990000`): `nanocode sessions <id>` lists all four turns, no summary prompt. Not done: the Codex harness, whose checkpoint history keeps only user messages and the compaction item after compaction, and the subagent-completion input it shows as a user prompt. Files: crates/backends/claude/src/agent.rs, crates/backends/claude/src/agent/durable.rs, crates/backends/claude/src/durability/format.rs.
- fix(claude): a background Bash command that a previous process left running is reported on resume (2026-11-14, e2e BUG 14). A `run_in_background` command dies when nanocode quits (Jobs::shutdown aborts it) and its completion can never be delivered, but nothing recorded that, so after resume the model waited for a notice that never came. Background jobs live only in the process (`Jobs`), so the restored history is the one record: when a Claude agent is built from a snapshot, `stopped_background_notices` finds this session's local job IDs (`<session>-bash-<n>`, so a fork's parent jobs and a hand's are left alone) in "running in background with ID" or "moved to the background (ID" texts with no later `<task-id>` notification, "stopped task:" or "is not running" for them, and queues one developer notice per job, a `<task-notification>` with status killed saying its completion will never be reported and its outcome is unknown; the notice ID (`background-stopped-<id>`) keeps a queued one from repeating, and once delivered its `<task-id>` settles the job for later resumes. Verified with the real binary in tmux against the mock: a cell starting `sleep 15 && echo BG > bg.txt` in the background, Ctrl-C Ctrl-C, 15 s wait (no bg.txt), `nanocode -c` and a prompt: the request carries the notice for `…-bash-0`; before, nothing. Not done: job IDs restart at 0 in a new process, so a new job can reuse an old ID. Files: crates/backends/claude/src/agent.rs.
- fix(claude): a turn cancelled while the model answers keeps its prompt (2026-11-14, e2e BUG 3). With Esc Esc during a Claude reply the user's prompt vanished: the next request lacked it (the model answered that there was no earlier question) and after resume the transcript no longer showed it; Codex keeps it. Cause: run_rounds builds the request in a local `pending` (history, notices, the prompt) and writes it into the conversation only after a model response; a cancel during the response returned `TurnCancelled` with the conversation unchanged, so the checkpoint that settled the cancelled turn dropped the prompt (a cancel during tool calls already kept it). Change: a response that fails because the user cancelled, not because the session is closing (that path releases the turn for resume), commits `pending` plus Claude Code's `[Request interrupted by user]` user message, as Claude Code does on an interrupt while streaming; the transcript shows the prompt and not the marker (an unadmitted user message after a prompt). Sim: the runtime scenario now cancels one root turn per seed with probability 30% (`CANCEL_TURN_PPM`, its own RNG stream so other draws keep their seeds) once the model has seen that turn's request, records the cancel in the world, and the model server checks that every later request of that root still carries the cancelled turn's prompt; mutation `drop-cancelled-prompt` rewrites that prompt out of requests and is caught (13 to 14 of 100 seeds), cfo row `canary_drop_cancelled_prompt`. Before the fix the invariant fails 13 of 100 seeds (`r0 turn 2's request lost cancelled turn 1's prompt`); after, `sweep.sh 1 400 --scenario runtime` passes 399 of 399, `--twice` and `--wire http` 149 of 149 each, `--tidy` clean. Real binary in tmux against the mock (`#slow 2`): the request after the cancel carries "first prompt …", "[Request interrupted by user]", "second prompt", and `nanocode sessions <id>` lists the cancelled prompt. Files: crates/backends/claude/src/agent.rs, bin/nanocode-sim/{cfo.sh,src/whole.rs,src/server.rs,src/world.rs,src/httpd.rs,src/network.rs}.
- fix(tui): automatic compaction shows its notice (2026-11-14, e2e BUG 15). A manual /compact showed "compacting context…" and "context compacted", an automatic one nothing, so a user could not tell why the model forgot details. Cause: the Claude harness emitted only `ModelCompactionCompleted` after its four automatic compactions (before a turn, between rounds, request-too-large and context-window recovery) and never `ModelCompactionStarted`, and the TUI mapped only Started; the manual path published both, and the "context compacted" line came from the action, not the event. Change: one `State::compact_in_turn` emits Started (index, active tokens, limit, as the manual path and Codex do), then Completed or `ModelCompactionFailed` with the error, and replaces the four copies of the timing and emit code; the TUI maps Completed to "context compacted" unless one was shown since the last "compacting context…", and the /compact action's success shows it only when the event has not (`AppEvent::Compacted { since }`), so a manual compaction still shows each line once whichever arrives first. Verified with the real binary in tmux against a mock Messages endpoint whose `#tokens 990000` reports usage: before, "after bigger" showed only the reply; after, "ℹ compacting context…" and "ℹ context compacted" above it. Commands: `cargo build --locked --release -p nanocode-cli`. Files: crates/backends/claude/src/agent.rs, bin/nanocode/src/{events,app,actions}.rs.
- fix(djs): Object.assign's native entry declines a key the target only inherits when the target is not extensible, so the builtin's [[Set]] fails and throws as the spec says (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 Code Mode conformance track: differential fuzzing). `assignable` (builtins/fast.rs) accepted any key found as a writable data property on the target's chain, then wrote it with CreateDataProperty, whose failure on a frozen, sealed or non-extensible target was dropped: `Object.assign(Object.freeze({}), {valueOf: 1})` returned the unchanged target where Node 24 throws a TypeError (OrdinarySet's CreateDataProperty on the receiver fails, Set's throw flag turns it into the error). An inherited key now needs an extensible target, as an absent one already did; own keys are unchanged. Found by output/cm-fuzz: this change alone makes 11 of the base run's 5,061 divergent programs (of 199,232) print what Node prints, each an assign of an object carrying `valueOf`/`toString` onto a frozen or sealed target. The repro output/cm-fuzz/repros/object-assign-nonextensible.js (7 cases: frozen, non-extensible and sealed targets with inherited keys, a sealed own key, a non-extensible object with an inherited writable key, an extensible one, a plain copy) differed from Node 24 on 4 cases before and none after. Instructions (`perf stat -e instructions:u`, three interleaved runs, djsfuzz): 300,000 `Object.assign({}, base, {c: i})` 2,199.45M -> 2,196.15M, 300,000 `Object.assign({}, {valueOf: i, b: 2})` 1,512.55M -> 1,514.65M. test262 subset 8,631 of 9,288 passing, the same set; the 25 edge cells print the same output and events. Code Mode cells with this track's three djs fixes together (output/cm-fuzz/cells.sh: 3,000 fuzz programs as cells through the cm-conf native-host runner, Claude backend; tscells.sh: 1,000 through nanocode-ts ts/run.ts on the rebuilt wasm; Node 24 reference with its native-function whitespace rewritten to djs's): native-host 2,926 to 2,975 cells printing what Node prints (the other 23: V8's object-literal order after a leading spread, for-in over a Proxy, V8's one-element sort shortcut), ts-node 934 to 952 (the other 46: nanocode-ts's web globals such as structuredClone, which the reference lacks, and the same V8 differences). The cm-conf suite on native-host is unchanged at Claude 575/600 and Codex 564/581 (no case calls these builtins; two timing-sensitive durability cases traded places). Files: crates/patches/djs/crates/djs-core/src/builtins/fast.rs.

- fix(djs): Function.prototype.toString of a bound function or a callable Proxy is `function () {\n    [native code]\n}`, with no name and no trap call (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 Code Mode conformance track: differential fuzzing). The spec requires a NativeFunction there, whose name part must be a PropertyName, and allows no other steps; djs printed a bound function as `function bound f() {…}` (two names, not NativeFunction syntax) and named a proxy by [[Get]] of `name`, which ran the handler's `get` trap (a throwing trap made toString throw), as QuickJS does. Builtins and host functions keep `function name() {\n    [native code]\n}` and JS functions their source text. Node 24 prints `function () { [native code] }` for both; the line breaks inside the braces are implementation-defined and stay djs's. Found by output/cm-fuzz: this change alone makes 1,178 of the base run's 5,061 divergent programs (of 199,232) print what Node prints, the largest class; with the reference's native-function whitespace rewritten to djs's (implementation-defined), this track's three djs fixes together make 3,443 of them match. The repro output/cm-fuzz/repros/fn-tostring.js (bound, twice-bound, a proxy whose `get` trap throws for `name`, a proxy of a builtin, of a class, a builtin, a JS function) gave 4 invalid or trap-calling results before and none after. test262 subset 8,631 of 9,288 passing, the same set (bound-function.js, proxy-*.js and built-in-function-object.js pass before and after); the 25 edge cells print the same output and events. Code Mode cells with this track's three djs fixes together (output/cm-fuzz/cells.sh: 3,000 fuzz programs as cells through the cm-conf native-host runner, Claude backend; tscells.sh: 1,000 through nanocode-ts ts/run.ts on the rebuilt wasm; Node 24 reference with its native-function whitespace rewritten to djs's): native-host 2,926 to 2,975 cells printing what Node prints (the other 23: V8's object-literal order after a leading spread, for-in over a Proxy, V8's one-element sort shortcut), ts-node 934 to 952 (the other 46: nanocode-ts's web globals such as structuredClone, which the reference lacks, and the same V8 differences). The cm-conf suite on native-host is unchanged at Claude 575/600 and Codex 564/581 (no case calls these builtins; two timing-sensitive durability cases traded places). Files: crates/patches/djs/builtins/function.ts and its generated builtins/gen/{prelude,prelude-slim,prelude-noembed}.js, resume-points.txt (`cargo run -p djs-bgen` in crates/patches/djs), crates/patches/djs/crates/djs-core/src/builtins/function.rs.

- fix(djs): RegExp.escape escapes what EncodeForRegExpEscape names and nothing else (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 Code Mode conformance track: differential fuzzing). SyntaxCharacter and `/` take a backslash, U+0009 to U+000D their ControlEscape letter, the other punctuators `,-=<>#&!%:;`~'"` (with the backtick), U+0020, U+00A0 and an initial ASCII letter or digit `\xHH`, the other white space, line terminators and lone surrogates `\uHHHH`, and every other code point is itself. djs wrote `\xHH` for every code unit below U+0021 and from U+0080 to U+00FF, as QuickJS does, so `RegExp.escape("café")` was `"caf\\xe9"` and `RegExp.escape("a\0")` `"\\x61\\x00"` where the spec and Node 24 give `"café"` and `"\\x61"` followed by U+0000. Found by output/cm-fuzz, a differential fuzzer that runs seeded random strict-mode programs in djs (output/cm-fuzz/djsfuzz, djs-embed with frozen_builtins(false) as Code Mode builds it) and in Node 24 (node:vm) and compares their printed results: in its base run of 199,232 programs (5,061 diverged from Node), this change alone makes 208 of the divergent programs print what Node prints. The repro output/cm-fuzz/repros/regexp-escape.js (12 inputs: U+0000, Latin-1 letters, NBSP and U+0085, LS, BOM, syntax characters, punctuators, lone and paired surrogates, C0 controls, U+3000) differed from Node 24 on 4 inputs before and on none after. test262 subset 8,631 of 9,288 passing, the same set (it has no RegExp.escape tests); the 25 edge cells print the same output and events. Code Mode cells with this track's three djs fixes together (output/cm-fuzz/cells.sh: 3,000 fuzz programs as cells through the cm-conf native-host runner, Claude backend; tscells.sh: 1,000 through nanocode-ts ts/run.ts on the rebuilt wasm; Node 24 reference with its native-function whitespace rewritten to djs's): native-host 2,926 to 2,975 cells printing what Node prints (the other 23: V8's object-literal order after a leading spread, for-in over a Proxy, V8's one-element sort shortcut), ts-node 934 to 952 (the other 46: nanocode-ts's web globals such as structuredClone, which the reference lacks, and the same V8 differences). The cm-conf suite on native-host is unchanged at Claude 575/600 and Codex 564/581 (no case calls these builtins; two timing-sensitive durability cases traded places). Files: crates/patches/djs/crates/djs-core/src/builtins/regexp.rs.

- perf(djs): `%TypedArray%.prototype.fill` writes its first element and then copies the filled run forward in doubling steps with `TypedArrayCopy` (one memmove per step for an array's own element kind) instead of one interpreted `TypedArraySet` per element (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 Code Mode conformance track: workerd CPU budget). Every element gets the one value `ToElementValue` converted before the loop, and no user code runs between the writes, so the copies store the same bytes a `Set` per element did. A 1 MiB fill was a million interpreted iterations, about 8 fuel each, so under nanocode-ts's Cloudflare cell budget (500 slices of 200,000 fuel) `new Uint8Array(8 * 1024 * 1024).fill(3)` stopped with `one synchronous run exceeded this host's CPU budget`, and the cases that fill 1 MiB chunks to reach the 32 MiB cell cap never reached it. Measured in nanocode-ts on Node on dev-georgios (one cell through the ts-node runner, 3 interleaved rounds against the module built from master, `Date.now()` around each loop): four 8 MiB `Uint8Array` fills 4,227 to 5,187 ms before and 21 to 49 ms after, 2,000 `Float64Array(512)` fills 128 to 155 and 23 to 31 ms, 20,000 `Uint8Array(16)` fills 106 to 203 and 99 to 145 ms. 1,323 fill results (nine element kinds by 12 values by 12 start and end pairs, both BigInt kinds, a `Uint16Array` at byte offset 6, lengths 0 to 65,537 from index 1, NaN, a BigInt array given a Number, a resizable buffer, 8 MiB) hash the same as Node's per group before and after. Conformance with output/cm-conf: limits/workerd-allocation-under-cap, limits/heap-cap-is-per-cell, limits/oom-configured-cap, limits/oom-keeps-earlier-output, limits/oom-uncatchable-no-catch-no-finally and limits/oom-workerd-default-cap fail on ts-workerd for both backends before and pass after, and limits/uncapped-hosts-allow-large-heap (64 filled 1 MiB chunks) failed on native-host and ts-node for both backends (the cell was still running at its yield) and passes after. `scripts/bgen.sh --check` passes; `cargo check --locked --lib` for nanocode-code-mode-engine and djs-embed and `cargo clippy --no-deps -p nanocode-code-mode-engine -- -D warnings` pass natively and for wasm32-unknown-unknown. Files: crates/patches/djs/builtins/typedarray.ts, crates/patches/djs/builtins/gen/prelude.js, crates/patches/djs/builtins/gen/prelude-noembed.js, crates/patches/djs/builtins/gen/resume-points.txt.

- fix(codex): Code Mode and tool-result images keep their `detail` in Codex function_call_output and custom_tool_call_output items, as upstream Codex does (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 Code Mode conformance track: Codex image detail). `function_output` (crates/backends/codex/src/model/input.rs) wrote `detail: None` for every `input_image`, so `image(x, "original")`, `image({ image_url, detail })`, an MCP block's `_meta["codex/imageDetail"]`, a content-results tool's detail and the default `high` never reached the item. Upstream Codex at the revision the backend pins (openai/codex c6e4438a, crates/backends/codex/upstream/tools.json) keeps it: `FunctionCallOutputContentItem::InputImage` carries `detail` (codex-rs/protocol/src/models.rs) and Code Mode's `response_adapter.rs` (codex-rs/core/src/tools/code_mode) maps each item's detail, `high` when it has none; each request then runs `normalize_image_detail` (codex-rs/core/src/client_common.rs), which removes detail for a Responses Lite model (models.json `use_responses_lite`: Astra, Sol, Luna, Daybreak and the 5.6 models) and turns `original` into `high` for a model without original support. nanocode's `strip_image_detail` (crates/backends/codex/client/src/responses/request.rs) already removes it for Sol, Terra, Luna, Astra and Daybreak Blue, so the wire to those models is unchanged. Function outputs now keep `Some(detail)` for inline and file images, so a model that is not Responses Lite (a custom model such as gpt-5.5, Kimi, GLM, MiMo, whose message images already carried detail) receives it, and on every model the history keeps it: replay after a checkpoint (`prepare_replay_images`, run/state.rs, through `prepare_history_images`) read the missing detail as `auto` and fit an `original` image to the high-detail limits, and the compaction estimate (client/src/session/compaction_estimate.rs `image_bytes`) counted an `original` image as a resized one. Claude's image block has no detail field; its exec description already says images reach the model at the size it accepts whatever their `detail` (the tool-result audio entry below), so description.rs stays as it is. Conformance: output/cm-conf (git-ignored), output/ cases, release builds of cm/notify-media e84fbbcce (before) and this change (after), the suite's grader with two runner changes: the runners record the model they drove (`--codex-model`, default gpt-6-luna), and for a Responses Lite Codex model the grader drops detail from the expected images only, as upstream's wire does, so a detail sent to Luna still fails. The 39 native-cli codex cases the notify-media track listed as failing on detail (output/image-*, generated-image-*, text-split-by-image, yield-control-media, max-output-tokens-mixed-*, max-output-tokens-images-free, default-keeps-empty-text-with-media, format-failed-keeps-media): with gpt-5.5, 0/39 -> 39/39 (all native-cli codex output/ 172/212 -> 211/212); ts-node codex (nanocode-ts 2aad477 with each SDK's wasm) the 44 detail cases with gpt-5.5 0/44 -> 44/44 (output/ 178/226 -> 222/226). With gpt-6-luna the wire carries no detail before or after, as upstream's does: 39/39 and 44/44 with the lite rule, 0/39 and 0/44 with the old grader, whose expectation of a detail on Luna's wire was wrong. The cases left failing are unrelated (image-many-interleaved keeps only the newest 8 images on a custom model or overflows Luna's context in ts-node; ts-node's usize pragma checks and exit-with-unawaited-call). Commands: `node output/cm-conf/cli/run.ts --nanocode target/release/nanocode --codex-model gpt-5.5 --backend codex --only output/`, the same with gpt-6-luna, `NANOCODE_TS=… NANOCODE_WASM_PATH=… node output/cm-conf/ts/run.ts --codex-model gpt-5.5 --backend codex --only output/`. Files: crates/backends/codex/src/model/input.rs.

- fix(code-mode): `performance.now()` in a cell revived after a restart continues the cell's own clock instead of starting again at zero, and a revived timer never fires before its delay (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 Code Mode conformance track: performance.now across restart). Journaled `performance.now()` reads replay their values, but a live read after replay was `started.elapsed()` from the revived engine's start (cell.rs), while a revived timer keeps its wall-clock deadline (`at_ms + delay_ms`); so `performance.now() - p0` around a 2 s timer read less than 2000 after a crash mid-timer, and could read negative. A cell journal's header now carries `started_at_ms` (`CellJournalHeader`, `CellJournal`, the engine's `CellJournaling`; new optional public fields, `None` in a journal written before this change), the wall time the cell was admitted. A replaying engine adds the wall time since then, read to the nanosecond against that whole millisecond so it never comes out short, to its own monotonic clock, and a read never goes below the last value the cell saw (replayed or live), which keeps the clock monotonic when the wall clock is set back between hosts. A revived timer's remaining time is `delay_ms + 1` less the wall time since `at_ms`: `at_ms` is the set time floored to a millisecond, so the true set time is before `at_ms + 1` and the old `at_ms + delay_ms - wall_ms()`, with both sides floored, let a timer fire up to 1 ms early, which is what was left of the failure once the clock continued. A cell that is not replaying reads the clock exactly as before (the base is zero), and a journal without `started_at_ms` revives as before. Conformance, durability/performance-now-continuous-across-restart on native-host: Claude fail (`monotonic false true`) to pass; 5 interleaved runs of both backends, origin/master 2 of 10 `monotonic true true`, this change 10 of 10; ts-node Claude passes before and after; the rest of durability and the timer crash cases (async/crash-mid-timer-*, tools/crash-mid-timer-*, durability/timer-*) pass on native-host as before. Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib` and `cargo clippy --no-deps -- -D warnings` for nanocode-code-mode-engine and nanocode-code-mode, natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, rustfmt. Files: crates/runtime/code-mode-engine/src/{cell.rs,journal.rs}, crates/runtime/code-mode/src/code_mode/{replay.rs,mod.rs}.

- fix(code-mode): a cell's journal is marked finished before its final result is returned, instead of by a task spawned after it (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 Code Mode conformance track: finished cells across restart). `CellJournals::finished` (69eb33022) spawned `mark_finished`, so the exec or wait that observed a cell end returned its result while the journal's finished mark could still be unwritten. A host that stopped in that window, a clean restart right after the reply included, revived the cell from its unfinished journal on the next `adopt`: it replayed the whole cell, sat as a live cell nobody waited on, and a later `wait` on its ID returned its final output a second time instead of `exec cell N not found` (durability/finished-cell-not-found-after-restart, once the runners really restart: native-host printed `done` again on both backends). `finished` is now async and `remove_and_join` awaits it, so the mark is saved (or, on OneLog, pushed ahead of the commit that carries the result) before the result goes out; a restored finished journal then stays dormant for recovery of the call that observed it, as 69eb33022 intends. Cost: one sink save awaited at the end of each journaled cell where there was one spawned before; with OneLog that is a lease push, with agent-host's `DurableCellJournals` an ordered store commit, and nothing changes for a runtime without journals. Conformance: durability/finished-cell-not-found-after-restart, native-host both backends, fail (`done` again) to pass; ts-node Claude passes (a graceful restart there ends the turn first). Commands: as in the entry below. Files: crates/runtime/code-mode/src/code_mode/{replay.rs,mod.rs}.

- fix(code-mode): `store()` values survive a restart: a cell that ends by itself saves the session's whole store map through its `CellJournalSink`, and the first `adopt` or `exec` of the session after a restart loads it back before any cell starts (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 Code Mode conformance track: store across restart). The exec description promises that `store` keeps a value "for later `exec` calls in the same session", but `CodeModeRuntime.stored` lived only in memory: after a restart only a revived cell's journal header carried values, and only the ones that cell started with, so `load` read `undefined` for every key a finished cell had stored (durability/store-persists-after-resumed-cell printed `undefined,two`). `CellJournalSink` gains `save_stored(session_id, stored)` and `load_stored(session_id)` (a JSON object of the session's values), both with defaults that save and load nothing, so a sink that does not implement them keeps the old in-memory behavior and no implementor breaks. A cell's writes are merged into the session map and, when the cell wrote any, the merged map is saved before the cell's result is reported; saves go one at a time under an `Owned` that `CellJournals` shares with its cells' `Persistence`, each taking the map as it is when its turn comes, so the last save holds every merged key even when cells finish together. `CellJournals::load` reads the map once per session with the journals, and `adopt` and `exec` put it into the runtime's map for keys the runtime does not hold. Sinks: OneLog (nanocode-ts, `nanocode-agent`) keeps the map as one `Record::Stored` under `$nanocode_stored\n<session>`, which a log snapshot carries forward, pushed like the cell's other records and committed with the next commit, so a write is exactly as durable as the step that made it (a crash that rolls a step back rolls its writes back with it); agent-host's `DurableCellJournals` keeps it as a content-addressed payload named by the session head's new optional `stored` field (a head without it reads as no values), blanking the previous payload's root as cell links are blanked; the conformance native runner's sink keeps it in memory across its incarnations. Unchanged and now stated here: the writes of a cell that is terminated, runs out of memory or exceeds the CPU budget are dropped (host.rs sends no stored values for those ends), as async/terminate-discards-stores, output/store-terminated-lost, limits/oom-drops-this-cells-store-writes and limits/cpu-exhausted-drops-store-writes pin: a cell's writes take effect together when the script ends by itself (completion, a thrown error, `exit()`), and a cell the host stops may be halfway through a multi-key update, so none of them is kept. The description is not changed: its "later `exec` calls in the same session" is what this makes true across restarts, and the stop rule is a property of the stopped cell, not of `store`. Conformance (the runners now restart for a `restart` step that follows no crash, see output/cm-conf; before, they ignored it, so store-persists-across-restart passed without restarting): native-host, both backends, store-persists-after-resumed-cell fail (`undefined,two`) to pass, store-persists-across-restart passes with a real restart (`after restart: {"n":7}`); ts-node Claude (nanocode-ts cm/durability over this SDK, wasm profile), store-persists-after-resumed-cell fail (`undefined,two`) to pass and store-persists-across-restart passes across a finished turn and a fresh `AgentRuntime`; full native-host suite, 1,408 runs: no new failure from this change. Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib` and `cargo clippy --no-deps -- -D warnings` for nanocode-code-mode, nanocode-agent and nanocode-agent-host, both again for nanocode-code-mode with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown` (nanocode-agent's wasm check fails on origin/master with the same unresolved cell-journal imports, unrelated), rustfmt. Files: crates/runtime/code-mode/src/code_mode/{replay.rs,mod.rs}, crates/runtime/agent/src/one_log.rs, crates/integrations/agent-host/src/cell_journals.rs.

- fix(image): an image with detail `low` is prepared like `auto` and `high` (fit to 2,048 px and 2,500 patches) and keeps its detail, instead of becoming "image content omitted because detail 'low' is not supported; use 'high', 'original', or 'auto'" (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 Code Mode conformance track: notify and media). image() documents and accepts `low` (description.rs, code-values.mjs), MCP `_meta` and the Chat transport take it, and the Responses API defines it (the provider gives the model a low-resolution version); only nanocode-image refused it, in `prepare_image` (tool outputs and history) and `load_for_prompt_data_url` (Read and view_image), so a documented option always lost the image. Low now takes the high-detail limits for the local resize and the provider applies its own low-resolution mode from the item's detail where the transport sends one (Code Mode outputs on Codex currently send none: model/input.rs `function_output` writes `detail: None`, a separate finding). Claude has no image detail and its own preparation, unchanged. `ImagePreparationError::UnsupportedLowDetail` and its placeholder leave. Conformance: output/cm-conf (git-ignored) at release builds of origin/master 1072097ac (before) and this branch (after), graded by the suite's grader with this track's runner fixes (Codex `additional_tools` in the scripted model, Claude inline notifications taken off before items are compared, companions of a failed Claude result, Codex notifications attributed to the result they follow) and `expect_on` entries for what a backend's wire carries: native-cli and ts-node codex output/image-detail-low-accepted and image-detail-null-argument carried the placeholder before and the image after (both still fail on the Codex wire's missing detail); Claude passed before and after. Files: crates/core/image/src/lib.rs.

- docs(code-mode): exec's `max_output_tokens` and wait's `max_tokens` no longer promise unlimited output, and Claude's exec description states its bound (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 Code Mode conformance track: notify and media). Both model backends keep at most 12,000 estimated tokens of one tool result's text, head and tail around `…N tokens truncated…`: Claude's `bound_tool_result` with `TOOL_RESULT_TOKEN_LIMIT` (UTF-16 units / 4, across the result's text blocks) and Codex's `truncate_output_content` with `TOOL_OUTPUT_TOKEN_LIMIT` (bytes / 4) when the output enters history. In output/large-100kb-text a 100,000-byte `text()` arrived as 47,980 bytes on native-cli for both backends, which is why only about 48 KB showed up; the runner read it correctly. The bound is a recorded context policy and is surfaced in the result, so it stays; the descriptions said "Omit for unlimited output". Now exec: "Omit it for no budget of its own; the agent may still shorten a long result in its context, marking the cut with `…N tokens truncated…`."; compact: "(default none, though the agent may still cut a long result, marked `…N tokens truncated…`)"; wait's description and schema: "Omit it for no budget of its own." / "Omit for no budget of its own."; Claude's exec schema: "Omit for no budget of its own."; and Claude's exec description: "A result keeps at most 12000 tokens of text (about 4 characters each), cut in the middle at `…N tokens truncated…`." from the constant. No behavior changes. The four large-* cases gain `expect_on` entries for the model-driven hosts with the computed cut (marker and byte count): native-cli claude and codex 0/8 -> 8/8, ts-node 8/8. Files: crates/backends/claude/src/{agent,claude_tools}.rs, crates/runtime/code-mode/src/code_mode/{description,spec}.rs.

- fix(backends): a tool result's audio, Claude's OpenAI image file references and a `data:` image URL without base64 reach the model as omission notes, and Claude reads a `DATA:` scheme as data (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 Code Mode conformance track: notify and media). Neither wire carries audio in a tool result: a Claude tool_result holds text, image and document blocks, and Codex function call outputs carry text and images (the existing note for documents in model/input.rs says so). Claude's `block()` (crates/backends/claude/src/claude_tools.rs) serialized every other item as JSON text, so `audio(dataUrl)` sent `{"type":"input_audio","audio_url":"data:audio/wav;base64,…"}` with the whole payload as text and `image({ file_id })` sent `{"type":"input_image","file_id":…,"detail":"high"}`; Codex's `function_output` passed audio on and the history's `truncate_output_content` (client/src/session/context.rs) then dropped it without a word, so the model saw the header and nothing. Now Claude sends "audio content omitted because Claude cannot use audio" and its existing "image content omitted because Claude cannot use OpenAI image file references" (prompt.rs, already used for prompts), and Codex "[audio omitted: Codex function call outputs carry text and images]" beside its document note. Claude's `block()` also matched `data:` case-sensitively and treated a data URL without `;base64,` as remote, so `DATA:image/png;base64,…` (RFC 2397 schemes are case-insensitive; image() and nanocode-image accept it) and `data:garbage` both became "remote image URLs are not supported"; the scheme is now case-insensitive and a data URL without base64 gets "image content omitted because it could not be processed", the note Codex's preparation gives. The exec description's audio() says tool results carry no audio and the model gets a note (compact too), and Claude's exec description adds that images reach the model at the size it accepts whatever their `detail` and that an image `file_id` arrives as a note. Conformance: output/cm-conf (git-ignored) at release builds of origin/master 1072097ac (before) and this branch (after), graded by the suite's grader with this track's runner fixes (Codex `additional_tools` in the scripted model, Claude inline notifications taken off before items are compared, companions of a failed Claude result, Codex notifications attributed to the result they follow) and `expect_on` entries for what a backend's wire carries: native-cli claude output/audio-* (8), yield-control-media, max-output-tokens-audio-kept, image-file-id, image-file-id-detail, image-file-id-length-limit, image-array, generated-image-file-id, image-data-url-uppercase-scheme and image-garbage-data-url-accepted 0/17 -> 17/17; native-cli codex audio-* (8) and max-output-tokens-audio-kept 0/9 -> 9/9 (yield-control-media now carries the note but still fails on Codex's missing image detail); ts-node claude the same 17 cases 0/17 -> 17/17 and ts-node codex the same 9 0/9 -> 9/9; values/audio-* (4), values/image-data-garbage and values/image-data-image-png-base64-invalid on native-cli and ts-node claude 0/6 -> 6/6 and values/audio-* on native-cli and ts-node codex 0/4 -> 4/4; native-host (Code Mode's own items) unchanged. Files: crates/backends/claude/src/{claude_tools,prompt}.rs, crates/backends/codex/src/model/input.rs, crates/runtime/code-mode/src/code_mode/description.rs.

- fix(claude): each Code Mode notification is its own text block at the end of the exec or wait tool_result, and the exec description says what `notify()` does on both backends (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 Code Mode conformance track: notify and media). The description said notify "immediately injects an extra `custom_tool_call_output` for the current `exec` call". Neither half held. A notification reaches the model with the next result the cell returns, the exec or the wait that observes it (`observe_updates` buffers it, crates/runtime/code-mode/src/code_mode/mod.rs; only the observer's live update is immediate), and only Codex has custom_tool_call_output items (one per notification after the call's output, backends/codex/src/model/run/tool_calls.rs). Claude's `code_reply` (crates/backends/claude/src/claude_tools.rs) appended each notification to a plain-text result with a newline and pushed it as a block onto a result with blocks, so `notify("n")` alone arrived as `Script completed\nWall time 0.0 seconds\nOutput:\n\nn`, indistinguishable from printed text, while next to an image it was its own block. A text result with notifications now becomes one block and every notification is a text block after it, the Messages counterpart of Codex's extra item. Description: `notify(...)`: "adds a separate output item for the current `exec` call after the next result the cell returns (this `exec`, or a later `wait`). Values are stringified like `text(...)`."; compact: "adds a separate output item for this call to the next result the cell returns". Conformance: output/cm-conf (git-ignored) at release builds of origin/master 1072097ac (before) and this branch (after), graded by the suite's grader with this track's runner fixes (Codex `additional_tools` in the scripted model, Claude inline notifications taken off before items are compared, companions of a failed Claude result, Codex notifications attributed to the result they follow) and `expect_on` entries for what a backend's wire carries: on native-cli claude the request after `notify("n")` carried one text block before and two (`Script completed…Output:\n`, `n`) after; output/notify-basic, -only, -order, -stringify, -many, -large, -before-failure-kept, -after-yield-arrives-with-wait and text-not-split-by-notify fail on native-host and native-cli claude in the baseline matrix (9 + 9) and pass after (the baseline failures were the grader comparing items before taking inline notifications off; with that fixed the old inline form passes too, so the case outcome does not separate the two forms), ts-node claude passes these 9. - fix(code-mode): `notify()` replaces the base64 payload of a `data:` URL with the note `text()` writes, `[<n> base64 characters not printed as text; <advice>]` (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 Code Mode conformance track: notify and media). The exec description says notify's values are stringified like `text(...)`, and `text()` sends every string through `without_data_urls` (crates/runtime/code-mode-engine/src/cell.rs `push_text`), so a printed image never reaches the model as thousands of base64 characters with no way to see it; `NOTIFY` in `host_call` sent its text straight to `RuntimeEvent::Notify`, so `notify(dataUrl)` put the whole payload into the model's context. It now runs the same function with the same rule (a payload no longer than the note is kept, the advice follows the media type). The case output/notify-not-scrubbed, which pinned the old behavior, is now output/notify-data-url-scrubbed and expects `data:image/png;base64,[200 base64 characters not printed as text; pass the value to image() to see it]` for a 200-character payload. Conformance: output/cm-conf (git-ignored) at release builds of origin/master 1072097ac (before) and this branch (after), graded by the suite's grader with this track's runner fixes (Codex `additional_tools` in the scripted model, Claude inline notifications taken off before items are compared, companions of a failed Claude result, Codex notifications attributed to the result they follow) and `expect_on` entries for what a backend's wire carries: native-host claude and codex pass (the old case passed by expecting the raw payload), native-cli claude and codex pass, ts-node (nanocode-ts at 2aad477 with this SDK's wasm) claude and codex 0/2 -> 2/2. Commands: `cd output/cm-conf/native && ./target/release/run --cases "cases/*.jsonl" --backend both`, `node cli/run.ts --nanocode target/release/nanocode --backend both`, `NANOCODE_TS=… NANOCODE_WASM_PATH=… node ts/run.ts --backend both --only output/`.
