- fix(code-mode): `exec`'s description says a call to a name missing from `ALL_TOOLS` is a nested call the host answers (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 Code Mode conformance track: tools-dedupe). It said such a call "rejects locally with `TOOL_NOT_AVAILABLE`; it does not dispatch a tool, unless its input names a `hand`". Since cells send missing names to the host (code-tools.mjs `missing`, the decision "A Code Mode cell sends a call to a nested tool missing from its catalog to the host"), that is not what happens: the call is a nested call like any other (it starts, gets a receipt, counts in "Nested calls still running", in the abandoned-call lists, toward the nested call limit and the cell guard), the host runs a tool a provider resolves by that name (`DynamicToolProvider::resolve`) or the named hand's tool, and only then answers `TOOL_NOT_AVAILABLE`; only Object's own names and `toJSON` still reject in the cell. The behavior is the intended one (it is what lets a provider's late tools and a hand's own tools work), so the model-facing text changes, not the code: "a call to a name missing from `ALL_TOOLS` is still a nested call the host answers: it runs that hand's tool of that name when its input names a `hand` (such as one only a phone offers) or a tool the host found since the cell started, and otherwise rejects with `TOOL_NOT_AVAILABLE`." The line is in every Code Mode `exec` description, so prompts that carry it change once. Checked on dev-georgios: output/tools-dedupe-check prints the old line from `exec_description` at 1072097ac and the new one here; output/cm-conf's missing-name cases (tools/missing-tool-*, tools/object-prototype-names-reject-locally, tools/json-stringify-tools) pass on native-host before and after. Files: crates/runtime/code-mode/src/code_mode/description.rs.

- fix(code-mode): `LocalCells` lists and dispatches nested tools as the tool host's registry does (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 Code Mode conformance track: tools-dedupe). `LocalTools` (local.rs), which nanocode-ts and every host on `LocalCells` run, differed from the registry (registry.rs `first_normalized_definitions`, `host_owned_name`, `nested_definition`, `execute_nested`) in five ways, and each now follows the registry: (1) tools whose names normalize to one Code Mode name (`a-b`, `a_b`, `a.b`) were all listed, so `ALL_TOOLS` held two `a_b` entries and `tools.a_b` called the last one (bootstrap.js overwrote the facade); only the first per normalized name is listed and `tools.a_b` calls it; (2) a call by raw name (`tools["a.b"]`) ran the last tool of that name (`find` searched from the end) and now runs the first, as the registry's `extend` keeps the first tool of a name; (3) host tools named `exec` or `wait` were listed and ran; they are left out of the catalog and a call to them is `TOOL_NOT_AVAILABLE` (`host_owned_name` moves to `nanocode_code_mode::embedded` and the tool host's two copies use it); (4) a `ToolSearch` definition was dropped from the catalog and a call to `tool_search` failed with `unsupported nested tool call: tool_search`; it is offered as the function `tool_search`, as `nested_definition` does, so `tools.tool_search()` sends `{}` like any function tool (the audit's "tool_search gets no `{}` default" held for neither host: the registry turns a ToolSearch into a function before bootstrap.js sees it, so no `tool_search` kind ever reached a cell); (5) with hands routed, a call to a name nothing lists whose `hand` is not a string failed with "`hand` must be the name of an attached hand; nothing was dispatched"; it is `TOOL_NOT_AVAILABLE`, as the registry checks `lists` and `routes_to_hand` before `take_hand`, while a listed tool given a non-string `hand` still gets the hand refusal. nanocode-ts refuses catalogs with colliding or reserved names when a session opens ("tool names `a-b` and `a_b` both normalize to Code Mode name `a_b`", "tool name `exec` is reserved by the Code Mode host"), so (1) to (3) reach it only through other embedders, but (5) changes what its cells see, since its sessions route hands (cells run under the hand `local`). Measured on dev-georgios with output/cm-conf (case changes listed in the track's notes), 1072097ac against this branch: native-host (`native/target/release/run --cases cases/tools.jsonl --backend both`) tools/duplicate-normalized-name-first-wins fail (`2`, `underscore`, tool `a_b` called) to pass, tools/duplicate-normalized-raw-name-via-bracket (new) fail to pass, tools/host-owned-names-not-nested (new) fail (`ALL_TOOLS` held exec and wait, both ran) to pass, on claude and codex; tools.jsonl 77 to 80 of 84 per backend, the other 4 being the crash cases of the durability lane; the full suite on native-host changes no other case's result; ts-node (`ts/run.ts --cases cases/tools.jsonl --backend claude`, nanocode-ts 2aad477's wasm built over each SDK) tools/missing-tool-non-string-hand-is-not-available (new) fail (`undefined:phone_only` with the hand refusal) to pass and no other case changes. output/tools-dedupe-check (`LocalCells` given a-b, a_b, exec, wait, a ToolSearch and an empty-named tool, with and without hands): before `ALL_TOOLS` `["a_b","a_b","exec","wait",""]`, `tools.a_b` ran a_b, `tools.tool_search()` rejected, exec and wait ran, `phone_only({hand: 5})` got the hand refusal; after `["a_b","tool_search",""]`, `tools.a_b` runs a-b, `tools.tool_search()` gets `{}`, exec and wait are `TOOL_NOT_AVAILABLE`, `phone_only({hand: 5})` is `TOOL_NOT_AVAILABLE` and `a_b({hand: 5})` still gets the hand refusal. Files: crates/runtime/code-mode/src/code_mode/local.rs, crates/runtime/code-mode/src/embedded/mod.rs, crates/runtime/tool-host/src/runtime/mod.rs, crates/runtime/tool-host/src/selection.rs.

- fix(code-mode): one function turns a tool name into its Code Mode name, and an empty name stays empty (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 Code Mode conformance track: tools-dedupe). `code_mode_description::normalize_identifier` replaces each character that cannot stand at its place in a JavaScript identifier with `_` and no longer turns an empty result into `_`; `LocalCells`' catalog uses it instead of its own copy (`identifier` in local.rs) and the tool host's `normalize_public_tool_name` calls it, so `ALL_TOOLS`, `tools`, the registry's normalized names and `exec`'s description name every tool the same way. Before, the description of a host whose first nested tool had an empty name showed `tools._(...)`, a `### `_` (``)` heading and a `_(args: …)` declaration, while `ALL_TOOLS` and `tools` held `""` and no cell had a `tools._`. The registry refuses an empty name when it builds (`ToolsBuildError::EmptyName`) and nanocode-ts refuses it when a session opens ("tool name must not be empty"), so only an embedder that hands `LocalCells` such a tool gets here, and both places now say `tools[""]`'s name, `""`. `schema_types.rs` quotes an empty property name explicitly, which it did before only because `""` became `_`. Checked on dev-georgios: output/tools-dedupe-check (`LocalCells` and `exec_description` over a function tool named `""`, built against 1072097ac and against this change): the description's example `tools._(...)` and heading `### `_` (``)` before, `tools.(...)` and `### ``` after; `ALL_TOOLS` `[""]`, `tools[""]({})` dispatching to it and the registry's `normalize_public_tool_name("")` = `""` before and after; output/cm-conf case tools/empty-name-catalogued-as-empty (new, native-host only, since nanocode-ts refuses the catalog at open) passes before and after on claude and codex. Files: crates/runtime/code-mode/src/code_mode/description.rs, crates/runtime/code-mode/src/code_mode/schema_types.rs, crates/runtime/code-mode/src/code_mode/local.rs, crates/runtime/tool-host/src/selection.rs.

- fix(code-mode): exec's description says what happens to unawaited work when a cell ends (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 Code Mode conformance track: description). "the isolate's lifetime ends and unawaited promises are silently discarded" was wrong three ways: an unhandled rejection fails the script ("Unhandled promise rejection: …", async/unhandled-rejection-at-end-fails), unawaited microtask-only chains still run to their end before the cell settles (async/unawaited-microtask-chain-completes), and an unawaited nested call is reported as abandoned with an unknown outcome (async/unawaited-call-abandoned-notice). Only work still waiting on a timer or a nested call is discarded (async/unawaited-timer-promise-discarded). The full and compact descriptions now say exactly that; behavior is unchanged, and those cases pass on native-host before and after. Files: crates/runtime/code-mode/src/code_mode/description.rs.

- fix(code-mode): the exec pragma reads `yield_time_ms` and `max_output_tokens` as Claude's exec arguments and `wait` do, and a token budget past `usize` is the same budget on wasm32 (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 Code Mode conformance track: wait and pragma arguments). Since 2026-11-12 the exec arguments and `wait` read a numeric string or a whole float as the non-negative safe integer it spells (`spec::integer_value`), but the pragma kept serde's plain `u64`/`usize`, so Codex's `// @exec: {"yield_time_ms": "100"}` failed while the same value as a Claude argument ran; and `max_output_tokens` was a `usize`, so on wasm32 (nanocode-ts) a safe integer above 2^32-1 failed serde with the generic two-field message instead of running. Now each pragma field goes through `integer_value` (null still means the default), a bad one fails with "exec pragma field `yield_time_ms` must be a non-negative safe integer, got -1", and `ExecPragma` is gone. Token budgets (`max_output_tokens`, wait's `max_tokens`) convert with `token_budget`, which maps a value above `usize::MAX` to `usize::MAX`: `truncate_content` already treats `usize::MAX` as no budget and no output a 32-bit host holds can exceed it, so the larger budget truncates exactly as much (nothing), where `max_tokens` answered "N is out of range" on wasm32 only. `wait`'s own parsing is unchanged: values/wait-yield-null and values/wait-yield-u64-max expected upstream Codex's `u64` parse recorded in native-behavior.json, which the 2026-11-12 contract replaced, so those cases now expect the safe-integer refusal. Measured with output/cm-conf: async/pragma-numeric-string (now expecting the cell to run), async/pragma-negative and async/pragma-fraction (the per-field message) fail on native-host claude and codex and ts-node claude before, pass after; async/pragma-unsafe-max-output and output/max-output-tokens-safe-maximum (budget 2^53-1) fail on ts-node before (wasm32 usize) and pass after; output/max-output-tokens-numeric-string (formerly -string-rejected, now expecting the cell to run), output/max-output-tokens-negative-rejected and output/max-output-tokens-unsafe-rejected (the per-field message) fail on native-host claude and codex before and pass after; the 26 pragma cases × 2 on native-host: 46/52 before, 52/52 after. Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-code-mode-engine -p nanocode-code-mode` natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --no-deps -p nanocode-code-mode-engine -p nanocode-code-mode -- -D warnings` natively and for wasm32, all clean; output/cm-conf's native runner (`run --cases <162 exit/wait/pragma/terminate/yield/unawaited cases> --backend both`) against master and this branch, and `ts/run.ts --backend claude` against nanocode-ts built from each (ts-node's Codex column fails every case with "no exec or wait step produced a result" on both builds, a runner problem outside this change). Files: crates/runtime/code-mode/src/code_mode/mod.rs.

- fix(code-mode): a terminated cell names the nested calls it abandoned (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 Code Mode conformance track: terminate). `CellUpdate::Terminated` built "Script terminated" from the buffered output alone and dropped `buffered.abandoned` and the calls still running, while Completed and ScriptFailed append `abandoned_calls`; so after `wait` with `terminate: true`, or a turn interrupt, the model was never told that a call it made may or may not have taken effect, against the exec description's "an `outcome: unknown` receipt is not permission to retry it" and the 2026-11-12 entry on abandoned calls. Now the terminated result ends with "Nested calls that had not returned when the script was terminated were abandoned: 1 slow. Whether each took effect is unknown. Check what each did before calling it again.", and a turn teardown's `cell_terminated` text carries it too. Measured with output/cm-conf: async/terminate-with-call-in-flight and async/yield-reports-running-call (both expecting the notice) fail on native-host claude and codex and ts-node claude before, pass after; the 19 terminate cases × 2 on native-host: 34/38 before, 38/38 after. async/terminate-finished-cell-returns-result now runs a second 300 ms cell before its terminate, since on the loaded build host the terminate could arrive before the cell's last statement and return "Script terminated" with the same output (it passed on master and failed once on this branch for that reason; the code path it covers is unchanged). Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-code-mode-engine -p nanocode-code-mode` natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --no-deps -p nanocode-code-mode-engine -p nanocode-code-mode -- -D warnings` natively and for wasm32, all clean; output/cm-conf's native runner (`run --cases <162 exit/wait/pragma/terminate/yield/unawaited cases> --backend both`) against master and this branch, and `ts/run.ts --backend claude` against nanocode-ts built from each (ts-node's Codex column fails every case with "no exec or wait step produced a result" on both builds, a runner problem outside this change). Files: crates/runtime/code-mode/src/code_mode/mod.rs.

- fix(code-mode): `exec` and `wait` read the updates a cell already queued before they yield (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 Code Mode conformance track: wait yield 0). `observe_updates` disabled its `updates.recv()` branch once the yield deadline had passed and returned on the yield timer, so `wait` with `yield_time_ms: 0` answered "Script running" with no output even for a cell that had finished long before, contradicting the wait description ("If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result"); the next wait then had to fetch it. Now a passed deadline, and the yield timer firing, take the path a preemption already took: count the updates and replayed updates queued at that moment, read exactly those (a Completed, failure or termination among them ends the call as usual) and then yield. Bounding the read to what was queued keeps a cell that prints faster than the observer drains from holding the call open. Measured with output/cm-conf: async/wait-yield-zero-on-finished-cell fails on native-host claude and codex and on ts-node claude before, passes after (3 of 3 repeated native runs); the case now runs a second 300 ms cell between the exec and the wait so the first cell has surely finished on a loaded host. async/exec-yield-zero-yields-at-once now yields a cell waiting on a timer (it asserted that a cell printing `x` and finishing yields anyway, the behavior fixed here) and passes on both builds. Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-code-mode-engine -p nanocode-code-mode` natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --no-deps -p nanocode-code-mode-engine -p nanocode-code-mode -- -D warnings` natively and for wasm32, all clean; output/cm-conf's native runner (`run --cases <162 exit/wait/pragma/terminate/yield/unawaited cases> --backend both`) against master and this branch, and `ts/run.ts --backend claude` against nanocode-ts built from each (ts-node's Codex column fails every case with "no exec or wait step produced a result" on both builds, a runner problem outside this change). Files: crates/runtime/code-mode/src/code_mode/mod.rs.

- fix(code-mode): `exit()` ends the cell through the host instead of throwing a private Symbol (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 Code Mode conformance track: exit). bootstrap.js's `exit` was `throw EXIT`, so `try { exit() } catch {}` swallowed it and the script went on (`caught`, then `after`), and any `finally` ran, while the exec description says it "Immediately ends the current script". Now `exit()` calls a new sync host function `__nanocodeExit` with the cell's terminal result (the same `terminal()` JSON a finished cell returns, so stores written so far persist as before); `ExecutionState` keeps it, and `Machine::run` checks for it after answering the host call, aborts the djs call (`Instance::abort`, which leaves the VM idle so the instance is recycled as after any cell) and sends that terminal through the same replay check a finished script gets (`ended`). No JavaScript runs after the call, so no `catch` or `finally` sees it, from the top level, a function, a `then` callback or a timer alike; the Symbol and its special cases in `uncaught` and `finish` are gone. nanocode-ts runs the same engine compiled for wasm32, and its prelude's `process.exit` calls the cell's `exit`, so both hosts change together. The description now says so ("like an early return from the top level, except that no enclosing `catch` or `finally` block runs"; the compact form "at once, running no `catch` or `finally`"). Measured with output/cm-conf: async/exit-inside-try-catch and output/exit-caught-by-try (now expecting nothing after `exit()`) fail on native-host claude and codex and on ts-node claude before, pass after; all 16 exit cases × 2 backends on native-host: 28/32 before, 32/32 after. Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-code-mode-engine -p nanocode-code-mode` natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --no-deps -p nanocode-code-mode-engine -p nanocode-code-mode -- -D warnings` natively and for wasm32, all clean; output/cm-conf's native runner (`run --cases <162 exit/wait/pragma/terminate/yield/unawaited cases> --backend both`) against master and this branch, and `ts/run.ts --backend claude` against nanocode-ts built from each (ts-node's Codex column fails every case with "no exec or wait step produced a result" on both builds, a runner problem outside this change). Files: crates/runtime/code-mode-engine/src/{bootstrap.js,cell.rs,host.rs}, crates/runtime/code-mode/src/code_mode/description.rs.

- fix(codex): `codex_tools::host_tools` registers write_stdin only for a shell that keeps sessions, `ShellExecutor::keeps_sessions` (default true) (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 Code Mode conformance track: Claude nested tools). nanocode-ts's host shell runs every command to its end and never returns a `session_id`, so its write_stdin could only fail (`session N is not running: this host's commands finish before exec_command returns`) while the catalog offered it; a shell that answers `false` now gets no write_stdin, and a call is refused locally as a missing nested tool (`TOOL_NOT_AVAILABLE`), as the exec description says of any tool absent from the catalog. Native shells (`ShellSessions`) keep the default and the tool. Measured with output/cm-conf, nanocode-ts 2aad477 built against 1072097ac and against this branch with its HostShell answering `false`: toolsets/codex/ts-write-stdin-refused (now: write_stdin absent from ALL_TOOLS and refused with TOOL_NOT_AVAILABLE) fail to pass on ts-node/codex; native-cli/codex toolsets 39 of 40 pass (the one failure, real-view-image, is a grader expectation outside this change), with write-stdin-present-native and real-write-stdin-session passing. `cargo clippy --offline --locked --no-deps --lib -p nanocode-process-contracts -p nanocode-backend-codex -- -D warnings`, natively and for wasm32, passes. Files: crates/core/process/src/lib.rs, crates/backends/codex/src/builtin_tools/host.rs.

- fix(claude): TaskOutput has one definition, `HostTool::definition` (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 Code Mode conformance track: Claude nested tools). The SDK described TaskOutput twice: `ClaudeHostTools` (the native builder's `host_tools`) used a schemars schema of `TaskOutputRequest` with no `timeout` maximum, and `host_tools` (nanocode-ts's Claude workspace tools) an explicit schema with `maximum: 300000` and another description, which is the only one any host reaches. Both now come from `HostTool::definition`: the explicit schema (task_id, block default true, timeout 0 to `MAX_TASK_OUTPUT_TIMEOUT_MS` = 300,000, the bound `host_tools` already enforced, default 30,000) with the host-owned description, and `ClaudeHostTools::execute` refuses a larger timeout as `host_tools` does, so the advertised schema is the enforced one. TaskOutput stays a host extension: native Claude sessions get no TaskOutput because their background commands report their end as session notices in the exec or wait result (claude_bash.rs `JobNotices`), while nanocode-ts's host shell cannot notify and says to poll with TaskOutput; toolsets/claude/taskoutput-absent-native and taskoutput-present-ts keep that split. The same holds for WebSearch: nanocode-ts adds `claude::web_search_tool` when its `web_search` config is on, and native Code Mode has none, since a native Claude selection has no switch for it (`without_defaults` clears the tool-host `web_search` flag, which only the Codex built-ins read) and turning it on would add a paid server-side search to every embedder's Claude sessions. Measured: toolsets/claude/schema-taskoutput-host and real-bash-background-taskoutput-host pass on ts-node/claude before and after (`node ts/run.ts --cases cases/toolsets.jsonl --backend both`, nanocode-ts 2aad477 built against 1072097ac and against this branch). `cargo clippy --offline --locked --no-deps --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude-tools -p nanocode-backend-claude -- -D warnings`, natively and for wasm32, passes. Files: crates/backends/claude/tools/src/tools/host.rs, crates/backends/claude/src/host_tools.rs.

- fix(claude): a nested Read, Edit, Write or TaskStop error is the bare message, and nanocode-ts's host file and task tools answer with the Claude Code 2.1.300 texts the native tools give (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 Code Mode conformance track: Claude nested tools). Claude Code wraps a failed tool_result in `<tool_use_error>…</tool_use_error>`; native `ClaudeFileTool` wrapped every `Err` that way and "use Claude Code 2.1.300's texts" above put the wrapper inside TaskStop's `Missing required parameter: task_id` and `No task found with ID: <id>`, also for calls from exec cells, where the text becomes a JavaScript `Error` message rather than a tool_result, while nanocode-ts's `HostFileTool` and `HostTaskTool` never wrap, so the same cell saw different text per host. Now a nested call (call ID with `/code-`, the marker `ClaudeBash` uses) gets the bare message: `ClaudeFileTool` wraps only a direct call's `Err`, and `TaskStopTool` strips the wrapper from a nested call's; direct calls and the texts themselves are unchanged. The host tools still had the texts from before that change: `HostFileTool` said `path: <path> does not exist` for Read (text and image) and Edit of a missing file, refused an Edit with an empty `old_string` of a missing file, and passed on the host's own error for a directory (nanocode-ts: `/workspace/<dir>: Is a directory`), and `HostTaskTool` said `task_id or its deprecated shell_id alias must be a string` and `unknown task_id in this session`. They now say `File does not exist. Note: your current working directory is <workspace>.` (without `Did you mean`, as `FileHost` lists no directories), create the file, answer `EISDIR: illegal operation on a directory, read '<path>'` for Read and `Error calling tool (Edit): EISDIR: illegal operation on a directory, read` for Edit when the host's read error is a directory one (starts with `EISDIR`, or ends with `: Is a directory` or names os error 21; `FileHost::read` has no directory result), and say `Missing required parameter: task_id` and `No task found with ID: <id>` as `TaskStopTool` does. Measured with output/cm-conf toolsets.jsonl, claude backend, on the release CLI and the nanocode-ts wasm module of this branch at 57a3ab89d: native-cli 59 of 59 and ts-node 61 of 61 Claude toolsets cases pass, including real-read-missing-native/-host and real-edit-missing (now `File does not exist. Note: …`), real-taskstop-unknown-rejects (`No task found with ID: nope`) and the new real-taskstop-missing-id-rejects, real-read-directory-rejects (ts-node said `/workspace/toolsets-dir: Is a directory` before), real-edit-directory-rejects, real-read-binary-rejects and real-edit-create-missing, each with the same text on both hosts and no `<tool_use_error>`. `cargo clippy --offline --locked --no-deps --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude -p nanocode-backend-claude-tools -- -D warnings`, natively and for wasm32, passes. Files: crates/backends/claude/src/{claude_files.rs,claude_bash.rs,host_tools.rs}.

- fix(claude): a nested `tools.Bash` call resolves with its structured result on a nonzero exit; only a direct call answers in Claude Code's text with `is_error` (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 Code Mode conformance track: Claude nested tools). The Claude Code text change above ("Bash keeps its working directory between calls and answers in Claude Code's text") sent every finished command through `rendered()`, which returns `ToolOutput::error` for an exit code other than 0, and that covered calls from exec cells too: the structured result was still attached, but the failed output made the cell's promise reject, so `try { const r = await tools.Bash({ command: "printf o; exit 3" }) } catch (e) {}` landed in `catch` with `e.exit_code` 3. prompts/code_mode.md says `tools.Bash` resolves to `{ stdout, stderr, exit_code }` and that cells test `result.exit_code`, the nested output schema has `exit_code` integer|null, and nanocode-ts's `HostBashTool` already resolved, so native was the outlier. `rendered()` already takes whether the call is direct (its call ID lacks `/code-`, the marker `ClaudeBash` uses for the nested timeout and stream budget; added by the direct Bash output entry below), and its last arm, reached only by a nested call with a nonzero exit, now returns the same text as a success instead of `ToolOutput::error`; the direct call's text, `is_error` and working-directory handling are unchanged. Measured with output/cm-conf (`node cli/run.ts --nanocode <bin> --cases cases/toolsets.jsonl --backend both`), the release CLI of 1072097ac against this branch: toolsets/claude/real-bash-nonzero-exit-resolves on native-cli/claude printed `rejected 3` before and `resolved 3 o` after; ts-node/claude passed before and after (nanocode-ts does not run `BashTool`); native-host runs only mock tools and has no case for it. `cargo clippy --offline --locked --no-deps --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude -- -D warnings`, natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, passes. Files: crates/backends/claude/src/claude_bash.rs.

- deps(alloc): `nc` and `nanocode-python` allocate with `nanocode_sys::alloc::Heap`, and mimalloc, libmimalloc-sys, cc, find-msvc-tools and nanocode's own shlex leave (2026-11-14, plan-25). `cargo metadata --offline` resolves 146 to 141 packages (registry packages 22 to 18); nothing else in the tree used cc, so shlex (its only user) and crates/core/shlex go too, and `nc` now builds with no C compiler (nanocode-python-cli still compiles python-capi's markupsafe extension with one). The release `nanocode` is 129,656 bytes smaller (72,843,016 to 72,713,360). Gate (DECISIONS 2026-11-10 and 2026-11-12 mimalloc entries): bench/cli on the cli-bench branch, `suite.mjs --parts=oneshot,firstframe --rounds=4`, `--parts=tools --steps=10 --toolrounds=2` and `--parts=fleet --fleet=8,32 --fleetrounds=1`, mimalloc and ours alternated in 6 batches, release builds of the same tree, this 5-core Linux Hand at load 7.4, medians (n=24/24/12/6/6), mimalloc -> ours: one-shot CPU 13.08 -> 13.29 ms (+1.6%), peak RSS 38.25 -> 37.62 MB; first frame CPU 17.76 -> 17.24 ms, RSS 36.18 -> 35.93 MB, anonymous 5.67 -> 5.40 MB; 10-step tool turn 4.66 -> 4.64 ms CPU a step, peak RSS 45.47 -> 45.73 MB (+0.6%); fleet of 8 46.48 vs 45.92 ms CPU per agent (+1.2%), RSS 37.54 -> 37.05 MB per agent; fleet of 32 41.91 -> 38.56 ms, 37.63 -> 36.97 MB. Earlier rounds at load 8-15 agreed within their noise (one-shot +0.9% to +4%, first frame -1% to -12%, tools -4% to +1%, RSS lower in every part). The agent-scale run: 8 concurrent Tokio tasks on 4 workers, each running 1,500 Code Mode cells (400 objects built, stringified and parsed in djs) and round-tripping a transcript item through serde_json, freed on another task, 7 interleaved rounds at load 13, system / mimalloc / ours: CPU 7.36 / 7.65 / 7.51 s, max RSS 13.7 / 18.5 / 18.0 MB. These runs predate one change in the previous commit (a large block resizes in place only while it stays above 256 KiB), which no part of these runs exercises measurably. The 20,000-agent swarm (output/durability-ledger) lives on dev-georgios and was not rerun here. Files: Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, bin/nanocode/{Cargo.toml,src/main.rs}, bin/nanocode-python/{Cargo.toml,src/main.rs}, crates/core/shlex (deleted), DEPENDENCIES.md.
- feat(sys): `nanocode_sys::alloc`, nanocode's own global allocator, not installed by this commit, and an allocator scenario in nanocode-sim (2026-11-14, plan-25: replace mimalloc with our own allocator). `Heap` implements `GlobalAlloc`; on unix it is a size-class allocator in crates/core/sys/src/alloc (class.rs, segment.rs, local.rs, os.rs), elsewhere it forwards to `std::alloc::System` (Windows and wasm32 keep the system allocator; wasm32 builds the module for parity and no binary installs it there). Design, after mimalloc's published one: 4 MiB segments aligned to their size so a block finds its segment by masking its address, 64 KiB slices, 52 classes up to 256 KiB (16-byte steps to 128 B, then 4 per doubling; a class's page spans enough slices for at least 8 blocks, so 32 KiB blocks take 4 slices), one heap per thread in a `const` thread_local with no destructor, owner-only free lists and a push-only atomic `thread_free` list per page that the owner takes with one swap (no ABA, no locks), larger blocks mapped directly with a lock-free 16-slot cache of at most 8 MiB, `mremap` growth in place on Linux, and fresh large mappings skip `alloc_zeroed`'s memset. A thread's exit is seen through a pthread key destructor (never a thread_local `Drop`): it collects its pages, returns empty segments to a 16-slot purged cache and puts the rest on a 1,024-slot lock-free abandoned list, from which a thread that needs a new segment adopts one. Empty pages go back to their segment; free slices are purged with `madvise` (`MADV_DONTNEED`, `MADV_FREE_REUSABLE` on Apple) once a heap holds more than 64 dirty free slices (4 MiB), and heap-wide collection of remote frees runs after `max(32, live pages / 4)` new pages, so no clock is read. Every bound is a named constant; an invariant broken inside the allocator writes its name to stderr and aborts (a `GlobalAlloc` must not unwind). Bounds reached: when the abandoned list is full a dying thread's segment stays owned by the dead heap and is not reused; when `pthread_key_create` fails a thread's exit is not seen, so its segments are not reused. `Local` drives one heap explicitly (`allocate`, `deallocate`, `reallocate` with an owned `Allocation`, `abandon`, `adopt_abandoned`, `census`) for the simulator. nanocode-sim gains `--scenario alloc`: four simulated threads interleave allocations (1 B to 2 MiB, alignments up to 1 MiB), local and cross-thread frees, reallocations, thread exits and adoption by seed, with every block's bytes written and checked; invariants: no live block overlaps another (handed out twice), contents survive, and the heaps' census of used small blocks equals the simulation's live count (every free is reusable), with `census` asserting each page's used, free and uncarved blocks add up to its capacity and every page is queued once. Mutations caught: overstate_size, forget_free, scribble (cfo.sh rows added). Checked: `nanocode-sim --tidy` clean; `bin/nanocode-sim/sweep.sh 0 2000 3 --scenario alloc` passed 2,000 seeds with 0 panics (each about 1,000 operations, 30,000 cross-thread frees and 4,000 thread exits per 100 seeds); `--seeds 5000..5200 --twice` identical digests; the three mutations are first caught at seeds 9002 (overstate_size, handed out twice), 9000 (forget_free, census) and 9000 (scribble, contents). The scenario found one inconsistency before landing: a large block shrunk in place below 256 KiB stayed in its mapping while its layout now named a small class, so a large block now resizes in place only while it stays above the small classes. Measured (output/alloc-ab from plan-25, 7 interleaved rounds, this 5-core Linux Hand at load 8.8, medians, system / mimalloc / ours): transcript JSON with cross-thread frees CPU 1.260 / 0.647 / 0.701 s, max RSS 43.8 / 52.5 / 49.0 MB; mixed-size churn 1.588 / 1.285 / 1.268 s, RSS 84.2 / 132.5 / 123.8 MB; process start 2.0 / 2.6 / 2.2 ms, 11.7 MB for all three. The dirty-slice bound was chosen there: 128 slices gave json RSS 54.8-56.0 MB, 32 gave 39.6 MB but churn +6% CPU from madvise, 64 is between. A stress harness (8 threads x 150,000 random alloc/realloc/free over 1 B-3 MiB and alignments to 2 MiB, 25% freed on another thread, every byte pattern checked, then 3,000 short-lived threads) ran clean three times. Files: crates/core/sys/src/lib.rs, crates/core/sys/src/alloc/*, bin/nanocode-sim/src/{main.rs,alloc.rs}, bin/nanocode-sim/cfo.sh.
- fix(psh): `env -i CMD` gives CMD an empty environment; the shell no longer adds `_` (2026-11-14, e2e bug log BUG 18, agent 30). The env utility runs its command through `UtilCtx::spawn`, whose `run_wrapped` ran an external like any command the shell runs, and `run_external_with` adds `_=<program>` to every child but one `exec` runs, so `env -i /usr/bin/env` printed `_=/usr/bin/env` and `env -i PATH=/usr/bin /usr/bin/env` printed two lines (bash runs coreutils env, which clears what bash passed it). `ExtOpts::cleared`, set from `SpawnEnv::clear`, now skips adding `_`; an explicit `env -i _=x CMD` still passes it, and `env CMD` without -i is unchanged. The sim does not run psh, so no scenario. Checks: `nanocode psh-shell -c 'env -i /usr/bin/env'` prints nothing, `env -i PATH=/usr/bin /usr/bin/env` one line, `env -i FOO=1 printenv` only FOO=1, `env -i _=x /usr/bin/env` `_=x`.
- fix(tui): bare `/runner` lists runners, and `/pass` always answers (2026-11-14, e2e bug log BUG 16, agent 30). `shlex_words` returned `None` both for an unterminated quote and for no words, and `/runner` read every `None` as "unterminated quote in /runner command"; it now returns `Some(vec![])` for an empty argument, so bare `/runner` is `/runner list`, and the `$EDITOR` caller refuses an empty command itself. `/pass` handed its argument to the MPP identity and said nothing; `Identity::answer` now returns the reply to show: with no email pass waiting (its inbox is not lent out) it says so and, for an address, that the next pass goes there; a decline of a waiting pass is confirmed; an address or code for a waiting pass is answered by that flow's own notices. `ModelClients::answer` takes `Fn(&str) -> Option<String>`. The sim does not drive the TUI, so no scenario. Checks: in tmux, `/runner` shows "no runners or listeners"; `/pass` shows "pass: no email pass is waiting; /pass <email> sets the address the next one goes to"; `/pass foo@bar.com` shows "pass: no email pass is waiting; the next one goes to foo@bar.com".
- fix(cli): an unwritable nanocode home no longer stops every command at startup, and the errors name the path (2026-11-14, e2e bug log BUG 13, agent 30). Telemetry opened its local files (`log/otel/<run>/` and, for the TUI with a log filter, `log/nanocode.log`) before anything else, and a failure was fatal with "failed to start telemetry: failed to open tracing output: Permission denied", naming no path, so `--ephemeral` (which writes nothing else) and a CI container with a read-only or missing HOME could not run one exec. `ObservabilityError::LocalFile(path, error)` now carries the path ("cannot write PATH: ..."); when that path is under the home, the CLI warns once ("running without local logs and telemetry: cannot write PATH: ...; set --home or NANOCODE_HOME to a writable directory to keep them") and installs telemetry without local files. An explicit `--log-file` elsewhere stays fatal. The JSONL store's `open_home` errors name the home too ("cannot open the session store in HOME: Permission denied"). The sim does not start the CLI, so no scenario. Checks: `exec --ephemeral` with `--home` a regular file, a mode 500 directory, or `HOME=/nonexistent` prints PONG, rc 0 (all failed before); without `--ephemeral` the store error names the home.
- fix(tui): a `!command` runs in psh through nanocode-process like the Bash tool, returns when the shell exits, streams its output, and esc esc kills it (2026-11-14, e2e bug log BUG 9, agent 30). `run_shell` ran `sh -c` with tokio's `output()`, which used /bin/sh (dash on many Linux hosts, so `${HOME:0:5}` was a bad substitution), read both pipes to EOF (a background job holding them kept the cell spinning: `(sleep 25 &); echo bg-done` took 25 s), collected stdout and stderr apart and showed them only at the end, and had no cancel handle. It now calls `nanocode_process::run_bash` (psh, the process group killed on drop, done when the shell exits) with an `OutputSink` that sends each chunk as `AppEvent::ShellOutput`; the app decodes UTF-8 across chunk ends and appends to the cell, keeping at most `SHELL_OUTPUT_BYTES` (1 MiB, what a transcript cell holds; the rest is counted and noted) and bounding the run by `SHELL_TIMEOUT` (2 h, the Bash tool's background maximum). The app keeps a `Shell` per running command with its task's `AbortHandle`; running shells count as busy, so esc esc interrupts them (the cell says "interrupted after Ns; its process group was killed") along with any turn. `nanocode_process` re-exports `OutputSink`. The sim does not drive the TUI, so no scenario. Checks: in tmux, `!echo ${HOME:0:5}` prints /home; `!(sleep 25 &); echo bg-done` finishes in 44 ms; `!echo out; echo err >&2; echo out2` keeps the order; a loop printing tick1..8 a second apart shows ticks as they come, and esc esc at 3.9 s stops it with no further output.
- fix(runners): `--runner-connect` reports its connection failures and fails fast on a rejected credential instead of staying silent or hanging (2026-11-14, e2e bug log BUG 6, agent 30). `RunnerPool::keep_connected` spawned its supervisor and returned at once, so startup never saw the first attempt: a wrong token or refused address ran on silently in alongside mode (rc 0, no warning), and in replace mode a rejected token stopped the supervisor while the pool kept waiting for a replacement hand, so the turn waited forever with no output. `keep_connected` now returns `Started`, a watch the supervisor answers once with its first outcome: connected or a transient failure (reported, then retried with backoff as before) answers `Ok`, a permanent one (authentication, catalog) answers its error and, in replace mode, stops awaiting a replacement. `RunnerAgents::activate` adds it to the startup receipts, so `initialize_runners` fails with it. The CLI subscribes to runner events before initializing: a startup failure is returned naming the runner ("runner NAME: attachment authentication failed: runner rejected the bearer credential", rc 1); exec prints later failures to stderr ("nanocode: runner NAME: ... Connection refused"), and the TUI forwards that same receiver, so the failures raised while it started are not lost. A replace-mode runner whose address refuses keeps retrying, as the hand may start later, now with the failure printed. The sim has no runner attachments, so no scenario. Checks: with `nanocode hand --listen 127.0.0.1:28947 --token good`, exec with `--runner-token bad` exits 1 at once with that message in both modes (alongside was rc 0, replace hung); a refused address prints the failure and proceeds in alongside mode; the good token runs the turn on the hand, rc 0.
- fix(python): nanocode-python streams stdin, stdout and stderr instead of reading all of stdin first and printing only at exit (2026-11-14, e2e bug log BUG 5, agent 30). Two layers buffered: `serve` read stdin to its end and wrote the run's collected `Ran::stdout`/`stderr` after the script finished, and the psh utility (bin/nanocode/src/python.rs) also read all of stdin before spawning the program and collected its pipes until exit. So `yes | python3 -c 'print(input())'` never ended, output did not stream, and stderr always came after stdout. `Run` now carries `stdio: Stdio`, `Held(Vec<u8>)` for the in-process utility and nanocode-shell (unchanged behaviour) or `Process` for `serve`, where `_host.input` reads the process's stdin one `read` at a time (or to its end for `-`) and `_host.output` writes each write through to the process's stdout or stderr and flushes; the output limit counts bytes written in both modes (`State::written`). The utility forwards the child's stdout and stderr to `SyncCtx::writer` from one thread each as chunks arrive, feeds stdin through a writer thread over a bounded channel (`STDIN_CHUNKS_IN_FLIGHT` = 1 chunk of `PIPE_CAPACITY_BYTES`, Linux's default pipe capacity, pipe(7)), stops feeding when the child exits, and polls the cancel flag at `CANCEL_POLL` while handing a chunk over or waiting. The sim does not run psh utilities, so no scenario. Checks: `PSH_UTILS_FORCE=python3 nanocode psh-shell -c 'yes | python3 -c "import sys; print(sys.stdin.readline().strip())"'` prints y at once, rc 0 (it hung before); a script printing to stdout and stderr with 1 s sleeps shows each line 1 s apart in order; `printf 'a\nb\n' | ... python3 -c 'print(sys.stdin.read().upper())'`, `python3 -` from stdin, and `seq 3 | python3 -c 'for l in sys.stdin: ...'` unchanged.
- fix(cli): `nanocode models` and `nanocode sessions` stop quietly when stdout closes instead of panicking (2026-11-14, e2e bug log BUG 1, agent 30). Both printed with `println!`, which panics on EPIPE because Rust ignores SIGPIPE, so `nanocode models | head -1` and `nanocode sessions --all | head -1` died with "failed printing to stdout: Broken pipe" and exit 101 (or a worker-task panic). They now write through one `StdoutLock` with `writeln!`, flush at the end, and treat `BrokenPipe` as the reader having had enough (`unless_closed`, exit 0); any other write error is reported. The lock is taken in plain functions (`print_transcript`, `print_sessions`) so the `sessions` future stays `Send` for `on_worker`, and the store is still flushed after a closed pipe. The sim cannot reach this (it drives no CLI subcommands), so no scenario. Checks: `cargo build --release -p nanocode-cli`; `nanocode models | head -1` and `nanocode sessions --all | head -1` print one line, rc 0.
- fix(claude): Messages API requests carry Claude Code 2.1.300's session identity: `metadata.user_id` = `{"device_id":…,"account_uuid":"","session_id":…}` (a JSON string, in that key order) and the `x-claude-code-session-id` header, on every request of the non-subscription wire, as the subscription wire already did (2026-11-14, ~/hill/analysis/cost-backlog.md item 4, claude-parity.md L6). Stock, captured in the parity mock (`~/wt/ci-p3/ident.py bad`, both arms against mock3.py): body `metadata: {"user_id":"{\"device_id\":\"bfe8…cacd\",\"account_uuid\":\"\",\"session_id\":\"0372d964-…\"}"}` and header `X-Claude-Code-Session-Id: 0372d964-…` on all 10 requests, device_id 64 hex, account_uuid empty without an OAuth account; stock's `EBe()` builds `{device_id: _M(), account_uuid: …||"", session_id: q()}` and `_M()` is the global config's `userID`, 32 random bytes in hex created once per install. nanocode sent neither. It matters beyond parity: Tempo's gateway takes `request.metadata?.user_id ?? wallet` as the affinity of a Messages request (tempoxyz/gateway src/Messages.ts:163, :184, :199), which `conversation()` (src/Models.ts:848) turns into Vercel's `providerOptions.gateway.sessionId` and `x-session-affinity`, so every nanocode session of one wallet with the same first two messages shared one sticky-routing key, where each stock session has its own. Now `api_body` writes `metadata` after `tools` from `SubscriptionIdentity::api_metadata` (device_id derived as the subscription wire derives it, from `install_id`, else the session), the request headers add `x-claude-code-session-id` with the bound session (`bind_subscription_session`, the agent's session id), and the CLI gives non-subscription Claude clients a per-install id (`ClaudeClient::with_install_id`) read from `$NANOCODE_HOME/install_id`, written with a new UUID on first use as stock writes `userID`; a home it cannot write still gets a fresh id for the run, as stock does. Measured with the release build: all 10 requests carry the field and the header, header = session_id, one device_id per session; two runs on one home send the same device_id with different session_ids, another home a different device_id. Parity scenarios bg, out, read, edit, par and maxtok still exit 0 with the same request counts as stock and the pinned nc runs (bg 8 = stock 8). System-role messages stay `[{"type":"text"}]`: stock sends a string except for the last message, which carries its moving cache_control marker as an array, but nanocode's API wire JSON of a history message is the same cached string its durable record stores (agent/history.rs `json`), and `Message.content` is a block list, so a string form needs its own wire encoding for no gain: the Messages API tokenizes both forms alike and the gateway flattens both to the same chat message (src/Messages.ts:922-935). Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude-client` native and `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode`, `cargo build --locked --release -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode`.
- fix(claude): the Bash tool's shell answers as `/bin/bash`, and a direct session's Bash description is Claude Code's, without the exec-cell sentence (2026-11-14, ~/hill/analysis/claude-parity.md L6). Claude Code 2.1.300 runs the user's bash, so a model saw `/bin/bash: line 1: x: command not found`, `$0` = `/bin/bash` and `$SHELL` = `/bin/bash` (exported, `declare -x SHELL="/bin/bash"`, even when its own environment has no `SHELL`), where nanocode's Bash, which runs every command in psh through `run_bash`, gave `psh: line 1:`, `psh`, an empty `$SHELL` and `declare: SHELL: not found`. The codex side got the same fix in 07ef124 (`PSH_NAME`); now `run_bash_with_environment`, the one path behind every `ForegroundExecutor` (the claude harness's Bash, direct, background and exec-cell calls, and the host adapters' Bash), sets `PSH_NAME=/bin/bash` (`nanocode_home::shell::default_shell_path`) and, when the environment has none, `SHELL=/bin/bash`, as `ShellSessions::execute` does. L6: the description carried `NESTED_TIMEOUT` ("A call from an exec cell without `timeout` waits the maximum instead, ...") in direct sessions too, which have no exec tool; `claude_bash::install` and `claude_files::selection` now take `code_mode`, `install_default_tools_with_providers` passes `!direct`, and the runner, hand and default installs keep the sentence, so Code Mode sessions are unchanged. Measured with a private copy of the parity mock (~/wt/claude-bash-p3: run3.py takes MODEL, and a new scenario shell2: an unknown command, a multi-line command with two unknown commands, a syntax error, `cd` to a missing directory, nested `bash -c` and `sh -c`, a background call read back from its output file, `printenv SHELL; declare -p SHELL; ${UNSET_Q:?...}` and a failed redirection), stock Claude Code 2.1.300 against nanocode-3638a2c and a release build of this tree (`cargo build --locked --release -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode`), tool_result texts compared exactly: shell2 2 of 10 identical before, 7 of 10 after; shell 1 of 2 before and after (the one left is `$BASH_VERSION`, psh's 5.3.9 against the host's 5.2.21). The three shell2 texts left differ in the background task's ID and output path, stock's `[exited with code 127]` line at the end of a background output file, and eval line numbers in a multi-line command: bash numbers a line of a multi-line eval text from the line where the word after `eval` ends (`/bin/bash: line 4: nosuch_two` for the second of three lines), psh from the line where `eval` starts (`line 2`). Bash description: 1,655 characters against stock's 1,406 before, byte-identical after (shell and shell2, input schema identical too); with `MODEL=claude-sonnet-4-6` (Code Mode, tools exec and wait) the request still carries the sentence. Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-process -p nanocode-backend-claude`, natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`. Files: crates/integrations/process/src/foreground.rs, crates/backends/claude/src/{claude_bash.rs,claude_files.rs,defaults.rs}.
- feat(sync): nanocode-sync's own lock-free `oneshot`, `mpsc` (bounded, unbounded, `WeakSender`, `WeakUnboundedSender`, `Permit`, `OwnedPermit`, `PermitIterator`), `Semaphore` (`acquire_many`, owned permits, `close`, `forget_permits`) and `OnceCell`, with tokio's names, methods, error types, `Display` and `Debug` text (2026-11-14, tokio replacement step 1a of plan-22). Nothing calls them yet; step 2 swaps the imports. nanocode-sys's existing `AtomicWaker` gains `wake_by_ref`, which keeps the waker registered as tokio's oneshot does, and nanocode-sys gains `queue::Queue`, a Vyukov MPSC linked queue whose one `Consumer` token is claimed once, so popping stays safe code. `oneshot` is a state byte, an `AtomicBox` for the value and two `AtomicWaker`s; it follows tokio's rules exactly, including that a value sent after `close` is handed back, that `close` and drop wake the sender's `closed()` every time until a value or the sender's drop completes the channel, and that a value sent before `close` can still be received. `mpsc` is the queue, a message counter whose low bit is the receiver's close, sender and weak counts, the receiver's `AtomicWaker` and, for bounded channels, a `Semaphore` of the capacity; the receiver ends when no message is counted and either no sender is left or the receiver closed and every reserved permit came back, as tokio's `is_idle` rule does, and `try_recv` waits out a push caught between its two stores as tokio waits out a busy slot. `Semaphore` keeps permits, waiters (FIFO by ticket in a persistent `OrdMap`) and the closed flag in one `Atom` changed by compare-and-swap: released permits go to the oldest waiter first, partly when it needs more (so `try_acquire` fails while anyone waits, as in tokio), closing leaves the queued waiters in place so a dropped or failed acquire returns what was assigned to it, and an acquire polled after `close` fails even if its permits were already granted, as tokio's does. `OnceCell` is a `OnceLock` plus a one-permit `Semaphore` closed once the value is set. Wakes go out in ticket order. Equality: output/channel-equality runs seeded op scripts (sends, try variants, polls of pending futures, drops of either side and of pending futures, closes, clones, downgrades and upgrades, reserves, queries, recv_many) for both `tokio::sync` 1.52.3 and `nanocode_sync` on a scripted single-thread executor and compares return values, `Poll` results, error `Display`/`Debug` text and which wakers were woken after every step: 0 differences over 5 seeds x 300,000 scripts for each of oneshot, bounded mpsc, unbounded mpsc, Semaphore and OnceCell. Stress (std threads, `blocking_send`/`send` and `blocking_recv`, 10M messages, per-producer sequence checked): 4P1C and 16P4C over 4 channels, bounded(64) and unbounded, no loss, duplicate or reorder. Cost, `channel-equality bench`, ns per message, three interleaved rounds against tokio on this 5-core Hand at load 9 to 10: oneshot create+send+try_recv 33 to 53 against 20 to 24 (the boxed value); unbounded same thread 15 to 19 against 16 to 38; unbounded 1P1C across threads 121 to 158 against 36 to 77; unbounded 4P1C 129 to 147 against 141 to 225; bounded(64) same thread 126 to 298 against 22 to 26; bounded(64) 1P1C 693 to 717 against 178 to 211; bounded(64) 4P1C 903 to 1,597 against 202 to 461. The bounded path pays a copy-on-write `Atom` swap (one allocation) per acquire and per release; an atomic permit fast path that drops to the `Atom` only while waiters exist comes before step 2 moves any bounded channel or semaphore onto these. Checks: `cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-sync` native and `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown` report nothing in the new files; `nanocode-sim --tidy` clean. Files: crates/core/sys/src/{waker.rs,queue.rs,lib.rs}, crates/core/sync/src/{oneshot.rs,mpsc.rs,semaphore.rs,once_cell.rs,waiters.rs,blocking.rs,lib.rs}.

- feat(python): the C API becomes a general object bridge and the regex package's C module (`regex._regex`, mrab-regex 2026.11.9) is compiled into python3: `import regex` works and passes its own test suite, 101 of 101, in python.wasm and natively (2026-11-14, Georgios: run the top compiled Python packages in plain wasm32 with a C API layer written in Rust, no Pyodide). crates/core/python-capi now holds: abi.rs, CPython 3.13's layouts (object, var object, the full type object with number, sequence and mapping methods, method, member and getset definitions, module definitions and slots, str, int, float, bytes, tuple, list, dict, slice, buffer) and protocol constants, checked against offsetof and sizeof from the headers for wasm32 and x86_64 by a probe turned into const assertions (a deliberately wrong one fails); heap.rs, PyMem_*, PyMem_Raw* and PyObject_Malloc/Calloc/Realloc/Free over Rust's allocator, each block with a header saying whether it is a plain block, a proxy of a Rust object, a pending object C is still filling (PyUnicode_New, PyBytes_FromStringAndSize(NULL), PyTuple_New, PyList_New) or an instance of a C type; bridge.rs, the exported static type objects and singletons (PyType_Type to PyCapsule_Type, _Py_NoneStruct, _Py_TrueStruct, _Py_FalseStruct, Ellipsis, NotImplemented), every PyExc_* pointer, the error indicator, and the crossing of objects: a Rust object crosses as one proxy per object (a map from its address), laid out as CPython lays it out for str, bytes, int, float, tuple, list (refreshed on each crossing), dict and slice so C macros read it, and as a bare header for the rest; a pending object becomes a Rust object the first time it crosses back; a C instance is owned by a `_capi.object` Rust object that decrefs it when dropped; proxies whose count reaches zero are freed when the outermost call into C returns; types.rs, a C static type becomes a Rust heap type (base `_capi.object`) with its methods, class and static methods, members, getsets and tp_ slots as dunders (repr, str, iter, next, hash, call, the six comparisons, getitem, len, setitem, delitem, contains, bool, init, new), weak references when tp_weaklistoffset is set, every METH_* calling convention, PyType_Ready, PyType_GenericAlloc/GenericNew, _PyObject_New(Var) and PyObject_Init(Var); module.rs, single-phase (PyModule_Create2) and multi-phase init (Py_mod_exec), module state, PyState_*, PyModule_Add* and a module named by the dotted name it was imported as (as CPython's package context does, so `regex._regex.compile.__module__` is 'regex._regex' and patterns pickle); api.rs, about 300 more functions (PyErr_*, PyObject_*, PyLong_*, PyFloat_*, PyNumber_*, PyUnicode_*, PyBytes_*, PyTuple_*, PyList_*, PyDict_* with PyDict_Next, PySlice_*, PySequence_*, PyMapping_*, PyImport_*, buffers, PyIter_Next); c/varargs.c, the variadic API in C because stable Rust cannot define C variadic functions (PyArg_ParseTuple(AndKeywords) and their Va and _SizeT forms, PyArg_UnpackTuple, Py_BuildValue, PyUnicode_FromFormat(V), PyErr_Format, PyTuple_Pack, PyObject_CallFunction/Method(ObjArgs)); include/libc gains time.h and the rest of ctype.h, and libc.rs provides the ASCII ctype functions and clock() from nanocode-platform's Instant on wasm32. crates/core/python/src/capi.rs only registers the extensions now. Wasm function-pointer casts: C extensions routinely store a function with fewer parameters than its slot's type (regex's `groupindex` getter takes only self); native ABIs ignore the extra argument, wasm's call_indirect traps ("null function or function signature mismatch"). On wasm32 build.rs reads each compiled extension object (its type, import, function and linking sections and its table-index relocations), lists every function whose address is taken with its real parameter count, compiles a wrapper TU that includes the source and adds that table, and cast.rs calls each C function pointer with the count it was defined with (padding with zeros or dropping extras); natively the table is empty and every call is the direct one. The vendored rustpython-vm's module creation no longer assumes a create slot returns a module made from a Rust definition (`__init_dict_from_def` and `__init_methods` skip a module without one). PyUnicode_Substring indexes the str's own CPython layout instead of walking code points from the start, which made every match's group O(position): regex's findall over a 240,000-character text went from 1,205 ms to 16 ms. Known limits: one interpreter per thread runs C extensions; heap-type proxies of Rust types are never freed; PyErr_CheckSignals uses vm.check_signals; a buffer of an object other than bytes is a read-only copy; C types based on builtins other than object are refused with SystemError. Checked on dev-georgios: regex's tests/test_regex.py 101/101 in python.wasm (each test in its own run) and with the native debug nanocode-python; markupsafe's earlier checks still pass. Benchmarks (best of 3 after a warm-up, ms, python.wasm against Pyodide 314.0.7 with its regex 2026.3.32 wheel, same script): regex findall 15.8 vs 16.4, sub 56.7 vs 33.5, e-mail findall 16.7 vs 15.5, split 22.5 vs 14.3, finditer 6.7 vs 2.8, total 118.3 vs 82.5; RustPython's own re on the same work 81.6 (Pyodide's re 63.5). nanocode-ts bench/python/score.ts: compiled modules 1/274 to 2/274, packages 1/18 to 2/18, C API symbols exported 5/538 to 289/538, external crates 5, limits 4/4; python.wasm 27,363,835 to 28,212,821 bytes (+848,986, most of it regex's Unicode tables). Interleaved, 5 rounds of compile, instantiate, `print(1)` and a json and re script, ms, master tree then this one: 70.8/23.8/195.6/112.5 110.3/13.2/82.2/50.4, 38.9/11.3/80.6/52.5 72.7/10.4/73.3/76.0, 53.3/9.0/66.8/72.0 52.3/22.2/109.2/83.3, 68.0/30.9/108.1/55.7 40.9/13.4/96.5/79.7, 45.3/10.2/136.4/114.5 68.9/13.3/112.8/52.5 (medians 53.3/11.3/108.1/72.0 and 68.9/13.3/96.5/76.0, shared machine under load). Commands: `cargo clippy --offline -p nanocode-python-capi -p nanocode-python --no-deps -- -D warnings` natively and for wasm32-unknown-unknown, `cargo build -p nanocode-python-cli`, `node scripts/check-dependency-boundaries.mjs` (78 crates). Files: crates/core/python-capi/{Cargo.toml,build.rs,c/varargs.c,include/libc/{ctype,time}.h,ext/regex._regex/*,src/*}, crates/core/python/src/capi.rs, crates/patches/rustpython-vm/src/builtins/module.rs, Cargo.lock.
- fix(cli): a retried model request replaces its dead partial reply and says it is retrying (2026-11-14, e2e BUG 2). When a Messages stream broke mid-reply and was retried, exec's `Printer` and the TUI's `EventMapper` kept the dead attempt's deltas and appended the retry's ("Mock reply 1 to: one Mock reply 2 to: ..."), exec printed no retry notice, and the TUI's said only "retrying model request (attempt N)". Both now read `model.attempt.retrying`: the keys streamed for that model call are dropped (both track key to call), the TUI writes the retry's first text over the dead cell, and `events::retry_notice` reads "model request failed (attempt 1 of 11), retrying in 0.6s: <error>" for both. Exec writes it to stderr, adding "the partial reply above is discarded" when text had reached a terminal; when stdout is not a terminal, exec holds each reply until its message completes (dropped on a retry), so a pipe or file gets only the reply that finished. The simulator drives the runtime, not the CLI's printers, so no scenario. Checked against agent 19's mock with a reset once mid-reply: piped stdout is exactly `Mock reply 2 to: ...` with the notice on stderr; in tmux exec shows the dead line, the notice and the retry on its own line; the TUI shows one `● Mock reply 2 ...` cell and `⚠ model request failed (attempt 1 of 11), retrying in 0.6s: ...`.

- fix(cli): use ANTHROPIC_API_KEY behind the Claude login when no endpoint is set (2026-11-14, e2e BUG 8). The CLI read ANTHROPIC_API_KEY only with NANOCODE_ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, so a machine with the key and no Claude Code login failed with "no Claude Code login found". With no base URL, NANOCODE_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY now builds `ClaudeClient::subscription_or_key`: the default client (nanocode's own login, then Claude Code's) under `ClaudeAuthOrKey` with the key behind it, so a signed-in member keeps the plan and the key takes over when the login gives no headers or cannot recover a 401. The request keeps the subscription wire, which the API accepts with an x-api-key (checked with curl and haiku through the egress proxy). Bearer tokens (ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN) still need a base URL, since `ClaudeAuthOrKey` carries an API key only. The login error now ends "sign in with /login claude or set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY". Checked with no ~/.claude: `exec -m claude-haiku-5-5 'Reply with exactly: PONG'` prints PONG with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and no base URL, and without the key prints the new hint.

- perf(tui): comparing two cells compares inline symbols as fixed 14-byte arrays instead of calling memcmp on their byte slices (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 CLI performance: first frame and per-frame CPU). `BufferDiff` compares every cell of the frame with the previous one (`Cell::eq`), and `Symbol::bytes() == Symbol::bytes()` went through a slice comparison, a call to libc's memcmp per cell: the largest single symbol in output/tuirender's 60-frame profile and in a first-frame profile of the CLI. `Symbol::same` answers equal for two unset symbols, compares two inline symbols by length and the whole fixed array (bytes past the length are zero, as `Symbol::new` writes them), and keeps the byte comparison for the rest, so equality is unchanged (an unset symbol still equals an inline blank). output/tuirender (as below), bytes identical at 80x24 and 240x70. First frame (medians of 9): 240x70 2,065,631 -> 1,781,049 user instructions (-13.8%), 80x24 541,369 -> 510,164 (-5.8%); 60 frames (n=7): 240x70 123.98M -> 107.37M (-13.4%), 80x24 28.32M -> 26.63M (-6.0%). CLI, the three tui changes of today together (dist builds of c88f7c2c0 with and without them through scripts/build-cli.sh with BOLT; bench/cli suite.mjs --parts=firstframe at 120x40, `perf stat -e instructions:u,instructions:k,page-faults` over each whole session from start to exit, 4 interleaved batches of 3 rounds, n=12 each, dev-georgios at load 100+): user instructions 9,125,998 -> 8,601,443 (-5.7%), kernel 11,814,268 -> 11,403,377 (-3.5%), page faults 848 -> 827. The first frame's bytes are identical at 80x24 and 240x70 (later frames differ only in the cells of the random session ID). Commands: `cargo clippy --offline -p nanocode-tui --no-deps -- -D warnings`. Files: crates/tui/src/ui/buffer.rs.
- perf(tui): a terminal `Cell` is 32 bytes instead of 40 (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 CLI performance: first frame). `Symbol` keeps up to `SYMBOL_INLINE_BYTES = size_of::<Box<str>>() - 2` = 14 bytes inline (with its length and the enum tag that fills the 16 bytes a boxed symbol takes) and a longer grapheme behind a thin `Box<Box<str>>`, so `Symbol` is 16 bytes and a cell is 16 + two 4-byte colors + a 2-byte modifier, padded to 32. Graphemes of 15 to 22 bytes (ZWJ sequences of three or more people, subdivision flags) now allocate where they did not, and longer ones, which allocated already, allocate twice. Both screen buffers shrink by a fifth, so the first frame fills and faults in a fifth fewer pages for them: at the bench's 120x40, 2 x 4,800 cells, 384 KB -> 307 KB. output/tuirender (see the entry below; run from a systemd user unit, so without COLORTERM and with the 256-color downsampling, for both builds), bytes identical at 80x24 and 240x70, first frame and 60 frames. First frame (medians of 9): 240x70 user 2,132,940 -> 2,065,529, kernel 3,299,617 -> 2,902,072 (-12%), page faults 407 -> 341; 80x24 user 546,469 -> 541,395, kernel 1,425,571 -> 1,409,789, faults 114 -> 107. 60 frames (n=7): 240x70 user 125.11M -> 123.98M, faults 408 -> 342; 80x24 user 28.09M -> 28.32M (+0.8%: the harness's streamed lines carry a 25-byte family emoji, which now takes two allocations per draw), faults 115 -> 108. Commands: `cargo clippy --offline -p nanocode-tui --no-deps -- -D warnings`. Files: crates/tui/src/ui/buffer.rs.
- perf(tui): a draw after a resize (the first frame among them) clears no buffer it has just allocated (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 CLI performance: first frame). `TerminalSession::draw` allocated both screen buffers with `Buffer::empty` (every cell `Cell::EMPTY`), then reset the current one before rendering and, since a new size is a full repaint, the previous one again before the diff, so the first frame wrote every cell of both buffers twice. The resets now run only when the size is unchanged (`current` on every such frame, `previous` when the frame is a full repaint), before rendering instead of after it; nothing between the two points reads `previous`. Checked with output/tuirender: one binary that enters a `TerminalSession` and draws a header, a status line, a styled prompt row and streamed lines with CJK, an emoji and a ZWJ family, built with the dist profile's fat LTO, one codegen unit and panic=abort, run in a pty by a Python driver under `perf stat -e instructions:u,instructions:k,page-faults`, before and after interleaved. The terminal bytes are identical at 80x24 and 240x70, for the first frame and for 60 frames. First frame (medians of 9): 240x70 2,468,998 -> 2,133,051 user instructions (-13.6%), 80x24 584,733 -> 546,275 (-6.6%); kernel instructions and page faults unchanged (240x70 3.30M/3.36M, 407/407). 60 frames (n=7): 240x70 125.45M -> 125.11M, 80x24 28.13M -> 28.09M, the first frame's saving and no per-frame change. Tried and not kept: diffing the first frame against a `previous` buffer that is never allocated (`BufferDiff` reading `Cell::EMPTY` for an empty previous). At 240x70 it saves another 133 to 165 page faults and 0.76M to 1.0M kernel instructions on the first frame, but each of three forms made every later frame dearer: `get().unwrap_or(&Cell::EMPTY)` +4% user instructions over 60 frames, a `step` generic over how previous cells are read +17% (`Cell::eq` stopped being inlined into either copy, with or without `#[inline]`), an index mask +5.5%. nanocode-ts does not run this code: nanocode-tui compiles to an empty crate on wasm32. Commands: `cargo clippy --offline -p nanocode-tui --no-deps -- -D warnings`. Files: crates/tui/src/terminal.rs.
- fix(claude): bound the Messages connection with a connect timeout and a stream idle timeout (2026-11-14, e2e BUG 11). `ClaudeClient::default` (the subscription login), `with_api_key`, `workload_identity` and the CLI's custom endpoint built their client with `nanocode_http::client()`, which sets neither, so a response that stopped sending after its headers held the turn for good (agent 19: 200 s of silence on one connection, no retry). They now share `ClaudeClient::http_client()`: `MESSAGES_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` 30 s, the Codex WebSocket's `CONNECT_TIMEOUT`, and `MESSAGES_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT` 300 s, Codex's `STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT` (stock Codex's stream_idle_timeout_ms), as the client's `read_timeout`, which bounds the head and each body read; a lapse is a timed-out body error, which `is_transient` retries under the usual uncertainty rules. The simulator's HTTP wire already stalls bodies past its idle bound and carries the `http-no-read-timeout` canary (cfo row canary_http_no_read_timeout); the bug was the CLI's client construction, which the simulator builds itself, so no new scenario. Checked against agent 19's mock with `stall #slow 310` (one word, then 310 s between words): the first request at t0, `nanocode: model request failed (attempt 1 of 11), retrying in 0.6s: Messages transport: request or response body error: operation timed out` and the second request at t0+300.8 s; wasm32 check of nanocode-backend-claude-client.

- fix(codex): transport errors keep their cause and drop internal durability wording (2026-11-14, e2e BUG 4). Codex's `map_http_error` used the `nanocode_http::Error`'s own Display, which stops at "error sending request for url (...)", so a refused port or a proxy's 403 lost its cause; the loop the Claude path already ran (`client_error`) is now `nanocode_http::error_detail`, used by `client_error`, Codex's `map_http_error` and the CLI's model listing. The final error also read "durable operation recovery execution policy failed: ..." (Codex's `recover_failure` re-dispositions a still-pending operation's error as Retry) or "durable operation previously failed: ..." (the operation's recorded failure, also on its first attempt). An `ExecutionPolicy` error whose source is itself a `NanocodeError` only changes the disposition, so it now shows and chains as that error (`cancellation recovery` is the other such layer); a layer reporting its own failure (`durability`, `Claude recovery`, `tool host interrupted`) keeps its name. `ReplayedExecutionFailed` shows the recorded error as it was. No simulator invariant reads error text. Checked with `NANOCODE_OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:1/v1` (models from a local list): `nanocode: Responses HTTPS request failed: error sending request for url (http://127.0.0.1:1/v1/responses): Connection refused (os error 111)`, and the listing error ends with the same cause; wasm32 check of nanocode-agent-types, nanocode-http and nanocode-backend-codex-client.

- fix(http): an untrusted TLS certificate fails at once with a hint instead of being retried (2026-11-14, e2e BUG 17). A server certificate the trust store rejects came back from `connect::tls` as an io error, the client counted it a connect error, and `nanocode_http::retryable` calls every connect error retryable, so the Claude loop retried an UnknownIssuer for 11 attempts and 184 s before saying anything. `connect::tls` now wraps a `rustls::Error::InvalidCertificate` in `UntrustedCertificate` ("the server's TLS certificate is not trusted; if a proxy intercepts TLS, set SSL_CERT_FILE to its CA bundle", the rustls error kept as its source), and `connect::untrusted_certificate` finds it in a chain: `retryable` answers false for it (the Claude and Codex HTTPS clients and everyone else on `nanocode_http`), and so does the Codex WebSocket's `is_transient_websocket`, whose connector uses the same `connect::tls`. Other TLS failures (alerts, resets) stay transient. The simulator's wires carry no TLS, so no scenario reaches this. Checked: against agent 19's private-CA mock (`/home/hand/e2e19-mock`, cert from ca.pem) `exec -m claude-haiku-5-5` fails in 1 s with `Messages transport: error sending request for url (https://localhost:18943/v1/messages): the server's TLS certificate is not trusted; if a proxy intercepts TLS, set SSL_CERT_FILE to its CA bundle: invalid peer certificate: UnknownIssuer` (was 184 s); `cargo clippy` clean in the touched files; wasm32 check of nanocode-http and nanocode-backend-codex-client.

- deps(tls): the graviola fork draws randomness from `nanocode_platform::fill_random` and uses plain `#[cfg]`; the getrandom and cfg-if workspace shims are deleted (2026-11-14, TLS plan step 5b). `mid/rng.rs`'s `SystemRandom` calls `nanocode_platform::fill_random`, so an installed platform host (the simulator's) controls every key share, nonce and TLS random, and without one it reads the kernel through nanocode-platform's entropy buffer as UUIDs do. The two `cfg_if!` blocks become `#[cfg]` items: `low/mod.rs`'s x86_64, aarch64 and unsupported-target arms put the arm's cfg on each item, and `low/ct.rs` keeps only its non-ctgrind arm, since the `__ctgrind` feature is gone. `test_toggle`'s debug-build arm, which read `GRAVIOLA_CPU_DISABLE_<id>` from the environment and printed on every CPU feature check, goes; the release arm stays for every build. crates/core/getrandom (66 lines) and crates/core/cfg-if (26 lines) had no other user. Checked: cargo check of nanocode-tls, -sandbox and -mpp, and of graviola for aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu; output/tls-equal now seeds randomness through a nanocode-platform host (getrandom is no longer in its graph except as that host's seeded source): all 150 reference transcript digests identical to the crates.io graviola build seeded through getrandom; output/tls-live through the Hand's HTTPS proxy unchanged. `cargo metadata` resolves 149 to 147 packages (26 third-party either way).

L1: `ClaudeWorkspaceFiles` keeps, per canonical path, the mtime and what the model has of the file (`View::Part` after an offset, limited or truncated Read; `Whole`/`Current` with a SipHash of the bytes after a whole Read, a Write or an Edit), in an `Atom` shared by its clones. An Edit is stale when the mtime moved past the recorded one and the bytes differ from a whole view; a stale Edit that applies gets stock's `(note: the file had been modified on disk since you last read it …)`, one that does not apply gets `File has been modified since read, either by the user or by a linter. Read it again before attempting to write it.`, an Edit of a file the model never read whole gets no suffix, and only a current file gets `(file state is current in your context …)`; `old_string` "" creates a missing file (parents included) or fills an empty one, and otherwise answers `Cannot create new file - file already exists.` L2: the continuation after max_tokens is `Output token limit hit. Resume directly — no apology, no recap of what you were doing. Pick up mid-thought if that is where the cut happened. Break remaining work into smaller pieces.` L3: a direct call to a tool with an upstream definition is checked against its offered schema first (missing required, unexpected with additionalProperties false, top-level type, numeric strings coerced for number and integer as stock coerces `"2"`, non-integers reported as `int`) and answered with `<tool_use_error>InputValidationError: <tool> failed due to the following issue(s):\n…</tool_use_error>` (new crates/backends/claude/tools/src/tools/input.rs); an unknown tool gets `<tool_use_error>Error: No such tool available: <name>[hint]</tool_use_error>` with stock's Grep and Glob Bash hints and its case-sensitivity hint; Read of a missing path answers `File does not exist. Left: Read dedupe (`Wasted call`), offset 0 numbering, the allow_large hint and relative Write paths (L6/M2), stock-only tools (Agent, NotebookEdit), Bash timeout semantics (M3), and a tool_use cut by max_tokens, which stock keeps as `__unparsedToolInput` and answers with the JSON InputValidationError while nanocode still replaces it with a text note and a second continuation. - scripts/build-cli.sh drops the BOLT output's copy of the linker's unwind tables: the shipped Linux nanocode 46,225,376 to 44,109,480 bytes (-2.1 MB, -4.6%; `xz -6` 13,678,088 to 13,315,272) (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 size track). BOLT writes a new `.eh_frame` and `.eh_frame_hdr` for the code it lays out and keeps the linker's as `.bolt.org.eh_frame` (1,876,748 bytes) and `.bolt.org.eh_frame_hdr` (235,948) in the first segment; with `-use-old-text` every function is rewritten, the `PT_GNU_EH_FRAME` header names the new table, and all 34,537 of its search entries point into the new `.eh_frame`, so nothing reads the old pair (the binary imports no `__register_frame_info`; Rust's unwinder finds tables through `dl_iterate_phdr` and `PT_GNU_EH_FRAME`). They could not be cut where lld put them, at the front of the read-only segment ahead of `.rodata`, whose addresses the non-PIE code holds, so `scripts/cli-eh-frame.ld` (`SECTIONS { .eh_frame : { KEEP(*(.eh_frame)) } } INSERT BEFORE .eh_frame_hdr;`, passed with `-T`) moves `.eh_frame` after `.gcc_except_table`, which puts both old tables at the end of that segment, and `scripts/trim-cli.py` (run on the stripped output) shortens that segment to end before them, removes their whole pages from the file and moves the later segments' and sections' file offsets down by that many pages (a multiple of every later segment's alignment, so addresses do not change) and marks the two sections NOBITS. It exits with an error, failing the build, unless the two sections exist, are adjacent at the end of a segment with no live section between, `PT_GNU_EH_FRAME` names another table and that table's binary search entries all point outside them; the unwind tables that are used are untouched (2,004,360 + 276,460 bytes, as before). Unchanged by the cut: program headers (the same 12, GNU_RELRO and TLS kept, where `objcopy -R` dropped GNU_RELRO), `nanocode --version`, and gdb's backtrace from a breakpoint on `write` during `--version` (12 frames, the same addresses) on the trimmed and untrimmed output of the same build; checked first on a small Rust program BOLTed the same way, whose `RUST_BACKTRACE=full` panic output (18 lines) is byte-identical before and after. Both binaries built by `scripts/build-cli.sh nanocode-cli nanocode` (BOLT 19) at 62a0936e4, before in its own target dir; bench/cli `suite.mjs --only=nc --rounds=3`, firstframe and oneshot, alternating them in 6 batches under `perf stat` (18 samples each, dev-georgios, load ~110), medians before -> after: first frame user instructions 9.125M -> 9.139M, kernel 12.19M -> 12.18M, page faults 843 -> 842; one-shot user 9.688M -> 9.669M, kernel 12.13M -> 12.10M, page faults 894 -> 893.5. Measured at 62a0936e4, before e1f0d5cfb's startup function order, which changes only which order BOLT writes functions in; the trim reads only section and segment headers and the new table, and refuses any other layout. nanocode-ts is not affected: it does not go through this script. Files: scripts/build-cli.sh, scripts/cli-eh-frame.ld, scripts/trim-cli.py.
