- deps(json): serde_json parses floats with std's `f64::from_str` and `f32::from_str` instead of its lexical module, which leaves (3,708 lines; 2026-11-14, JSON plan step 3). A number whose significand fits in u64 is exact when the significand is at most 2^53 and the power of ten at most 10^22 (2^24 and 10^10 for `f32`), one correctly rounded multiply or divide; otherwise its significand and exponent are written into the scratch buffer as `<digits>e<exponent>` and parsed by std. A number past u64 keeps its integer and fraction digits in scratch as before and is parsed as `<integer>.<fraction>e<exponent>` (a missing part written as 0). An infinite result is still `number out of range`, at the same position. Agent 23 measured std against lexical on 11,497,985 seeded texts and 50,300,695 round trips with 0 differences. Equal, output/json-equal: 100,000,000 seeded number texts (up to 800 integer and fraction digits, exponents -400..400 and past 100,000, trailing garbage) into `f64`, `f32` and every 8th into `Value`, comparing bits and error texts with line and column, plus 3,000,000 documents and 100,000,000 f64 round trips, 0 differences. Speed: a full-precision f64 (17 digits, so past the exact path) parses in 126 to 145 ns against 67 to 98 ns (+44% to +97%); the corpus streamed as `Box<RawValue>` +0.8% to +3.4% and parsed into `Value` -0.7% to +1.6%, within the bar. Commands: `cargo check --locked -p serde_json`, natively and for wasm32-unknown-unknown. Files: crates/patches/serde_json/{src/de.rs,src/lib.rs,src/lexical/ (deleted)}.

- fix(process): psh answers as `/bin/bash` when it stands in for bash, and exec_command's `shell` runs the shell Codex 0.162.1 would pick (2026-11-13, ~/hill/analysis/codex-parity.md section 3). Stock spawns the user's shell, so a model saw `/bin/bash: line 1: x: command not found`, `$0` = `/bin/bash` and `$SHELL` = `/bin/bash`, where nanocode gave `psh: line 1:`, `psh` and an empty `$SHELL`; and stock honors `shell`, where nanocode ran every `shell` in psh (`{"cmd":"echo $0","shell":"/bin/sh"}`: stock `/usr/bin/sh`, nanocode `psh`; real runs had `psh: ` 3 times in one m4-codex ds trial). Now: psh takes `$0` and the name in front of its messages from `PSH_NAME` when the command line gives none (embedded, warm and standalone alike; psh's own variable, taken out of the environment like `PSH_NESTED_OFF`), and `ShellSessions::execute` sets `PSH_NAME=/bin/bash` (`nanocode_home::shell::default_shell_path`) and, when the environment has none, `SHELL=/bin/bash` for every command psh runs. A requested `shell` whose name is not bash resolves as stock does (`nanocode_home::shell::requested`): sh or zsh is the user's passwd shell when it has that name, else the first on the command's `PATH`, else `/bin/sh` or `/bin/zsh`; any other name (dash, fish, a missing zsh) is `/bin/sh`; it runs as a cold process, `SHELL -lc CMD` or `-c` with `login: false`, never in psh. Stock's resolution was measured, not read: a shellprobe scenario in a private copy of ~/hill/parity2 (`run2.py shellprobe stock-codex`) gave `/bin/sh` -> `/usr/bin/sh`, `sh` -> `/usr/bin/sh`, `/usr/bin/bash` and `bash` -> `/bin/bash` (the passwd shell), `zsh` (not installed), `/bin/dash` and `fish` -> `/bin/sh`, `/nonexistent/sh` -> `/usr/bin/sh`. Measured with `cargo build --locked --release -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode` and `run2.py <scenario> nc-codex`, tool outputs compared with stock after dropping chunk id and wall time: exits 11 of 11 identical (6 of 11 with the nanocode-m4 binary), shellprobe 9 of 13 (0 of 13); the 4 left are `$$`'s value, `/proc/$$/exe` (the nanocode binary), `SHELL` exported where stock's is an unexported shell variable, and a nested `sh -c` speaking bash (`sh: line 1: x: command not found` where dash says `sh: 1: x: not found`). bash scenario: 12 of 15 identical, the rest `$BASH_VERSION`/`/proc/$$/exe`, timing and a file the old stock run lacked. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p` nanocode-home, nanocode-process, psh, nanocode-psh-embedded (native) and nanocode-home, nanocode-process, nanocode-psh-embedded (`--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`), all exit 0.
- deps(json): serde_json formats floats with its own safe port of zmij 1.0.23's scalar path (crates/patches/serde_json/src/float.rs, 400 lines), and zmij leaves (2026-11-14, JSON plan step 2). std's formatter cannot stand in: zmij rounds exact ties half to even and writes `1e+16` and `0.00001` where std rounds half up and writes `1e16` and `1e-5` (agent 23's output/json-floats: 9,224 of 50.3M f64 and 97,447 of 49.8M f32 differ). The port keeps zmij's arithmetic move for move: the 618-entry 128-bit power-of-ten table computed at compile time from the same minor, major and fixup tables (Dougall Johnson's method), `compute_dec_exp` and `compute_exp_shift` instead of the 2,048-byte shift table, the regular 64-bit path with its extra digit from the fractional part (Xiang JunBo), the 32-bit path with its 34-bit fraction, the irregular path at powers of two (the f32 significand shifted in 32 bits, as zmij does), subnormals scaled to the threshold, f32's 7-digit adjustment, and zmij's layout (fixed notation for decimal exponents -5..=15 for f64 and -6..=12 for f32, `e+`/`e-` with the exponent's digits otherwise, `0.0` for zero, `NaN`, `inf`, `-inf` from `format`). Gone: asm!, the SSE2, SSE4.1 and NEON digit and shuffle paths, `get_unchecked`, the exponent-string table, the build script and zmij's 68 unsafe sites; the text is written into nanocode-sys's `DecimalText`, which gains `put_point`, `put_exponent` ('e' and the sign), `put_zeros`, `copy_within` and `span`, so its bytes stay ASCII and `span` stays the one unchecked UTF-8 view (`text` now calls it). Equal, output/json-equal (crates.io serde_json =1.0.150 with zmij beside the vendored copy, in one process): every f32 bit pattern (4,294,967,296 values through `to_writer`, every 256th also through `Value::from(f).to_string()` and the invalid-type error text that formats the float), 1,000,000,000 seeded f64 (uniform bits, decimal-shaped, powers of two and of ten with two neighbours each side, subnormals, MIN, MAX, EPSILON and the edges, small odd significands times 2^-60..2^50 for exact ties, signs flipped at random; every 64th also through `Value` Display, `Number` Display, the error text and a parse back), 0 differences; changing the f32 tie digit from 2 to 3 is caught at 0x3b200000 (0.0024414062 against 0.0024414063). Speed, output/json-equal `bench` (minimum of 7 interleaved rounds, three runs, load 11 to 12 on the 5-core Hand): `to_writer` of 1,000,000 seeded f64 26.5 to 31.8 ns with zmij, 38.0 to 43.6 ns with the port (+36% to +50%), f32 13.9 to 16.3 against 15.7 to 17.8 ns (+7% to +27%); the plan's benchmarks do not move: the session log and OTLP trace corpus (643 lines, 2.46 MB) parsed line by line into `BTreeMap<String, Box<RawValue>>` -0.5%, 0.0%, -0.3%, streamed as `Box<RawValue>` 0.0%, -0.1%, +0.4%, and re-encoded from `Value` -16.5%, -2.9%, -7.7%. Packages: `cargo metadata --locked` 149 to 148 (third-party 24 to 23). Commands: `cargo check --locked -p serde_json -p itoa`, natively and for wasm32-unknown-unknown. - fix(claude): automatic compaction of a model that is not a Claude model goes straight to Claude Code's summary prompt, without the server-compaction request first, and direct sessions announce a changed Bash working directory with Claude Code's `# Environment update` (2026-11-13, ~/hill/analysis/claude-parity.md M4 and L5). M4: since the server-compaction entry of 2026-11-10 every compaction first resent the previous main request with `compaction: {"type":"summarize"}` and the `compact-2026-09-04` beta, and only took the prompt path when the reply had no `compaction` block; a custom model through the Tempo gateway never returns one and does not refuse with an error naming compaction, so `summary_refused` was never set and each compaction paid one more call at the largest context of the session. Claude Code 2.1.300 never asks for it: its binary (~/hill/stock/rt/claude-glibc/claude) holds no `compact-2026` string. Server compaction is now asked only when the model is a Claude model (`ModelSelection::as_claude`, as `recovery_thinking` decides), so Claude models keep the 2026-11-10 behavior; and a server-compaction reply that ends without a block now also stops the session asking again, as a refusal naming compaction did, so a Claude id behind a gateway without server compaction wastes one call per session instead of one per compaction. L5: Claude Code puts `# Environment update\n - Primary working directory: <new> (was <old>)\n\n` before `<total_tokens>` in the system message after the tool round that changed its working directory (`ugt`, field `workingDirectory`), including the reset to the project directory after `cd /`; nanocode tracked the direct Bash cwd (`LocalBash::cwd`) but never said so. The cwd atom is now created by `install_default_tools_with_providers`, handed to the Bash tool and, through `ClaudeTools::working_directory`, to the agent, whose `environment::WorkingDirectory` compares it with the last one announced each round in direct (`upstream_context`) sessions; Code Mode calls do not move the cwd, so nothing changes there. Not ported: stock's `Is a git repository: X (was Y)` line. Checked with the parity mocks on copies of their scripts (~/wt/cc-p3, ~/wt/cc-p1) and a release build of this tree: `WIN=100000 NC=<build> run3.py compact nc-claude` sent 17 requests, 13 main and 4 summary prompts, none with `compaction` or the compact beta; the build before (runs3/compact/nc-claude) sent 16, 10 main, 3 probes (22,572 bytes of messages) and 3 summaries, and the probes used up 3 of the mock's 12 scripted steps; stock sends 8 main and 3 summaries and then stops for its refill breaker. `run.py nc-claude` (baseline, 17 requests as before) now sends at message 4 `# Environment update\n - Primary working directory: …/work/sub (was …/work)\n\n<total_tokens>14999988 tokens left</total_tokens>` and at message 40 `…/work (was …/work/sub)`, the same texts as stock at the same indexes. Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude` native and `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude` (no warnings in the crate; with `-D warnings` it stops at three existing `useless_conversion` errors in nanocode-sys), `cargo build --locked --release -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode` (pass).

- fix(process): an exec_command or write_stdin output that overflowed the 1 MiB capture is truncated with Codex 0.162.1's header: `Warning: truncated output (original token count: <all bytes / 4>)`, then the `... N bytes omitted ...` line, instead of a token count of the kept 1 MiB and `Total output lines: N` (2026-11-13). Stock's `ExecCommandToolOutput::truncated_output_with_policy` (codex-rs/core/src/tools/context.rs at rust-v0.162.1) takes this branch whenever its head-tail buffer omitted bytes: the count is the call's `original_token_count`, the `Total output lines` line is left out, and the marker is repeated above the cut unless the kept text still holds it. The kept bytes and the `…N chars truncated…`/`…N tokens truncated…` counts were already stock's. The custom-model 10,000-byte cap the cost backlog's item 3 asked for (~/hill/analysis/cost-backlog.md section 3, ~/hill/analysis/codex-parity.md section 4) needs no change: the entry of 2026-11-13 on the 10,000-token default and the `chars truncated` entry already give `Model::Custom` 10,000 bytes head and tail, and a debug build of 3638a2c equals stock on every truncated output of the parity mock's bigout (5), trunc2 (4) and lane (5) scenarios after masking chunk IDs and wall times. Measured with ~/wt/codex-bytecap-par/run3.py (ctp's mock3.py with a new scenario `huge`: `seq 1 300000` with and without `max_output_tokens` 200, `seq 1 300000 | head -c 1048576` and `1048577`, 150,000 copies of `é€😀`, and a running process polled with write_stdin), ds/low, against stock: before, 6 of 7 `huge` outputs differed (`original token count: 262152` and `Total output lines: 164133` where stock has `original token count: 497224` and `... 940319 bytes omitted ...`); after, all 7 are equal, and bigout, trunc2 and lane are unchanged (the only differences left are timing in bigout's polled loop and lane's tty workdir, process ids and psh texts, which other entries cover). Change: nanocode-process-contracts gains `limit_omitted_in(output, limit, unit, marker, original_token_count)`, sharing the head-and-tail cut with `redact_and_limit_in` through `cut_middle`; nanocode-process's `take_output` calls it when `CapturedChunk::omission_marker` is set. Not changed: stock truncates every other tool output in history with the model policy times 1.2 (12,000 bytes, `chars` marker, for unknown models; `with_serialization_allowance` in codex-utils-output-truncation), where the codex client keeps `TOOL_OUTPUT_TOKEN_LIMIT` (12,000 tokens) for all models; with only exec_command, write_stdin and view_image offered to custom models no output reaches either limit. `cargo check --locked --lib` of nanocode-process-contracts and nanocode-process, natively and for wasm32-unknown-unknown, passes without warnings. Files: crates/core/process/src/lib.rs, crates/integrations/process/src/{lib.rs,output.rs}.
- fix(images): gateway requests keep their images within the limits measured in cmp2, and a 1-token incomplete with images in the history drops them and resends instead of ending the run (2026-11-14). The image-heavy tasks (video-processing, extract-moves-from-video, gcode-to-text) died two ways no harness survived (~/hill/analysis/glm-backlog.md item 2; ~/hill/analysis/loss-backlog.md item 3): (a) a Responses request carrying at least 2.9 MB of base64 images comes back `response.incomplete` (max_output_tokens) after 1 output token on every retry: the failing last requests carried 2,913,430 to 5,416 KB of image URLs (extract-moves-from-video__XTjiu3y 2,913,430 bytes in 11 images; the two nc-codex losses video-processing__SaqSeG6 and __BGYN8zB 3,453,034 and 4,679,126 bytes in 3 images of up to 2 MB each), and the largest that succeeded carried 2,641,785 (extract-moves-from-video__5A4PbiG, 14 images); (b) @cf (Workers AI) answers error 8007 "Image count N exceeds limit 8 per request", which ended 8 stock-claude GLM trials. nanocode's codex harness sent view_image's PNGs as they were (about 3 MB of base64 for one 1920x1080 frame, so a single image passes the limit) and evicted to 8 images for every model, which the DeepSeek route does not need (stock-codex DS succeeded with 28 images; codex-parity.md item 2a). `ImageWindow` (nanocode-image) now carries a byte budget beside its image count: `GATEWAY` allows 2,641,785 bytes of image URLs (the largest successful request), `WORKERS_AI_GATEWAY` adds the 8-image limit and `WORKERS_AI` is that limit alone. The codex harness uses `WORKERS_AI_GATEWAY` for a non-OpenAI model (Glm53, Kimi, Mimo, Custom) whose ID starts with `@cf/`, `GATEWAY` for the other non-OpenAI models, and keeps `CODEX` for OpenAI models; the claude harness uses `WORKERS_AI` for `@cf/` models (Messages requests of 3.1 MB succeeded in cmp2, so no byte budget) and Claude Code's 100/600 otherwise. Under a budget an image whose base64 exceeds an eighth of it (330,223 bytes, so the 8 newest always fit) is re-encoded when the request is built, with nanocode-image's own codec: JPEG at quality 85 (its `JPEG_QUALITY`) at the same dimensions, shrinking by the square root of the size ratio only while still too large, cached by the source's digest, so the stored history is untouched and every later request carries the same bytes and keeps its cached prefix. Eviction then drops the oldest images when the kept ones pass the budget, down to half of it, the same half-window batches the count already used, so the prefix breaks once per batch rather than on every new image. Recovery: when a call fails with `response.incomplete`, reason max_output_tokens and at most 1 output token (`ResponsesError::is_empty_incomplete`), the codex harness sends the same call once more inside the same model step with every image replaced by Codex's rejected-image stub ("[image omitted after the provider rejected its data]"), and on success replaces the images in the session history the same way (`repair_rejected_request`); the client's retry policy treats that incomplete as final for both its attempts and its stream reconnects (`retry_attempt` and `reconnectable` in crates/backends/codex/client/src/tower/middleware/retry.rs, the reconnects of 322de32), so it reaches that resend at once, and every other incomplete is retried as before; the claude harness, on a max_tokens stop with at most 1 output token, replaces the images in the pending history with that stub before its continuation. view_image results carry their `detail` again ("high", as stock Codex sends; codex-parity.md item 2b). Measured with output/imgmock (a scripted mock: 10 view_image or Read calls on 1920x1080 PNGs of 2.2 to 2.6 MB, `NC=<binary> python3 run.py <arms>`) and output/image-budget (nanocode-image alone): each frame's 2,886,916 to 3,440,104 bytes of base64 became 286,520 to 297,328 bytes of JPEG at full size, in 130 to 185 ms the first time (opt-level 1) and about 1.6 ms from the cache. On the DeepSeek model the codex request after the 9th frame went from 16,193,934 bytes of image URLs in 5 frames (master, which evicted 4 at the 9th) to 2,631,851 in 9, and after the 10th from 19,634,060 in 6 to 1,156,112 in 4 (stock Codex: 31,590,320 in 10); Claude requests on DeepSeek are unchanged (3,923,232 bytes in 10 frames). On `@cf/zai-org/glm-5.3-flash` both harnesses keep at most 8 images: the request after the 9th frame carries 5 (codex 1,454,799 bytes, claude 2,007,276), where stock Claude Code sends every image (and got 8007 in cmp2). With the mock answering every request that holds an image with a 1-token incomplete (or a max_tokens stop), stock Codex exits 1 after 7 posts and Claude Code exits "API Error: Claude's response exceeded the 65536 output token maximum" after 5, while nanocode exits 0 in both: the codex harness posts each image call once, then once with the stub and goes on (7 posts for 3 frames in 12 s; before the retry policy treated the incomplete as final it posted the image call 31 times, 94 posts in 297 s), and the claude harness replaces the image after the first max_tokens stop and finishes in 7 requests. `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-image -p nanocode-backend-codex-client -p nanocode-backend-codex -p nanocode-backend-claude`, natively and for wasm32-unknown-unknown, passed. Files: crates/core/image/src/{history.rs,lib.rs}, crates/backends/codex/client/src/{transport/error.rs,tower/middleware/retry.rs}, crates/backends/codex/src/model/{input.rs,run/images.rs,run/lifecycle.rs,run/responses.rs,run/side.rs,run/turn.rs}, crates/backends/claude/src/{agent.rs,agent/images.rs}.
- nanocode-http's server ends the connection after a streamed reply whose declared `content-length` the stream does not meet, and writes no byte past it; `nanocode-sim --scenario http_server` drives the server with a scripted, misbehaving client on a simulated socket and found it (2026-11-14). The server is what the sandbox's egress proxy and other nanocode servers stand on, and no scenario ran it: `--wire http` runs only the client. The scenario scripts up to 6 exchanges on one connection, pipelined or one at a time: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE and HEAD over HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/1.0, with `connection: close` or `keep-alive`, bodies without framing, by `content-length` (up to 4 KiB, 64 KiB one time in ten) or chunked (up to 6 chunks, chunk extensions, trailers), delivered in seeded pieces with seeded gaps (pieces as small as one byte); a handler that reads the whole body, one part of it, or none before it answers; replies of 200, 201, 204, 304, 404, 500 and 503 that are empty, whole, or streamed with a `content-length` that is exact, absent, longer or shorter than the stream; a malformed request head; and the client cutting the connection at a seeded byte with an EOF or a reset. It checks that the handler sees the requests the client sent, in order and with the bodies it sent; that an independent reader (its own framing and chunk decoding over `wire::parse_response` heads) reads one well framed response per handled request, with the handler's status and body, none for HEAD, 204 or 304; that the server answers no request after one that obliges it to close (`connection: close`, HTTP/1.0 without keep-alive, a close-delimited stream) and handles every request it may (all of them unless a reply obliges it to close, a handler left body unread, the head is malformed or the cut came first); that it fails only on the malformed head or a cut; and that nothing hangs or runs past 30 minutes of virtual time. The bug: `server::respond` sent a streamed `Outgoing::Stream` reply with its handler's `content-length` header as declared and kept the connection when the stream ended. A stream shorter than its declared length left the client waiting for bytes that never came, then reading the next response's head as the rest of the body; a longer one wrote bytes past the declared length, which the client read as the next response's head. On the server before this change (and the scenario as first written, with a gap after every piece; a gap now follows one piece in a hundred, since one-byte pieces each followed by a gap took `--seed 17624` past the time limit), seeds 0..500 fail 10 times and 1000..3000 71 times, every failure after such a reply: `--seed 443` hangs (a short reply, the client waiting for its body while the server waits for the next request), 54, 328 and 451 read `invalid HTTP version` where the next head should be, and 118, 166, 176, 340, 400 and 474 see the server handle requests after the mismatched reply. Now `respond` reads the declared length (`declared_length`), writes at most that many bytes of the stream and returns that the connection may not be kept when the stream yields more or ends short, and an unreadable `content-length` on a stream closes it too. A streamed reply whose length is right is written as before, so the egress proxy, which streams an upstream body with the upstream's `content-length` and ends it with an error when the upstream is cut short, behaves as before. Mutations: `corrupt_response_byte` flips a bit of a byte the client reads at a seeded offset under 400, and `drop_request_byte` drops a byte of the first request; over seeds 0..400 they are caught by 210 and 255 seeds. bin/nanocode-sim/cfo.sh gets the rows `http_server` (8), `http_server_twice` (2) and a canary for each mutation. Checks on the hosted Hand (5 cores, -j 2): with this change seeds 0..335,000 of `--scenario http_server` pass, and 30,000..35,000 with `--twice`; the ten seeds above pass. The gate on the hosted Hand (5 cores shared by three agents): `nanocode-sim --tidy` clean; `cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-http -p nanocode-sim` and `cargo check --locked --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p nanocode-http` report nothing in either crate; `cargo check --locked --workspace --all-targets` passes; runtime seeds 7740000000000..+3,000 of `--store kv`, 7741000000000..+1,000 of `--store memory` and 7742000000000..+500 of `--store kv --twice` pass. The last two are short of 3,000 because the runtime scenario ran about two seeds a second there, and neither it nor anything it runs changes here: nanocode-http's server is not on its path. Rebased onto 3638a2c7e, where nanocode-sync's streams replace futures-util (the scenario builds its streamed replies with `nanocode_sync::stream::iter`), the release binary passes seeds 0..30,000 of `--scenario http_server` and 30,000..33,000 with `--twice`, the two mutations are caught by 210 and 255 seeds of 0..400, the ten seeds above pass and `--tidy` is clean.
- perf(store-jsonl): a session summary's anchor digest is stored as 64 hex characters instead of a JSON array of 32 numbers, and an array written before is still read (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 CLI performance track: sessions at 14,600). The anchor (where a summarized journal ended and the SHA-256 of what followed) was 2.2 MB of the summaries base's 11.6 MB at 14,600 sessions, and parsing its 467,000 numbers (`parse_integer`, `SeqAccess::next_element`, `parse_number`) was about 10% of the user instructions of listing after the changes above. `Anchor::digest` is `#[serde(with = "hex_digest")]`: it serializes lowercase hex and deserializes either a 64-character hex string or the old 32-number array, so existing summaries keep working and are written in hex at their next rewrite (an older nanocode ignores a hex digest's summaries with its existing warning and rebuilds them). The base shrinks 6% (11.62 to 10.90 MB). Measured with output/sessions-list as above on the plain-base copy and on the same copy with its digests converted to hex, the newest session, 3 interleaved runs, identical counts in every run: 542.2M user instructions before, 473.0M after (-13%), page faults 15,340 to 15,165; the old-format copy read by the new build costs what it did (547.8M); the same sessions listed. Checks as above. Files: crates/integrations/store-jsonl/src/summaries.rs.

Measured with output/sessions-list as above on the plain-base copy, the newest session, 3 interleaved runs: 581.8M user instructions before, 542.2M after (-6.8%), page faults 15,430 to 15,340. Checks as above. Files: crates/integrations/store-jsonl/src/sessions.rs.

- perf(store-jsonl): the session summaries file (`sessions/.summaries`) keeps its base as plain JSON instead of a zstd frame, and a base in the old compressed form is still read and is rewritten plain the next time the summaries change (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 CLI performance track: sessions at 14,600). Every listing reads the base; at 14,600 sessions it was a 1.5 MB frame of 11.6 MB of JSON, and decompressing it (`nanocode_zstd` `decode_and_execute_sequences` and `huf0::decompress_4x_using_dtable`) was 16% of the user instructions of listing after the change above. A plain base starts with `{`, which a compressed one (its first byte is the archive format, 1) never does, so `base` tells them apart, and `append` declines to extend a journal behind a compressed base, so `record` rewrites it plain (lazy migration). Rewrites no longer compress the whole map either, the cost a write paid each time the journal outgrew its base. The file grows about 7x (11.6 MB at 14,600 sessions, where fx's index.jsonl is 5.4 MB); an older nanocode reading a plain base ignores it with its existing warning and rebuilds summaries from the sessions. Measured with output/sessions-list on two copies of the same 14,600-session home, one with the base converted to plain JSON (the bytes `rewrite` writes), the newest session (`list_page` limit 1), 3 interleaved runs: 698.6M user instructions before, 581.8M after (-17%), kernel 220M both, page faults 15,700 to 15,430; on a still-compressed base the new build reads it at the old cost (698.5M); both list the same sessions. Checks as above. nanocode-ts does not run this crate. Files: crates/integrations/store-jsonl/src/summaries.rs.

- perf(sessions): `nc sessions` lists 100 sessions, newest first, unless `--limit N` asks for another number (fx's page, its largest `--limit`), and says on stderr when more remain; `--continue` and the terminal's session picker ask the catalog only for what they show (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 CLI performance track: sessions at 14,600). `SessionStore::list_page(workspace, limit, keep)` is new: it reads the store's summaries as `list` did, drops a summary whose `scope` (the workspace `listed_summary` writes) names another workspace before parsing its record, orders the rest by the summary's `updated_at_ms` (the record's, by construction), and parses records only until `limit` of them are in the workspace and pass `keep`. `list` is `list_page(None, usize::MAX, |_| true)`, with the same order and result. Before, every listing parsed all 14,600 records (`serde_json::from_str::<SessionRecord>`) and `nc sessions` printed all 14,590 of the bench workspace (1.5 MB); `latest_session` (`--continue`, `nc exec --continue`) and the picker filtered `list()`'s result. Measured with output/sessions-list as in the entry above, its `list` mode against `list_page` with the CLI's page (101, the page and one to tell whether more remain) and with 1 (`latest`), 3 interleaved runs, user instructions identical in every run: page 854.4M before, 699.7M after; newest session 811.2M to 698.6M (-14%); `list_page(Some(workspace), usize::MAX, ..)` prints the same 14,590 lines in the same order as `list` filtered by workspace (862.5M). `cargo clippy --no-deps -D warnings` of nanocode-durability (native and wasm32) and nanocode-cli pass. nanocode-ts runs `list`, whose result is unchanged. Files: crates/runtime/durability/src/catalog.rs, bin/nanocode/src/{lib.rs,cli.rs,sessions.rs,actions.rs}.

- perf(store-jsonl): listing a JSONL home's session files remembers the keys it has seen in a `HashSet` instead of searching the list built so far for each directory entry (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 CLI performance track: sessions at 14,600). `Sessions::files`, which `nc sessions`, `--continue`, the terminal's session picker and every other listing run first, skipped a key it had already listed (a session's `.jsonl` beside its `.jsonl.zst`) with `files.iter().any(|(listed, _, _)| *listed == key)`, so a home of n sessions compared about n²/2 keys: 106M string comparisons at 14,600 sessions, which `perf record` of `nc sessions` showed as about half of its samples (one loop plus `__memcmp_evex_movbe`). The first file seen for a key still wins, as before. Measured on dev-georgios with output/sessions-list (a release build against these crates that opens the bench/cli 14,600-session home with `JsonlStore::open_home_in_background`, lists it with `SessionStore::list` and prints the workspace's sessions) on a copy of ~/store14600/nc, `perf stat -e instructions:u,instructions:k,task-clock`, 3 interleaved runs each (user instructions identical in every run): listing 3,386.8M user instructions before, 854.4M after (-75%), task clock 494.8 to 181.1 ms (medians), the same 14,590 lines; the newest session alone 3,343.6M to 811.2M. `cargo clippy --offline -p nanocode-store-jsonl -p nanocode-durability --no-deps -- -D warnings`, native and wasm32, passes. nanocode-ts does not run this crate (it is native-only). Files: crates/integrations/store-jsonl/src/sessions.rs.

- `nanocode-turnlog` keeps stored bytes linear and cold reads at the tail: a snapshot commit archives the snapshot it supersedes in the same transaction, and the load query finds the last snapshot through a partial index (2026-11-14, Georgios: a cold open reads only the latest snapshot and its tail, and storage stays linear in session length). Why: with `snapshot_rows` 64 a durable-cloudflare session of 203 turns stored 6 snapshots of 917,952 B beside 276,091 B of rows, because every snapshot holds the whole state (the conversation) and none was ever removed, so stored bytes grew as length squared over n. The load statement read the tail twice (2k + 2 rows for a tail of k rows): its subquery `ORDER BY seq DESC LIMIT 1` walks every tail row back to the snapshot before the outer range reads them again. What changed: (1) `SqlLog::load` creates `nanocode_log_snapshots ON nanocode_log (scope, seq) WHERE substr(body, 1, 1) = 's'` with `IF NOT EXISTS` and the SQLite subquery names it with `INDEXED BY` (the planner picked the primary key without it, `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` in node:sqlite), so a cold load reads k + 2 rows. Building the index on an existing log reads its rows once. (2) A superseded snapshot becomes an archive row (tag `a`): the suffix of the snapshot's plain text that starts at a record boundary, holds every `Event` record of the snapshot and covers the last 32 KiB (`codec::WINDOW`, the deflate window that the following rows use as their dictionary), packed without a dictionary. `rows` treats it as a boundary, so `history` pages and the rows after it decode as before, and `load` never returns it because a newer snapshot follows it. The writer computes the suffix when it writes a snapshot and when `open` loads one (`Previous`), and archives only when the archive is smaller than the snapshot and needs no more parts. (3) `LogHost::append_compacting(scope, rows, Compaction { archived, dropped })` writes the snapshot rows, rewrites the archived rows and deletes the dropped parts in one transaction. Its default calls `append`, so other hosts keep fat snapshots and stay correct. `SqlLog` and `MemoryLog` implement it, and `append` is `append_compacting` with an empty compaction. Tried and not kept: a pointer row at seq 0 that names the last snapshot (costs a write on the first commit and an upsert per snapshot, and the partial index gives the same reads), and writing the tail into every snapshot so a cold open reads one row (it writes the whole state at every commit, so bytes written per turn grow with the session). Measured with durable-cloudflare output/turns.mjs (local workerd, `TURNS=1 LONG=5|43|200`, base and new runs interleaved, 3 cold opens per run, rows of the cold turn plus the warm turn after it), base = build-0624213 bundle with the integrator's `snapshot_rows: Some(64)` wasm, new = this SDK built for wasm32 (`cargo build --profile wasm`, `wasm-opt -O3` as scripts/build.mjs does) plus the nanocode-ts schema marker change: log statement rows at 8 turns 32/40/48 -> 16/20/24, at 46 turns 56/64/72 -> 29/33/37, at 203 turns 34/42/50 -> 18/22/26. Stored log bytes at 203 turns: 1,194,043 (412 r rows 276,091 + 6 s 917,952) -> 563,599 (412 r 275,261 + 1 s 256,017 + 5 a 32,321), SQLite file 1,777,664 -> 1,261,568 B. At 46 turns (one snapshot, nothing to archive) 138,905 -> 139,776. Warm turns are unchanged: reply 2 rows written, cell 2, timer 3, charge 3, 0 read. Cost per snapshot commit, measured in a miniflare probe: the snapshot row writes 2 rows (row and index entry) instead of 1, and the archive update reads 1 row and writes 1, so a snapshot commit costs 2 more written rows and 1 read row, once per n commits. nanocode-sim: `SimHost` implements `append_compacting` with a staged compaction that commits with the tick and drops on a crash (`Rows::tcompactions`, `Rows::view`), asserts that each archive is a suffix of the snapshot it replaces with the same events, and `--state-bytes N` pushes an N-byte host record per scope so snapshots exceed the window. New invariant: with `--state-bytes`, a scope stores at most one `s` row after every commit. Mutation `snapshot_kept` (the host ignores the compaction) fails 1,379 of 2,000 seeds (`sweep.sh 0 2000 2 --scenario turns --policy turnlog --snapshot-rows 4 --state-bytes 131072 --mutation snapshot_kept`), and the existing `snapshot_rows_ignored` still fails 1,801 of 2,000 with `--snapshot-rows 4`. Source mutation of `suffix` that drops the window (`while start == plain.len() || found < events`) fails 213 of 300 seeds with `--twice --snapshot-rows 4 --state-bytes 131072` (the next row does not decompress). Dropping the event clause (`while start > floor`) is not caught, since the simulator's hot events always fit inside the 32 KiB window. Checks (sim, seeds 0..2000, 2 jobs): `--twice`, `--twice --retain 0`, `--twice --snapshot-rows 4`, `--twice --retain 0 --snapshot-rows 0`, `--twice --snapshot-rows 3 --row-limit 1024`, `--twice --calm --snapshot-rows 2`, `--twice --snapshot-rows 4 --state-bytes 131072` and `--twice --retain 0 --snapshot-rows 2 --state-bytes 131072 --row-limit 4096` pass 2,000 of 2,000 with 0 panics (the last one in 698 s, since a 4 KiB row limit splits each 128 KiB snapshot into parts). durable-cloudflare `node scripts/drill.mjs` with the new bundle: 3 of 3 scenarios completed, no failures. `cargo check --offline --locked --lib -p nanocode-turnlog -p nanocode-agent`, `-p nanocode-turnlog --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `-p nanocode-agent -p nanocode-code-mode --features nanocode-code-mode/local-cells --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo +1.97.1 clippy --no-deps -- -D warnings -A clippy::useless_conversion` for nanocode-turnlog on both targets and nanocode-sim, rustfmt on the changed files. Files: crates/core/turnlog/src/{codec,host,lib,writer}.rs, bin/nanocode-sim/src/{disk,main,turnlog,turns}.rs.
- `OneLog::submit_buffered` admits a turn without its own row: the `Admitted` record and the queued event stay in the writer's buffer and become durable with the turn's next commit (the External call or timer wait of a cell, a cancel, or the finish), so a turn whose host acknowledges it only through an open event stream writes 1 row for a reply or a synchronous cell and 2 for a timer or `charge` cell, against 2 and 3 with `submit` (2026-11-14, Georgios: fewer SQLite rows per warm turn on durable-cloudflare). What each warm row was, on durable-cloudflare's local workerd (`output/turns.mjs`, every row an `INSERT INTO nanocode_log`, none in nanocode-ts tables): a reply or synchronous cell wrote `Point::Admission` (`OneLog::submit`) and `Point::Finish` (`close`), a timer cell also wrote `Point::Call` from `OneLogJournals::save` when the save arms the timer (it carries the model step's checkpoint and the cell header), and a `charge` cell also wrote `Point::Call` from `EffectGate::before`. `start` commits nothing on a warm object, and the model step's `Settle::Durable` commit writes no row outside recovery. Which rows a guarantee needs: the External call row and the timer row (no recovered turn asks the model again for a step whose cell waited, `cell_model_once`) and the finish row (a result a client saw is never replaced by a rerun) stay. The admission row is needed only when the host answers before the turn runs, as the 202 reply does. A host that answers with the turn's own event stream can lose the admission with the stream, and the client then submits the same request_id again, which `submit` and `submit_buffered` treat as new or existing by the log, so `submit` keeps the old behavior and `submit_buffered` is the opt-in. `submit_buffered` first calls `Lease::secure`, so after an open the floor row still lands before any event seq is published (the first turn after a cold open writes the floor row in place of the admission row, the same count as before). Not done: batching a finish with the next admission (the result is visible before the next admission and a crash would replace it with a rerun), and buffering on durable-vercel (its `Journal.place` can commit the placement in a batch before a buffered admission reaches the journal, which would lose the turn). nanocode-sim's cell turns (bin/nanocode-sim/src/cells.rs) now submit half of their turns buffered, expect 1 or 2 rows for a clean buffered turn plus the floor row after an open (`cell_rows`), and check the new invariant `admission_kept`: a turn acknowledged to its client (a `submit` that returned, or a buffered admission once a later append landed) is in the log after every crash. The mutation `ack_buffered_admission` acknowledges a buffered admission at once and is caught by 149 of seeds 0..400. Checks: `bin/nanocode-sim/sweep.sh` with `--scenario turns --policy turnlog`: seeds 0..3000 `--twice` passed 3000, 0..2000 `--retain 0 --twice` passed 2000, 0..2000 `--snapshot-rows 8 --twice` passed 2000, 3000..6000 passed 3000, 0 panics, `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-agent -p nanocode-turnlog` and the wasm32 check of nanocode-agent with `nanocode-code-mode/local-cells` pass, clippy (`cargo +1.97.1 clippy --locked --lib -p nanocode-agent` and `-p nanocode-sim --no-deps`, `-D warnings -A clippy::useless_conversion`) passes, and with a nanocode-ts pack of this change durable-cloudflare `npm run drill` passes charge, waiting and deploys (3 of 3) and durable-vercel `npm run drill` passes 8 of 8, the 4 waiting runs included. Measurements (durable-cloudflare `output/turnsby.mjs`, the integrator's `output/turns.mjs` with per-statement row deltas, TURNS=5, local workerd, interleaved build-0624213 against this change): warm rows written per turn, reply, synchronous cell, timer cell, charge cell, mean of 5 turns, in each of 3 runs (2 rounds of turnsby.mjs and one full turns.mjs): before 2, 2, 3, 3 in every run, after 1, 1, 2, 2 in every run, rows read 0 in both. Statement bytes per turn fall slightly (reply 868, 882, 879 to 835, 833, 823 B, charge 4,865, 4,855, 4,850 to 4,822, 4,814, 4,793 B). Turn times are within the noise of the shared machine (reply 18, 33, 24 ms against 59, 35, 21 ms, synchronous cell 29, 66, 52 against 70, 51, 39 ms, timer 93, 99, 83 against 96, 99, 91 ms, charge 3,054, 3,052, 3,046 against 3,087, 3,063, 3,038 ms with its 3 s confirmation). The long session of turns.mjs (43 synchronous cell turns, then 3 workerd restarts): a cold turn plus the next warm turn write 4 rows against 5 and read 156, 162, 168 rows against 240, 248, 256, since the log holds fewer rows, with cold turns of 231, 292, 247 ms against 231, 314, 234 ms. - fix(cli): a custom model's context window comes from the `context_window` of its /v1/models entry when `--context-window` is not given, instead of the harness default of 272,000 (Codex) or 200,000 (Claude) (2026-11-14). The Tempo gateway lists `context_window` on all 27 of its ids (2026-11-14), and the defaults are wrong both ways for the open models: @cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.7-code has 262,144, below the Codex default, so a Codex-harness session would compact only after the provider's limit, and the vercel and boundless Kimi K3/K3.1 ids have 1,000,000 and 1,048,576, so the Claude harness compacted at 167,000 tokens (200,000 less its 33,000 reserve). `fetch_models` reads the field; `custom_endpoint::apply` keeps it only for custom ids (not ids that parse as a known Codex or Claude model, such as @cf/zai-org/glm-5.3, which keep their own windows and caps); both harnesses' configure hooks look it up by the model the agent is built for, through new `CodexBuilder::selected_model` and `ClaudeBuilder::selected_model` getters, so subagents and `/model` switches get their own model's window; `--context-window` still wins. Harbor arms pass `--context-window`, so benchmark runs are unchanged; a plain `nc exec` on the gateway's GLM-5.3-Flash and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash ids (custom, listed at 1,048,576) now uses that window. Checked with a local mock whose first reply calls Bash and reports 180,000 input tokens, and the debug binary: on the Claude harness with vercel/moonshotai/kimi-k3.1-pro (listed at 1,000,000) the binary before started a compaction (`compaction summary did not end normally`, since the mock answered the summary request with a tool call), after it sent the tool result and ended with `OK` in two requests; nowindow/model, listed without a window, still compacts. The Codex harness uses the window as its turn-start compaction limit for custom models, which needs a second turn, and in the debug build `--continue` is cut short by a panic in the JSONL store (crates/core/zstd/src/encode/bits.rs:25, shift left with overflow), so that side was not measured end to end. Before: `{cmd: ls` gave `failed to encode exec_command arguments: key must be a string at line 1 column 2`; write_stdin to an id never issued gave `unknown logical process session` (the routed tool's lookup); write_stdin to session 3 after it exited gave `write_stdin failed: Unknown process id 4`, the internal id behind the logical one; and `{"cmd":"echo hi","bogus":1}` was refused with serde's unknown-field list where stock runs the command (~/hill/analysis/codex-parity.md section 5, scenarios `badcalls`, `poll`, `stdin`). - fix(codex): when a custom model's byte budget is what cuts an exec_command or write_stdin output, the marker counts the characters removed (`…N chars truncated…`), as Codex 0.162.1 writes, instead of `…N tokens truncated…` (2026-11-14). - perf(tui): the terminal interface reads agent events itself instead of through a forwarding task, and a Responses stream publishes held display deltas before any other event and yields to the worker when its cooperative budget ends (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 latency SLA: rendered tok/s equal to provider tok/s). Traced on dev-georgios (marks for socket chunk, delta publish, forwarder, TUI receive and frame, `bench/sla` 20,000 tokens unpaced): the TUI runtime has one worker (the entry of 2026-11-13), and `App::ready` spawned a task that copied `AgentEvents` into the app channel. A Responses connection task that drains buffered SSE events never returns Pending while the socket has data, so that task, and the Tokio timer for the next frame, waited behind it: published deltas reached the TUI in bursts 5 to 30 socket reads (2 to 6 ms) after they were published, and frame deadlines fired up to 9 ms late. Three changes. First, `App` keeps `events: Option<(u64, AgentEvents)>` and `event_loop` selects on it beside the app channel (the generation check is unchanged, `AppEvent::Agent` is gone), so a publish on the worker wakes the main thread directly. Second, `receive` in crates/backends/codex/client/src/tower/stream.rs flushes the pending display delta when the decoded event is not a text, reasoning or tool-input delta: the last tokens of a reply waited until `output_item.done` (the whole reply text, parsed after `output_text.done` and `content_part.done`, which repeat it), 1 to 9 ms after they arrived. Third, natively, each received event takes one unit of Tokio's cooperative budget (`tokio::task::coop::consume_budget`), and the pending delta is flushed before the budget runs out, so the connection task yields after the runtime's own budget instead of after 128 socket reads. The TUI also draws at once on `assistant.message`, as it does on the run's end. Measured with nanocode-ts `bench/sla/run.ts` (mock, lanes `nc@base,nc-claude@base,nc@fix,nc-claude@fix` interleaved, 10 samples x 2 turns, the bench processes at SCHED_RR 5 because the machine ran at load 100 to 270; base is 62a0936e4), p50 / p99 of tail (provider's last write to last token drawn, ms) and rendered/provider ratio p50 / p1: Responses unpaced 20k tail 6.87 / 8.84 -> 4.64 / 6.24, ratio 0.848 / 0.804 -> 0.873 / 0.824 (provider 720k to 750k tok/s); Claude unpaced tail 3.83 / 5.48 -> 3.02 / 4.16, ratio 0.920 / 0.857 -> 0.944 / 0.908; paced 100k tok/s Responses tail 5.83 / 6.86 -> 3.89 / 4.98, ratio 0.974 -> 0.983, Claude 2.80 / 5.51 -> 2.08 / 2.70, ratio 0.988 -> 0.992; paced 20k tok/s Responses tail 5.94 / 14.22 -> 4.01 / 5.84, ratio 0.995 -> 0.996, Claude 2.82 / 3.55 -> 1.88 / 2.70, ratio 0.998 -> 0.999. Not reached: 0.99 unpaced. The fixture stamps the last token when `res.write` returns, while Node still holds the bytes, and the trace shows the last socket chunks reaching the client 1 to 3.5 ms later with the client idle before them; at 750k tok/s the provider window is 27 ms, so 0.99 leaves 0.27 ms for receive, parse and one frame. Commands: `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli`, `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-codex-client --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-cli -p nanocode-backend-codex-client` (nothing in the changed files). - fix(codex): models without OpenAI's remote compaction (custom Responses endpoints such as the leaderboard's DeepSeek and GLM, and the built-in GLM, Kimi and MiMo) compact locally at 90% of the context window with upstream's summarization prompt, as stock Codex 0.162.1 does with `remote_compaction = "unsupported"` (2026-11-14). Evidence: ~/hill/analysis/codex-parity.md section 1. In the parity mock's `compact` scenario (each step adds about 11 KB of output, window 16,000 tokens) stock sends 19 requests, four of them compactions (requests 3, 7, 11 and 15: the whole history plus a user message with upstream's `SUMMARIZATION_PROMPT`, `tools: []`, `parallel_tool_calls: false`) and restarts the history as developer context, environment context, the user messages and one user message `SUMMARY_PREFIX + "\n" + summary`; nanocode never compacted (`auto_compact_token_limit` returned a limit only for the five OpenAI models, and the only compaction it knew was the server's `compaction_trigger` item), so with `CTXLIMIT=16000` its 5th request got `context_length_exceeded` and it exited 1 while stock finished. Change: the threshold is 90% of the window for every model (`context_window_compact_token_limit`, the configured limit still wins); for a model outside `remote_compaction` the compaction request ends with `local_trigger()` (upstream's prompt, byte for byte from the stock capture) instead of `compaction_trigger`, is sent without tools and with `parallel_tool_calls: false`, skips the gateway's inline-compaction check, and its reply's last assistant `output_text` becomes the summary message that `install_history` puts after the retained user messages (earlier summary messages are no longer retained, and the retained user messages get upstream's 20,000-token budget, `COMPACT_USER_MESSAGE_MAX_TOKENS`, instead of the remote path's 64,000); when a local compaction request itself exceeds the window, the oldest history item (with its call or output) is dropped and the request retried, as upstream's inline compaction does. Not done: retrying a generation request that got `context_length_exceeded` mid-turn. Stock 0.162.1 does not do that either: with `CTXLIMIT=12000` under a 16,000 window it fails the turn and exits 1 on both an HTTP 400 and an SSE `response.failed` (`Codex ran out of room in the model's context window`), and nanocode keeps the same behavior (the turn fails and `force_compaction` makes the next turn compact). A prototype that compacted and retried in `drive_session` compacted correctly but then failed durability (`cannot advance past an unsettled effect`), since a failed model step has no recorded outcome; doing it needs a failure outcome for model steps. Measured with the parity2 mock (~/wt/compact-parity: mock3.py adds the SSE overflow, cmp.py compares the requests): nanocode's prompt is 6.4 KB (1,612 mock tokens) smaller than stock's (its 3 tool schemas against stock's 7 and its permissions message against stock's skills message, separate parity items), so at window 16,000 it compacts one step later (requests 4, 9, 14 of 18); with the window lowered by that difference (14,209) all 19 requests match stock's one by one: same compaction positions, compaction requests with `tools: []` and `parallel_tool_calls: false`, the prompt message byte-identical, every non-developer item identical apart from ids, wall times and the known chars/tokens truncation marker, and the summary message byte-identical. With `CTXLIMIT=16000` nanocode now finishes (18 requests, exit 0) instead of exiting 1 at request 5. `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-codex-client -p nanocode-backend-codex`, natively and for wasm32-unknown-unknown, and `cargo build --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode` passed without warnings. - fix(claude): a tool call whose input is not valid JSON is answered with Claude Code's InputValidationError and the turn goes on, instead of ending the session (2026-11-14, parity finding H1 in ~/hill/analysis/claude-parity.md). When a model streamed `input_json_delta` fragments that did not parse and the response was not cut at max_tokens, `finish` in crates/backends/claude/client/src/lib.rs returned `ClaudeError::Json`, which is not retryable, so `nanocode exec --harness claude` exited 1 with `nanocode: Messages JSON: EOF while parsing a string at line 1 column 29` (parity3 scenario `bad`, step 5: 5 requests, then exit). GLM-5.3-Flash produced such input in 2 of 63 stock-claude GLM trials (cmp2 adaptive-rejection-sampler a1-t1, 23,464 bytes; regex-chess a2-t3, 1,828 bytes), and Claude Code recovered both times and finished. Claude Code 2.1.300 (its bundled cli: `BFt="__unparsedToolInput"`, the stream assembler and `_kr`) keeps the call in history as `{"__unparsedToolInput":{"raw":<the input's first 2048 UTF-16 units>,"len":<its UTF-16 length>}}` and, before checking the input against the tool's schema, answers it (is_error) with `<tool_use_error>InputValidationError: <tool> was called with input that could not be parsed as JSON.\nYou sent (first <n> of <len> bytes): <raw's first 200 UTF-16 units>\nCommon causes: unescaped backslashes in file paths (use / or \\), unescaped control characters, or truncated output. Retry with valid JSON.</tool_use_error>`. Its cut (`ne`) counts UTF-16 units and drops a high surrogate left alone at the end; here the cut takes whole chars while their UTF-16 length stays within the limit, which gives the same text. `finish` now builds that input (serde_json keeps insertion order, so `raw` precedes `len` as in stock), and `durable_tool` answers a call whose input is exactly that object (one key, `raw` a string, `len` an integer) with that text, after the interrupt and cancel checks and only when the tool has a handler, so an unknown tool still gets the unknown-tool answer, as stock looks the tool up first. A call cut at max_tokens keeps its existing text (finding L2), and input that parses but is not an object still fails with `ClaudeError::Protocol`. - deps(sync): nanocode-sync carries the futures, streams and sinks nanocode used from futures-util, so futures-util, futures-core, futures-sink, futures-task and slab leave (2026-11-14). What: `nanocode_sync::future` (BoxFuture, LocalBoxFuture, Either, FutureExt with map, boxed, boxed_local, shared, now_or_never, catch_unwind, poll_unpin, left_future and right_future; select, join, join_all, select_all, Shared, abortable with Abortable, AbortHandle, AbortRegistration and Aborted; std's ready and poll_fn), `nanocode_sync::stream` (Stream, FusedStream, TryStream, StreamExt with next, map, filter, filter_map, then, chain, take, fuse, collect, buffered, boxed, boxed_local, poll_next_unpin and split; TryStreamExt with map_ok, map_err, try_next and try_fold; BoxStream, unfold, try_unfold, once, iter, empty, FuturesUnordered, FuturesOrdered, SplitStream and SplitSink) and `nanocode_sync::sink` (Sink, SinkExt with send, feed, flush, close, with and the poll_*_unpin calls); the traits and AtomicWaker are re-exported at the crate root. AtomicWaker lives in nanocode-sys, the crate allowed unsafe code, as futures-core's algorithm. The 23 crates that named futures_util now name nanocode_sync, `pin_mut!` became `std::pin::pin!` and `noop_waker_ref()` became `Waker::noop()`. Why: DEPENDENCIES.md's goal of nothing outside the async baseline; nanocode used a small part of futures-util, and the rest came with slab and three more crates. Equal: every combinator polls in futures-util 0.3.32's order. FuturesUnordered polls its futures in the order they were woken through a FIFO ready queue (a tokio unbounded channel of Arc'd tasks, so wakes from any thread stay lock-free) and yields after two futures woke themselves or after polling as many futures as it held, as futures-util does; FuturesOrdered is that set with a binary heap of finished outputs; join_all polls up to 30 futures together and more through FuturesOrdered; buffered(0) never pulls (futures-util loops while the queue is shorter than the window); select_all swap_removes the winner; Shared keeps the future in an AtomicBox that the polling handle takes, the output in a OnceLock and one AtomicWaker per handle in a copy-on-write map that the inner waker wakes, moves the output out without a clone in the last handle, and poisons the other handles when the poll panics; split's halves take the value out of an AtomicBox and wake the other half when they put it back. Different: with no unsafe pin projection, an adapter boxes what it wraps once (`Pin<Box<S>>`) and keeps the future it waits on in a `Pin<Box<Option<Fut>>>` reset in place for each item, and join and join_all box each future; every adapter is Unpin; FilterMap and With give get_mut only over an Unpin inner; Either is a Future only over Unpin halves and not a Stream or Sink; there is no FusedFuture. nanocode-sim's tidy allows nanocode-sync's own definitions of FuturesUnordered, FuturesOrdered and join_all (24 uses); simulated crates still go through InOrder and join_in_order. Downstream: the Stream, Sink and extension traits on nanocode's public types (event streams, ResponseStream and BoxStream, WebSocketStream's Stream and Sink, `nanocode_http::Body::wrap_stream`, which takes a `nanocode_sync::TryStream`) and AbortHandle, Shared and BoxFuture are nanocode_sync's now, so tempoxyz/pyramid-core and tempoxyz/pyramid import nanocode_sync's traits where they call StreamExt or SinkExt on nanocode's streams or pass streams into nanocode. Bench (output/futures-equality bench, median of 5 interleaved runs of 20,000, ns, futures-util against nanocode-sync, on the shared 5-core Hand at load 9.6): select of two ready futures 1/1, join_all of 8 ready 38/286, FuturesUnordered draining 64 ready 3,170/8,412, map+filter+collect over 1,000 items 2,591/2,222, unfold of 1,000 items 2,749/4,919, Shared with 3 handles 135/1,120; ours pays one allocation per boxed future and per task, and Shared's copy-on-write waker map per handle. cargo check --locked --workspace --all-targets passes; cargo clippy --all-targets on the changed crates adds no warning (the one in a new file fixed); wasm32-unknown-unknown cargo check --lib passes for nanocode-sys, -sync, -types, -agent-core, -durability-core, -http, -websocket, -mcp-http, -code-mode, -subagents, -durability, -tool-host, -backend-claude-client, -backend-claude, -backend-codex-client and -backend-codex (nanocode-agent fails for wasm on master too); rustfmt --check finds no new difference in a changed file; nanocode-sim release --tidy is clean and sweep.sh 0 1000 with 2 workers passes 1,000 of 1,000 with 0 panics for --scenario runtime --store kv, --store memory, --store kv --twice and --wire http. - fix(claude): headless (exec) root sessions wait for running background Bash jobs and wake the model with Claude Code's task notification, instead of killing them when the model ends its turn (2026-11-14). Claude Code 2.1.300 in print mode keeps going while a background shell runs (`park`: `holdForBackgroundShells`, flag `tengu_tidy_sloth` default on). Each completion is queued as a new user message `<system-reminder>\n` + `J3e` (the `[SYSTEM NOTIFICATION - NOT USER INPUT]` preamble) + the `<task-notification>` + `\n</system-reminder>`. The wait is bounded by the shell's own deadline: `CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS` (default `lPt=600000` after the last turn) does not apply while any shell's `deadlineAt + 5000` is ahead (`jk`), and a shell that reaches its deadline is killed with "was stopped after reaching its background time limit". nanocode's exec ran headless sessions with `ends_with_turn`: it told the model the job "is terminated when you give your final response", reaped it at turn cleanup and exited. The parity mock's `bg` scenario made 7 requests where stock made 8 (~/hill/analysis/claude-parity.md H2). Now `Delivery` (claude_bash.rs) is one of `Prompted` (interactive root, as before), `Held` (headless root) or `EndsWithTurn` (subagents, as before). A held session tells the model "You will be notified when it completes." (stock's text) and steers each notification into its turn wrapped exactly as above. It also gets a `turn_hold` hook (agent.rs) that runs when the model ends its turn with no steer pending: it waits until a notification is steered in (the loop then continues, as for any steer) or no background job is left owing one (`Jobs::busy`: phase Background and not aborted without a result). It returns at once when there are none and cancels with the turn. The hook takes its baseline and subscribes before the loop checks for pending steers, so a notification that lands in between is not missed. Every nanocode background job already has a deadline (`timeout`, default 600000 ms and at most 7,200,000, or 600000 after a foreground timeout), which is stock's bound. Not done: stock's 600000 ms ceiling for shells without a deadline (nanocode has none); nanocode keeps its own output tail ("Output:\n...", "The command printed nothing.") inside the notification, and mid-turn notifications stay separate user messages (L4), now with the wrapper. Measured on 884c2d3 (before: that commit's debug build; after: it plus this change) with a copy of the parity mock (~/wt/bgjobs-parity: `run3b.py` with `NC=<binary>` and `TAG`, plus scenarios `bgnever`, a `sleep 100000` with `run_in_background` and `timeout: 4000` followed by an end_turn, and `plain`, one Bash call then DONE). `bg`: stock 8 requests, before 7, after 8; the woken request ends with the assistant's "Waiting for the background job." then the notification (stock 894 chars, after 920: longer task ids and paths plus "Output:\nlate-bg"). The background tool result is 313 chars, down from 539, against stock's 303 in the same harness (same text, longer id and path). `bgnever`: stock 3 requests in 5.2 s with a `killed` notification, before 2 requests in 0.1 s (job killed), after 3 requests in 4.1 s with the same `killed` summary and note. `plain`: both requests byte-identical before and after (15,619 and 15,981 bytes, ids normalized). `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude`, natively and for wasm32-unknown-unknown, passed with no warnings; `cargo build --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode`. Files: crates/backends/claude/src/{agent.rs,claude_bash.rs,defaults.rs}.
- fix(claude): direct Bash output, timeouts and tool-result bounds follow Claude Code 2.1.300 (2026-11-14). Three gaps on the parity mock (~/hill/analysis/claude-parity.md M1-M3). Output: nanocode kept up to 30,000 bytes of each stream, stdout then stderr, so a 282 KB `seq 1 50000` cost 30,132 characters in every later request and 3,000 interleaved stdout/stderr lines came back as 47,921 characters with the stderr lines after all the stdout lines; Claude Code runs `eval '<command>' < /dev/null` with stdout and stderr on one file and, when a successful command prints more than 30,000 bytes, answers `<persisted-output>\nOutput too large (<size>). Full output saved to: <file>\n\nPreview (first 2KB):\n<preview>\n...\n</persisted-output>`, the preview being the output without leading blank lines and trailing whitespace cut at 2,000 UTF-16 units, or at the last newline in them when that lies past unit 1,000 (`rlt`, `QRe=2000` and `exe` in the 2.1.300 binary); a failing command's error text is cut to its first and last 5,000 characters with `\n\n... [N characters truncated] ...\n\n` once it is over 11,024 (`Wc`, `nan=1e4`, `_R=1024`). Timeouts: nanocode moved every timed-out command to the background; Claude Code does that too, except for a command whose first word is `sleep` (`Urs`, `Nrs=["sleep"]`), which it kills and answers with `Exit code 143\nCommand timed out after <rn(ms)>` followed by what it printed (seconds floored below a minute, else `<m>m <s>s`), and it uses the maximum for a `timeout` above 600000 without a note. Bounds: every tool result was middle-truncated at 12,000 tokens, so a Read of a 3,001-line, 87.8 KB file lost lines 866-2201 inside one line, below Read's own 25,000-token cap. Change, in direct (not exec-cell) Bash calls only: the wrapper adds `2>&1`, so the executor's stdout holds both streams in order; a completed call whose output was cut (the task output file holds it all) and exited 0 gets the persisted-output block naming that file and its size (text_files' `size_text`, which is Claude Code's `Zt`), one that failed shows its first 30,000 bytes as Claude Code does, and a failing call's text gets the 10,000-character head and tail cut; a timed-out command starting with `sleep` is stopped, its output file read back and the 143 answer returned; the over-maximum timeout note stays for exec cells and background calls. agent.rs bounds exec and wait results at 12,000 tokens as before, leaves Read unbounded (it bounds itself, at 25,000 tokens or, with allow_large, the room left) and bounds other tools at 25,000 (Claude Code's Read and MCP output cap). Code Mode is unchanged: exec-cell Bash calls keep separate streams, 128 KiB per stream with cut notices, background on timeout and the 12,000-token exec bound. Measured with a copy of the parity mock (~/wt/bashout-parity: run.py takes NC, and two extra scenarios out2 and timeout2/timeout3), stock Claude Code 2.1.300 against nanocode before (af6c014) and after, tool_result characters with paths and task ids normalized: out 2121/2121/2120/8/2118 stock, 30132/30132/30130/8/47921 before, the stock bytes after; out2 (merged small output, failing small and 288 KB output, exactly 30,000 bytes, 40,001 bytes of `\u00e9`, leading blank lines, 106 KB on stderr only, a newline before unit 1,000) 9 of 9 results byte-identical to stock after (before: `a\nc\nb` for `echo a; echo b >&2; echo c`, 30,148 for the failing 288 KB output against stock's 10,044); timeout `Exit code 143\nCommand timed out after 1s` and `fast` as stock (before 444 and 115 characters); timeout2 `sleep 5` with timeout 2999 gives `Command timed out after 2s` as stock, and `echo partial; ...; sleep 5` still moves to the background as stock does; read 87,791 characters for the 3,001-line file as stock (before 48,023). Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude-tools -p nanocode-backend-claude`, natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo build --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode`. Not done: the auto-background message's own text ("You will be notified when it completes...") and Read's error texts, which other entries cover. Files: crates/backends/claude/tools/src/tools/bash.rs, crates/backends/claude/src/{claude_bash.rs,agent.rs}.
- refactor(platform): every `tokio::time`, `tokio::spawn` and `tokio::runtime::Handle::try_current` call outside nanocode-platform goes through it (2026-11-14, tokio replacement step 0 of /home/hand/plans/plan-22.json). nanocode-platform gains `sleep_until`, `timeout_at`, `Sleep` (`after`, `until`, `deadline`, `reset`; `Unpin`, for the `select!` loops that move a deadline), `Interval` with `interval`, `interval_at` and `MissedTickBehavior::{Burst, Delay}`, and `Handle` (`try_current`, `spawn`, `enter`) with `TryCurrentError`; `sleep_until`, `timeout_at`, `Sleep` and `Interval` exist on wasm32 too, over the Host. Without a Host nothing changes: `sleep_until` and `timeout_at` call tokio's, `Sleep` holds a boxed tokio `Sleep` and resets it in place, `Handle::try_current` answers tokio's handle and its error text, and `Interval` keeps tokio's tick rule over `Sleep`, the 5 ms late-tick tolerance included (`MISSED_TICK_TOLERANCE`). With a Host they go to the Host, so the code that read tokio's clock directly (the tool runtime's heartbeats and handshakes, the Codex idle timer, the sandbox's audit tick, Claude's Bash, session locks, splice, MCP, MPP and computer timeouts) runs on the simulator's virtual time when one is installed, and the `Instant`s these sites compare come from `nanocode_platform::now()` rather than `tokio::time::Instant::now()`. `Handle::try_current` answers the Host first, so the seven "host, else tokio's handle, else ..." branches (handle.rs, owned.rs, Actor::spawn, the Mailbox hand-off, child journal, memory and session drivers) become one call; claude_tools' guard cancellation, the Codex executor's driver, agent-host's runners and MPP's background saves, which asked tokio alone, now reach an installed Host too. The 29 `tokio::pin!` become `std::pin::pin!`, and the three grouped `spawn` imports (lanes, session locks, the egress proxy) call `nanocode_platform::spawn_task`. tidy: the `Handle::try_current` ban becomes a ban on `tokio::runtime` (grouped imports included, so the platform's own `Handle` passes), the `tokio::time`, `tokio::spawn` and `Handle::try_current` allowances leave, and so do the `Instant::now` allowances of claude_bash, splice and session locks; the one `tokio::runtime` allowance is shared_store's own current_thread runtime when no Host is installed. Left for the executor steps: computer's Linux `Exec` (its own tokio runtime and `block_on`) and process output's `Handle::current().block_on` from a blocking thread. Checks: `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli -p nanocode-sim -p nanocode --all-targets`; `cargo clippy` on the same reports nothing in the touched files; `cargo check --locked --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` for nanocode-platform, -sync, -agent-core, -durability, -backend-claude, -backend-codex, -backend-codex-client, -code-mode, -subagents, -http, -mcp-http and -websocket; `nanocode-sim --tidy` clean; `nanocode-sim --seeds 1..150 --scenario runtime --twice` passes 149 of 149 with identical runs, as do `--scenario runtime` and `--scenario runtime --wire http` (release build). Packages: `cargo metadata --locked` unchanged. Files: crates/core/platform/src/{native.rs,host.rs,interval.rs,lib.rs}, bin/nanocode-sim/src/tidy.rs and 66 call sites.

- fix(claude): a 402 from the Tempo gateway's payment layer is retried like a server error (2026-11-14). The gateway answers some requests with a 402 that is not about the account: its payment Durable Object timing out (`/reference#description/payment-failed`, "Durable Object is overloaded. Requests queued for too long."), or a voucher race between a key's concurrent requests (`https://paymentauth.org/problems/verification-failed`, "voucher cumulativeAmount must be strictly greater than highest accepted voucher", and `https://paymentauth.org/problems/session/delta-too-small`), often right after its 500s. The Claude client retried 408, 409, 429 and 5xx only, as Claude Code 2.1.300 does, so the first such 402 ended the run: in cmp2, 9 GLM and 29 DeepSeek nc-claude trials ended on their first and only 402, all of them payment-failed (10 GLM and 33 DeepSeek stock Claude Code trials met the same 402, which it does not retry either; stock Codex reconnects). Across every harbor run's nanocode stderr the 402 problem types were payment-failed (79), delta-too-small (13), verification-failed (6) and `https://paymentauth.org/problems/session/insufficient-balance` (3), the last a real lack of funds that retrying does not fix. `ClaudeError::is_transient` now also counts a 402 whose problem-details `type` is one of the first three, so it gets Claude Code's backoff (500 ms doubling to 32 s) within the 11 attempts; an `x-should-retry` header still decides first, and every other 402, insufficient balance included, still ends the turn. Measured against ~/hill/retrymock (a copy of mock.py with the payment-failed, delta-too-small and insufficient-balance bodies added) (`run.sh <binary> claude <plan> <tag>`), master af6c014 against a debug build with the change: a verification-failed, payment-failed or delta-too-small 402 then success, 1 post and failed before, 2 posts and success after; an insufficient-balance 402 then success, 1 post and failed for both; nine 502s then a verification-failed 402, 10 posts and failed after 147 s before, 11 posts and success after 184 s after, and the same with a payment-failed 402 (11 posts, success, 184 s). Stock Claude Code 2.1.300 fails both plans (1 post; 10 posts). A 409 then success takes 2 posts and succeeds for both builds, as before. `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude-client`, natively and for wasm32-unknown-unknown, passed. Files: crates/backends/claude/client/src/lib.rs.
- perf(turnlog): the fold keeps the bytes of its in-memory events as a running total instead of summing every event on each commit (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 nanocode-ts per-turn CPU). `Lease::commit` asks `Fold::hot_bytes` on every commit whether the events held in memory outgrow the state (the boundary-row rule), and `hot_bytes` walked all of `events` to add up their lengths. `Fold::hot_bytes` is now a field: an event record adds its length when `apply` pushes it, and `seal`, the one place events leave, recounts what it keeps. output/turnlog-replay (both sessions of the stored nanocode-ts log replayed through `TurnLog`, `perf stat -e instructions:u`, three interleaved runs each, dev-georgios): 3,771.4M instructions before, 3,754.5M after (-0.45%, identical in every run), the same stored bytes and fold digests.
