- RustPython's host layer builds for Windows again: rustpython-host_env's WMI query calls the BSTR functions itself and its errno table names the WinSock values, so rustpython-host_env, rustpython-vm and rustpython-stdlib check for x86_64-pc-windows-gnu and x86_64-pc-windows-msvc (2026-11-13). Before, `cargo check --locked --lib -p rustpython-host_env --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` failed with 5 errors: crates/patches/rustpython-host_env/src/wmi.rs called `crate::ctypes::{wcslen, sys_alloc_string_len, sys_free_string}`, which exist only with the `ctypes` feature, and that feature needs libffi, which is not in the lock. wmi.rs now has its own `wcslen` (count units up to the NUL, as ctypes' did through widestring's `from_ptr_str`) and `sys_alloc_string_len` and calls SysAllocStringLen and SysFreeString from windows-sys, the same calls with the same NULL and length checks. With that fixed, rustpython-vm failed with 30 errors (exceptions.rs and stdlib/errno.rs): libc 0.2.191 now defines the CRT's EWOULDBLOCK, ETIMEDOUT and 32 more socket errno values for Windows (EWOULDBLOCK is 140), so crates/patches/rustpython-host_env/src/errno.rs's `pub use libc::*` and `pub use wsa::*` re-exported two values under each name, which rustc reports as 25 ambiguous-glob-re-export warnings in host_env and as errors where the names are used. errno.rs now re-exports the 34 names of its `wsa` module by name, which shadows libc's glob, so each is the WinSock value (EWOULDBLOCK is 10035, WSAEWOULDBLOCK), as RustPython intended and as CPython's errno module gives on Windows. Nothing else changes; no package enters or leaves. This is the base for checking the Windows dependency replacements that follow, which could not be compiled before. Commands, all clean apart from warnings that were there before: `cargo metadata --locked`; `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli`; `cargo check --locked --lib -p rustpython-host_env -p rustpython-vm -p rustpython-stdlib` with `--target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` and `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`; `cargo clippy` of the same three for x86_64-pc-windows-gnu (host_env and stdlib have no warnings; vm has 4 dead-code warnings, `WindowsSysResult` and `without_winerror`, unused on Windows before this change too); `cargo check --locked --lib` and `cargo clippy --locked --lib` of rustpython-host_env natively and for wasm32-unknown-unknown, and of rustpython-vm and rustpython-stdlib natively and `cargo check` for wasm32-unknown-unknown (the warnings there, 7 ruff_python_ast cfg names, nanocode-sys webp `const fn` and two vm wasm unused items, are on r4-deps too).
- nanocode-observability's log bridge leaves, and log 0.4.33 leaves the lock and every target's graph (2026-11-13, Georgios: ~0 third-party dependencies). The bridge (crates/integrations/observability/src/log_bridge.rs, 211 lines) installed a `log::Log` that turned log records from dependencies into tracing events with `log.target`, `log.module_path`, `log.file` and `log.line` fields, and `normalize` let the compact, pretty and JSON formatters print those fields as the event's target, file and line. Since nanocode-http replaced reqwest and hyper (7e91e67f4) and the previous commit moved rustls-platform-verifier to tracing, no crate in any target's graph names log (`cargo metadata --locked --filter-platform` for x86_64 and aarch64 Linux and macOS, Android, iOS, Windows and wasm32), so the bridge could receive nothing. `init` no longer calls `log::set_logger` and `log::set_max_level`; `event_meta` reads the event's own metadata, which is what it returned for every event that was not a bridged record; the three formatters stop skipping fields named `log.*`, which only bridged records carried (no tracing call in the workspace names such a field). The workspace's `log` entry and the crate's dependency leave. Output for every event the workspace emits is the same, since `normalize` returned None for all of them. Commands: `cargo metadata --locked`, `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli`, `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-observability`, `cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-observability --lib`. Third-party packages after this commit (and after the RustPython commits before it): x86_64 Linux 80 to 79, aarch64 macOS 83 to 82, wasm32 60, Windows 87 to 86; outside the accepted set only base64 (named by our crates, replaced by the simd round's own base64) and on Windows RustPython's host layer dependencies remain.
- The patched rustls-platform-verifier reports through tracing's macros instead of log's, and its `cert-logging` feature and the optional base64 dependency behind it leave (2026-11-13, Georgios: ~0 third-party dependencies). Since nanocode-http replaced reqwest and hyper (7e91e67f4), nothing third-party in any target's graph names log: only this crate and nanocode-observability's log bridge do, so this is the first of two steps that take log out of the lock. crates/patches/rustls-platform-verifier/src/verification/{others,apple,macos,windows}.rs: the eleven `log::error!`, `log::warn!` and `log::debug!` calls (a failed verification, ignored and loaded platform roots, unreadable keychains) are the same `tracing::` calls with the same messages; Cargo.toml trades `log = "0.4"` for `tracing = { version = "0.1.44", default-features = false, features = ["std"] }`, which the workspace already builds. `log_server_cert`, which logged each end-entity certificate in base64 only when `cert-logging` was enabled (nothing enabled it), and its four call sites leave, with the feature, so Cargo.lock no longer records base64 for this crate. What differs: these events are now native tracing events whose target is the module path (`rustls_platform_verifier::verification::others` and so on), with file and line in their metadata, where the log bridge turned each record into a `log event` with `log.target`, `log.module_path`, `log.file` and `log.line` fields that the formatters folded back into the same target, file and line; the text, level and filters are the same. Commands: `cargo metadata --locked`, `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli`, `cargo check --locked --lib -p rustls-platform-verifier -p nanocode-tls` natively and for aarch64-apple-darwin (on gak-9) and x86_64-pc-windows-msvc where ring builds, `cargo clippy --locked -p rustls-platform-verifier --lib`. Packages per target are unchanged by this commit (log is still named by nanocode-observability).
- rustpython-codegen and rustpython-vm emit their diagnostics with tracing's macros instead of log's, and log leaves the wasm32 build (2026-11-13). Both crates drop `#[macro_use] extern crate log` and depend on tracing 0.1.44 with `default-features = false` (the workspace already builds tracing for every target, std included, so no package arrives); each call keeps its level and message: codegen's compile.rs `trace!` on each compiled statement and expression and on each finished code object (5 calls), and rustpython-vm's `debug!` on struct format codes (buffer.rs, 2), on `eval`'s code object and on every raised exception (frame.rs), `warn!` when zipimport fails to initialize (import.rs), `info!` on a JIT fallback (function.rs, `jit` feature) and the `trace!` calls behind the `vm-tracing-logging` feature (frame.rs and macros.rs' `vm_trace!`) become `tracing::trace!`, `tracing::debug!`, `tracing::warn!` and `tracing::info!`; the commented-out `warn!` and `trace!` lines stay as they were. What changes for the events: before, each was a log record that nanocode-observability's log bridge (crates/integrations/observability/src/log_bridge.rs) turned into a tracing event on its shared `log event` callsite with target `log` and the record's target, module path, file and line in `log.target`, `log.module_path`, `log.file` and `log.line` fields, and only where a log logger was installed (never on wasm32, where log's records went nowhere); now each is a native tracing event with its own callsite, whose metadata target is the module path (rustpython_codegen::compile, rustpython_vm::frame and so on, the same string log used as the default target, so `NANOCODE_LOG` filters by target select the same events) and whose file, line and module path are metadata rather than fields, with the formatted text in `message`; on wasm32 they reach whatever tracing subscriber the embedder installs. Natively log stays (reqwest, rustls and the bridge use it). Not run: rustpython-vm with `vm-tracing-logging` or `jit`, and rustpython-codegen without `std` (cargo refuses features for the excluded patches from the workspace root, and nanocode builds none of them); those edits only change the macro path. Smoke check: the r4-deps debug nanocode-cli and one from this commit give byte-identical output for output/flags-smoke.py through `nanocode psh-shell -c 'python3 flags-smoke.py'`, 31 lines. Packages: wasm32-unknown-unknown third-party 63 before, 62 after (log leaves; base64 is the one package left outside the accepted set), 166 to 165 packages in all; x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu (101 third-party, 207 in all), x86_64-pc-windows-msvc (108) and aarch64-apple-darwin (104) unchanged. Commands: `cargo metadata --locked`, `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli`, `cargo check --locked --lib` and `cargo clippy --locked --lib` for rustpython-codegen and rustpython-vm natively and for wasm32-unknown-unknown, `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-python --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`; all pass, with only warnings r4-deps also has (rustpython-vm's unused `eval_breaker_pending` and `PyStr` import on wasm32, checked on r4-deps; nanocode-sys' two `const fn` suggestions; ruff_python_ast's unknown cfgs).
- The vendored RustPython crates declare their bit-flag sets with nanocode-flags' `flags!`, and bitflags leaves the wasm32 build (2026-11-13). crates/core/flags (package nanocode-flags, a workspace member and workspace dependency, no dependencies, `no_std`, 295 lines against bitflags 2.13.1's 5,986) is one `macro_rules!` macro with bitflags 2's two input forms: `struct Name: Bits { const FLAG = value; .. }` declares `struct Name(Bits)` with the caller's attributes and derives, and `impl Name: Bits { .. }` adds the same items to a tuple struct the caller declared (the ruff parser's `RecoveryContext`). It generates only what nanocode's build calls, found by marking every method `#[deprecated]` and dropping every operator impl, then running `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli` until it compiled: the `pub const` flags, `empty`, `all`, `bits`, `from_bits_truncate`, `from_bits_retain`, `is_empty`, `is_all`, `intersects`, `contains`, `insert`, `remove`, `set`, `union`, `difference`, `iter`, `iter_names`, `|`, `|=`, `&`, `&=`, `-`, `-=` and `!`, each with bitflags 2.13.1's arithmetic (`!` and `from_bits_truncate` mask with `all()`, `-` and `remove` keep unknown bits, `iter` yields the named flags then one value of leftover bits). Left out because nothing calls them: `from_bits`, `from_name`, `toggle`, `intersection`, `symmetric_difference`, `complement`, `^`, `^=`, `Extend`, `FromIterator`, the `Flags` trait, the hex formatting traits and parsing. The struct form always writes `Debug` as bitflags' does (`Name(A | B | 0x40)`, `Name(0x0)` when empty, names in declaration order with bitflags' rule for multi-bit flags, through `debug_tuple` so `{:#?}` matches too), so the 19 call sites that derived `Debug` drop it from their derive lists and `InterpolatedStringFlagsInner`, `BytesLiteralFlagsInner` and `SreInfo`, which derived none, gain one; derived `Hash`, `Eq` and `Default` hash and compare the bits as before. Call sites: rustpython-codegen symboltable.rs, rustpython-common cformat.rs and cjk/iso2022.rs, rustpython-compiler-core bytecode.rs, rustpython-ruff_python_ast nodes.rs (4) and token.rs, rustpython-ruff_python_parser parser/expression.rs and parser/mod.rs, rustpython-sre_engine constants.rs (2), rustpython-vm descriptor.rs, function/method.rs, gc_state.rs, object/core.rs, protocol/buffer.rs, _ctypes/base.rs, _io.rs (2) and vm/compile_mode.rs; rustpython-vm's `#[macro_use] extern crate bitflags` goes. Equality (output/flags-eq, release with debug assertions): the 22 flag types, copied verbatim, are declared with bitflags 2.13.1 and with `flags!` side by side, and every kept method and operator, the constants, `all`, `Default`, the `Hash` value, `{:?}`, `{:#?}` and padded Debug strings, `iter` and `iter_names` agree over 7,164,448 seeded operand pairs (every bit pattern of each u8 and u16 type plus 300,000 pairs per type, biased toward combinations of declared flags, unknown bits and the sign bit of the i32 types), and the impl form agrees for 300,000 pairs; two mutations (`!` without the mask, leftover bits without `0x`) each fail it. Smoke check: a debug nanocode-cli from r4-deps and one from this commit run the same script through `nanocode psh-shell -c 'python3 flags-smoke.py'` (re flags and inline-flag errors, TextIOWrapper newline tracking, BufferedReader detach, compile in exec, eval and single modes, `from __future__` and top-level-await flags, an AST dump with string prefixes, co_flags of nested, coroutine, generator and async-generator functions, symtable, printf formatting, gc debug flags, memoryview, the three ISO-2022 codecs, classmethod and staticmethod, syntax errors) with byte-identical output, 31 lines. Packages: wasm32-unknown-unknown third-party 64 before, 63 after (bitflags leaves; base64 and log stay outside the accepted set); x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc and aarch64-apple-darwin keep bitflags through tower-http and their third-party counts (101, 108, 104); the Linux graph gains nanocode-flags (206 to 207 packages). Commands: `cargo metadata --locked`, `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli`, `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-python --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo check --locked --lib` and `cargo clippy --locked --lib` for each of the seven RustPython crates natively and for wasm32-unknown-unknown, and `cargo clippy --locked --lib -p nanocode-flags` natively and for wasm32; all pass, with only warnings that r4-deps has (ruff_python_ast's unknown `salsa` and `cache` cfgs, nanocode-sys' two `const fn` suggestions on wasm32, rustpython-vm's unused `eval_breaker_pending` and `PyStr` import on wasm32).
- nanocode-computer's macOS backend reads Core Foundation through nanocode-sys's own `core_foundation::Object`, and core-foundation 0.10.1 and core-foundation-sys 0.8.7 leave the lock (2026-11-13). crates/core/sys/src/core_foundation.rs (macOS only) loads CoreFoundation lazily with dlopen and dlsym into one function table behind a OnceLock, as trust_settings.rs does, so nanocode-sys links no framework into binaries that never call it (nanocode-cli's macOS graph has no nanocode-computer). `Object` owns one CF reference: `from_create_rule` and `from_get_rule` take one, Clone retains, Drop releases, PartialEq is CFEqual and Hash is CFHash. It does what ax.rs used core-foundation for: `string` (CFStringCreateWithBytes, as `CFString::new`), `static_string` (CFStringCreateWithBytesNoCopy with kCFAllocatorNull, as `from_static_string`), `number` (CFNumberCreate with kCFNumberFloat64Type), `true_value`, `mutable_data`, `array` and `dictionary` with the CFType callbacks, type checks, `text` (CFStringGetCStringPtr first, then CFStringGetBytes, as CFString's Display), `text_equals` (CFEqual against a NoCopy string, as `PartialEq<&str>`), the UTF-16 length, unit and prefix `shown` needs, `float` and `integer` (CFNumberGetValue as Float64 and SInt64), `boolean` (pointer equality with kCFBooleanTrue, as `bool::from(CFBoolean)`), `array_values` (retained items up to a limit, NULLs skipped, as ax.rs's `array_items`), `dictionary_find` (GetValueIfPresent), `dictionary_value` (GetValue) and `data_bytes`. `RunLoop` wraps CFRunLoopGetCurrent, AddSource, RemoveSource and RunInMode. ax.rs keeps its AX, CoreGraphics and ImageIO FFI, about 40 functions, statics and the observer callback, so moving it is not small and it stays. Its extern signatures take nanocode-sys's `Reference`, and `Element` and `Observer` hold an `Object` instead of a raw CFTypeRef, so ax.rs's own CFRetain, CFRelease, CFEqual, CFHash and CF casts are gone: it has 51 unsafe blocks instead of 55 and gains none. mod.rs reads `Object` where it read `CFType`. Differences, all on input core-foundation could not handle either: a NULL from AXValueCreate, kAXTrustedCheckOptionPrompt or kCGImageDestinationLossyCompressionQuality panics with a message naming it, where core-foundation panicked with "Attempted to create a NULL object."; an action name that is not a CFString panics, where core-foundation read it as a CFString without checking; the CFNumberType argument is a CFIndex, as CFNumber.h declares it, where core-foundation-sys passes a u32. New unsafe in nanocode-sys, each block one call: one `transmute` per resolved symbol (33, each to the signature in the CoreFoundation headers), two reads of the kCFAllocatorNull and kCFBooleanTrue globals, `unsafe impl Send` and `Sync` for `Constant` (immutable CF constants that live as long as the process), dlopen, dlsym and dlerror (with `CStr::from_ptr` on dlerror's NUL-terminated message), one call per CF function on a reference an `Object` owns or the caller vouches for, `CStr::from_ptr` on CFStringGetCStringPtr's NUL-terminated result, and `slice::from_raw_parts` over CFDataGetBytePtr and CFDataGetLength. `from_create_rule` and `from_get_rule` are the two `pub unsafe fn`s; their contract is that the pointer is NULL or a CF object the caller owns (create rule) or borrows (get rule), and `clippy::missing_safety_doc` is allowed on them because the repository writes no doc comments. Equality on gak-9 (M1 Max, macOS 26.3), output/computer-check: one release binary on origin/master's crate and one on this one, each driving `nanocode_computer::Computer` over `Provider::native(Native::default())` with the same JSON steps, run interleaved. list_apps (bundle_info, processes, on_screen) and get_app_state for TextEdit, Calculator, Nudge (with its JPEG screenshot: CFData, CGImageDestination and the quality dictionary) and Finder give byte-identical output, 102,291 bytes in each of 2 old/new pairs. A mutating sequence gives byte-identical output, 14,221 bytes in each of 3 pairs. It runs set_value on TextEdit's text area with a non-ASCII, emoji and newline string, select_text (AXSelectedTextRange through AXValueCreate), type_text, scroll, set_value back to empty, Calculator clicks (AXPress) and press_key (CGEvent), with get_app_state between steps. An earlier build of this commit (link-time CoreFoundation instead of dlopen) matched in 4 more read pairs and 2 more mutating pairs. Debug builds of both the old and the new crate panic at engine.rs:691, because `line.actionable.then_some(next - 1)` evaluates `next - 1` eagerly and overflows when the first line is not actionable. That is on master and untouched here, so the harness uses release builds. Packages: 307 before, 305 after. Commands: `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli` on the Hand and on gak-9; `cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-sys -p nanocode-computer --lib` on the Hand (Linux, `--target aarch64-apple-darwin`) and natively on gak-9; `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-sys -p nanocode-computer` with `--target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` and `x86_64-apple-darwin`; `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-sys --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`; `cargo clippy --locked --lib -p nanocode-sys -p nanocode-tls --target aarch64-apple-ios`. All are clean.
- pymath's math on targets that are neither Unix nor Windows (wasm32-unknown-unknown) is its own port of libm 0.2.16, and libm leaves the lock (2026-11-13). crates/patches/pymath/src/m_libm/ holds exactly the 37 functions m_rust.rs called (acos, acosh, asin, asinh, atan, atan2, atanh, cbrt, ceil, copysign, cos, cosh, erf, erfc, exp, exp2, expm1, fabs, floor, fmod, frexp, hypot, ldexp, log, log10, log1p, log2, modf, nextafter, pow, remainder, sin, sinh, sqrt, tan, tanh, trunc) and their helpers (rem_pio2, rem_pio2_large, k_sin, k_cos, k_tan, expo2, k_expo2, remquo, scalbn), with the arithmetic libm runs on wasm32: there `intrinsics_enabled` is off on stable Rust and `arch` only selects x86 and aarch64 code, so every function takes libm's generic path. libm's generic ceil, floor, trunc, fabs, copysign, scalbn, sqrt (Goldschmidt iterations over its 128-entry reciprocal square root table) and fmod are written out for f64. fmod's reduction past 32 exponent steps computes the exact remainder (x << e) mod y in u128 steps of 64 bits instead of libm's `linear_mul_reduction`, which computes the same integer. cbrt keeps only libm's round-to-nearest path and uses `f64::mul_add`, a correctly rounded fma like libm's own. libm's `force_eval!` (volatile reads that only raise floating-point exceptions, which Rust cannot observe) and the unchecked `i!` indexing are gone, so the module has no unsafe. rem_pio2_large keeps libm's pointer-width choice of the 2/pi table (66 words on 32-bit targets, 690 on 64-bit) and turns libm's release-mode `_ => {}` for a precision outside 0..=3 into `unreachable!`, since rem_pio2 always passes 1. The module carries libm's own clippy allows (assign_op_pattern, eq_op, excessive_precision, float_cmp, int_plus_one, just_underscores_and_digits, many_single_char_names, mixed_case_hex_literals, needless_late_init, needless_return, unreadable_literal, zero_divided_by_zero). Equality, output/libm-check (its own workspace, the port included by `#[path]`, libm =0.2.16 as the reference, splitmix64 seed 0x5eed): 10^8 inputs per function, 3.7×10^9 in all, compared with `f64::to_bits`. Inputs are random bit patterns, 44 specials (±0, ±inf, quiet, signalling and negative NaNs with payloads, the smallest and largest subnormals, ±MIN_POSITIVE, ±MAX, ±1, ±0.5, ±2, π/2, π, the exp overflow and underflow thresholds and more), specials ±32 ulps, numbers between 2^-64 and 2^16, and subnormal-range numbers. Pairs add y = x, y within 4 ulps of x, and small integers and halves, and ldexp takes n across all of i32, ±32 and ±2200. The full cross product of the specials runs too. Against libm with `force-soft-floats` (its wasm32 configuration) there are 0 differences on x86_64 (hosted Hand), 0 on aarch64 (gak-9, M1 Max), and 0 with the harness built for wasm32-wasip1 under wasmtime 27. Against libm's default features on native, x86_64 differs only in NaN bits: 60,036,627 acosh and 47,561,276 sqrt inputs, because `sqrtsd` returns the x86 default NaN 0xfff8000000000000 for a negative operand where libm's generic sqrt, ours and wasm32 return 0x7ff8000000000000. aarch64 differs only in the NaN bits of 3,528,812 sqrt inputs, because `fsqrt` keeps a NaN operand's payload. No non-NaN result differs anywhere. The specials cross product counts 2 mismatches in every run; recomputing each special through `std::hint::black_box` finds none, so they come from LLVM folding NaN payloads at compile time in the harness's unrolled constant loop, not from the code. A release wasm32 build of pymath writes one 577,916-byte rlib against 378,392 (pymath) + 1,493,212 (libm) before, in the same wall time within noise (41.8 s and 47.7 s against 41.7 s and 53.5 s on the shared Hand, mostly nanocode-numeric). Packages: 308 before, 307 after. Commands: `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli`, `cargo check --locked --lib -p pymath` native and `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --locked -p pymath --lib` native and wasm32, all clean.
- nanocode-jpeg tells its IDCT whether a block's AC coefficients are known to be zero, so it no longer ORs 63 coefficients per block to find the DC-only blocks, and the progressive scans test the restart counter before calling the restart handler, making decodes 1 to 5% faster on x86_64 and 1 to 3% faster on aarch64 with every output byte unchanged (2026-11-13, Georgios: close the decode gap to zune-jpeg without changing an output byte). crates/core/jpeg/src/idct.rs gains `AcCoefficients { Zero, Present, Unknown }` as a parameter of `transform`: Zero takes the DC-only fill, Present the full IDCT, Unknown computes the OR as before. crates/core/jpeg/src/bitstream.rs's `decode_block` ORs every dequantized AC coefficient it writes into the zeroed block and reports Zero or Present from it; that is exact because positions only grow and every write below position 64 lands on a distinct coefficient, so it reports Unknown when the block ran past position 64 (a clamped or wrapped write may have overwritten an earlier one, or the DC). crates/core/jpeg/src/progressive.rs reports Zero when the block's nonzero mask (the previous commit) has no AC bit, which means every quantized AC coefficient is zero, and Unknown otherwise, since a nonzero coefficient times its quantization factor can still wrap to zero. `self.todo == 0` is now tested before `handle_restart_main`, which returns at once otherwise, so nothing else changes. Not equal: nothing. No unsafe code. Equal (equal against a copy of the previous commit): x86_64 3,819 corpus files with 22,110 mutated copies, aarch64 1,467 files with 17,436 mutated copies, 0 differences; with SIMD forced off x86_64 3,819 files and 7,370 mutated copies and aarch64 1,467 files and 8,718 mutated copies, 0 differences. Measured (thread CPU time, previous and new code alternating, medians): x86_64, hosted Hand, load average 5 to 6, the nine Wikimedia photos, 11 rounds: 944.2 ms before, 913.6 ms after (1.033x; progressive 1.05x and 1.01x, sequential 0.995x to 1.02x); aarch64, gak-9, load average 31 to 39, the eight benchmark photos, 21 rounds twice: 109.8 to 107.7 ms and 111.2 to 109.2 ms (1.02x; every file 1.006x to 1.032x). Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-jpeg` natively and for wasm32-unknown-unknown, `cargo clippy --locked --lib -p nanocode-jpeg` (x86_64 and aarch64-apple-darwin), `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli`.
- nanocode-jpeg's progressive refinement scans skip zero coefficients through a per-block bit mask of nonzero AC coefficients instead of testing every position, so progressive JPEGs decode 11 to 15% faster on x86_64 and 29 to 39% faster on aarch64 with every output byte unchanged (2026-11-13, Georgios: close the decode gap to zune-jpeg without changing an output byte). crates/core/jpeg/src/progressive.rs keeps one u64 per coefficient block (bit z set when the coefficient at zigzag position z is nonzero) beside each component's coefficient buffer, allocated with it (a sixteenth of its size); crates/core/jpeg/src/bitstream.rs's AC first scan updates the bit of every coefficient it writes (set or cleared by the written value, so a later write to the same clamped position stays exact) and the AC refinement uses the mask: for each decoded symbol it finds the zero that ends the run as the (run + 1)-th set bit of the inverted mask within the band (at most 15 bit clears), reads the correction bits of the nonzero coefficients before it in ascending order with trailing_zeros, and sets the bit of the new coefficient it writes; the end-of-band path tests mask >> 1 instead of scanning 63 coefficients and walks only the nonzero ones. A correction never makes a nonzero coefficient zero (successive approximation is at most 13, so adding or subtracting the bit, 1..=8192, cannot wrap an i16 to zero), so the mask stays exact. Before, the refinement tested every position of the band with an unpredictable branch, 44% of a progressive decode's time on x86_64 (perf) and 53% on the M1 (sample). The order of every bit read and every refill is the same as before: in the first pass refills only follow correction bits, as before; in the end-of-band pass the old loop tested for a refill after every position, zero or not, so the new code repeats that test after each run of zero positions, at most twice, since two such tests always leave at least one bit (a refill that stops at a marker adds no bits, the next one pads 32) and further tests do nothing; the coefficients keep their natural order, so the dequantization and IDCT are untouched. Storing coefficients in zigzag order instead was tried: the refinement got as fast, but undoing the order before the IDCT made finishing 5x slower on the M1. Not equal: nothing, except that the masks are one more allocation of a sixteenth of the coefficient buffers, which can fail where the buffers alone would not. No unsafe code. Equal (equal against a copy of the previous commit): x86_64 3,819 corpus files with 22,110 mutated copies (random bytes overwritten after the first SOS or the file cut), 0 differences; aarch64 1,467 files (the 284 corpus and benchmark files and the 1,183 cjpeg files, a third of them progressive, with restart intervals, every sampling and successive approximation) with 17,436 mutated copies, 0 differences; with SIMD forced off (output/jpeg-scalar) aarch64 1,467 files and 8,718 mutated copies and x86_64 3,819 files and 7,370 mutated copies, 0 differences. Measured (thread CPU time, previous and new code alternating, medians): x86_64, hosted Hand, load average 4 to 6, 15 rounds: 5169x6759 progressive 4:4:4 388.2 to 349.4 ms (1.11x), 3363x4339 progressive 4:2:0 131.2 to 114.0 ms (1.15x), a baseline 4032x3024 control 46.8 and 45.0 ms (unchanged code, noise); aarch64, gak-9, load average 33 to 40, 25 rounds twice: 3072x2048 progressive 4:2:0 26.7 to 20.7 ms (1.29x), 1744x2464 progressive 4:4:4 24.9 to 18.0 ms (1.39x), the baseline 4:2:0 control 1.00x. Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-jpeg` natively and for wasm32-unknown-unknown, `cargo clippy --locked --lib -p nanocode-jpeg` (x86_64 and aarch64-apple-darwin), `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli`.
- nanocode-jpeg's fancy upsampling runs its horizontal (h2v1) and vertical (h1v2, and both halves of h2v2) filters in AVX2 through nanocode-sys on x86_64, 2.2x and 1.4x faster per sample, which makes 4:2:0 and 4:2:2 decodes 1 to 4% faster with every pixel unchanged (2026-11-13, Georgios: close the decode gap to zune-jpeg without changing an output byte). crates/core/sys/src/jpeg.rs gains `upsample_horizontal(input, output) -> usize` (the interior centres it filled, a multiple of 16, starting at centre 1, with output[2..] holding their pairs) and `upsample_vertical(input, near, far, output) -> usize` (the samples of both output rows it filled, a multiple of 16); both run only after the same `vector_unit()` and only on x86_64 (`cfg!(target_arch = "x86_64")`), and crates/core/jpeg/src/upsample.rs finishes the rest of each row with its unchanged scalar loops. The kernels compute the same i16 expressions as the scalar code, (3 * x + 2 + neighbour) >> 2, with wrapping `_mm256_mullo_epi16` and `_mm256_add_epi16` and the arithmetic `_mm256_srai_epi16`, which equal Rust's release i16 arithmetic for every input (the decoder's samples are 0..=255 anyway); the horizontal kernel loads each centre's left, centre and right lanes from one 18-sample window and interleaves even and odd outputs with `_mm256_unpacklo_epi16`, `_mm256_unpackhi_epi16` and `_mm256_permute2x128_si256`. No NEON kernel: on the M1 LLVM already vectorizes the scalar loops with NEON, and a NEON horizontal kernel measured 0.98x, so aarch64 keeps the scalar code. Not equal: nothing. Unsafe blocks and their invariants: the calls into `x86::upsample_horizontal` and `x86::upsample_vertical` after `vector_unit()` found AVX2; `_mm256_loadu_si256` from `&[i16; 16]` lanes cut from an `&[i16; 18]` window and from `&[i16; 16]` chunks (readable by type), `_mm256_storeu_si256` into `&mut [i16; 16]` chunks (writable by type); the windows and chunks exist only after the entry points assert output.len() == 2 * input.len() and, for the vertical filter, that both neighbour rows match the input row. Equal: output/jpeg-simd's `upsample` compares the kernels with the scalar loops over 300,000 seeded rows of 3 to 702 samples (full-range i16, 0..=255, and extremes such as i16::MIN and i16::MAX), 0 differences; `equal` against a copy of the previous commit's nanocode-jpeg and nanocode-sys gave on x86_64 3,819 corpus files and their mutated copies with 0 differences, and with SIMD forced off (output/jpeg-scalar) 0 differences; aarch64 compiles the entry points but never enters a kernel. - nanocode-jpeg's baseline Huffman decoder keeps its bit window in registers for the whole block, so sequential JPEGs decode 4 to 25% faster on x86_64 and 8 to 16% faster on aarch64 with every output byte unchanged, closing most of the remaining gap to zune-jpeg 0.4.21 (2026-11-13, Georgios: close the decode gap to zune-jpeg without changing an output byte). crates/core/jpeg/src/bitstream.rs moves the bit buffer, its left-aligned copy and the count of bits left into a private `Window`; `decode_block` copies it into a local field by field, decodes the DC and every AC coefficient of the block through `#[inline(always)]` refill code (the four-byte read and the byte-by-byte path with 0xFF00 unstuffing and marker detection, as before) and stores it back field by field on every exit, errors included. Before, the refill's byte path was an out-of-line call taking `&mut self`, so LLVM kept the window in memory and reloaded it after every refill, a store-to-load chain on every symbol (perf on x86_64 and the M1 disassembly showed the loads); whole-struct copies of the window are avoided on purpose, since its padding made LLVM copy the struct through the stack (tried, 20% slower). The refill test of marker, overread and end of image becomes one local flag, recomputed after every byte-path refill, the only place these fields change inside a block, which frees registers on x86_64. The progressive decoders (DC first and refine, AC first and refine) keep the old in-place window with the out-of-line cold byte path: inlining it into their bit-serial loops made progressive files 3 to 7% slower. Not equal: nothing; the bits read, the refill points (so the bits padded after a marker and the overread count), the fast and slow symbol paths and every error are the same code as before, only where the window lives changed. No unsafe code. Equal: output/jpeg-simd (reference-jpeg and reference-sys are copies of crates/core/jpeg and crates/core/sys at the previous commit, `equal` decodes every file with both and compares width, height, colour, pixels, ICC profile, Exif and errors) gave on x86_64 (hosted Hand) 3,819 corpus files (Wikimedia photos up to 8256x5504, the image-rs, libjpeg-turbo, zune-image, jpeg-decoder and Pillow test images, Pillow-generated files) and 11,055 copies with random bytes overwritten or cut after the first SOS, 0 differences, and on aarch64 (gak-9) the 284 corpus and benchmark files with 2,160 mutated copies plus 1,183 cjpeg-made files (1x1 to 1023x767, every sampling cjpeg accepts, progressive, restart intervals, grayscale, optimized tables) with 4,732 mutated copies, 0 differences; with SIMD forced off (output/jpeg-scalar, nanocode-sys's `vector_unit()` returning false) x86_64 gave 3,819 files and 7,370 mutated copies and aarch64 284 + 1,080 mutated + 1,183 + 2,366 mutated decodes, all with 0 differences. - nanocode-jpeg's encoder runs the forward DCT with quantization and the RGB-to-YCbCr conversion in AVX2 and NEON through nanocode-sys, and writes its entropy-coded data a word at a time, producing the same bytes 2.6x faster on x86_64 and 1.4x faster on aarch64 (2026-11-13). crates/core/sys/src/jpeg.rs gains `forward_dct_quantize(samples, table, output) -> bool` and `rgb_to_ycbcr(rows, planes) -> bool` behind the same single `vector_unit()`. The forward DCT is image 0.25.6's jfdctint in i32 lanes (rows first, then columns, each a pass over eight vectors between two transposes), with the quirk it carries: the column pass rounds its odd part with 1 << 10 and shifts by 15. Quantization keeps the exact float steps: i32 division by 8 toward zero ((c + ((c >> 31) >>> 29)) >> 3), conversion to f32 (exact under 2^24), an IEEE f32 division by the factor (`_mm256_div_ps`, `vdivq_f32`, never a reciprocal), truncation to i32, and rounding half away from zero from the f32 remainder compared with ±0.5. The colour conversion takes eight interleaved RGB pixels per row (`_mm_shuffle_epi8` deinterleave, `vld3_u8` on NEON) through image's 16-bit fixed-point weights in i32 lanes; every result is 0..=255, so the saturating packs equal its `as u8`. crates/core/jpeg/src/encoder.rs gathers each block's rows with one copy per row when the block is inside the image (edge blocks still repeat the last column and row pixel by pixel), calls the kernels and falls back to its scalar `forward_dct`, `quantize` and `rgb_to_ycbcr` when they return false. Its bit writer holds 64 bits and writes four bytes at once when none is 0xFF (byte by byte with the 0x00 stuffing otherwise), writes each Huffman code and its magnitude bits in one call, and finds the AC coefficients from a 64-bit mask of nonzero zigzag positions (trailing_zeros, at most 63 steps) instead of testing all 63. The emitted symbols, the padding with ones and the dropped partial byte at the end of the scan are unchanged. Unsafe blocks and their invariants: the calls into `x86::forward_dct_quantize`, `x86::rgb_to_ycbcr`, `arm::forward_dct_quantize` and `arm::rgb_to_ycbcr` after `vector_unit()` found AVX2 or NEON; `_mm256_storeu_si256` into `&mut [i32; 8]` output rows and `vst1q_s32` into `&mut [i32; 4]` halves (writable by type); `_mm_loadu_si128` from the `&[u8; 16]` head of a row and `vld3_u8` from `&[u8; 24]` (readable by type). `forward_dct_quantize` asserts every quantization factor is at least 1 (the encoder clamps its tables to 1..=255), because a zero factor would give infinity, which the SIMD truncation turns into i32::MIN where Rust's `as` saturates. Equal (same harnesses as the decode kernels entry, reference-jpeg's encoder against this one): x86_64 1,000,000 seeded blocks through `forward_dct_quantize` and `rgb_to_ycbcr` (random, all 0, all 255, a 0/255 checkerboard, ramps and extreme mixes, with random factors 1..=255, all 1, and 1..=12) and 14,108 encodes (each decodable corpus file of up to 2 MB at qualities 1, 50, 85 and 100, plus 2,000 random images of 1x1 to 300x300, smooth and noisy, gray and RGB, random quality) with 0 differences; forced scalar 200,000 blocks and 12,508 encodes, 0 differences. aarch64 2,000,000 blocks and 4,332 encodes over the gak-9 corpus, plus 2,944 over the 1,183 cjpeg files, 0 differences; forced scalar 732 plus 2,944 encodes, 0 differences. Measured (thread CPU time, interleaved, medians, quality 85 as nanocode-image encodes): x86_64, hosted Hand, load average 25: encoding the nine decoded Wikimedia photos took 3,290.4 ms before and 1,261.1 ms after (2.61x; 1.95x for the grayscale one). aarch64, gak-9, load average 14 to 19: the eight decoded benchmark photos 354.5 to 248.8 ms (1.42x), 71 decoded corpus images 8,796.0 to 6,282.8 ms (1.40x; LLVM's own NEON vectorization of the scalar DCT leaves less to gain there). Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-sys -p nanocode-jpeg` natively and for wasm32-unknown-unknown, `cargo clippy --locked --lib -p nanocode-sys -p nanocode-jpeg` for x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, aarch64-apple-darwin and wasm32-unknown-unknown, `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli`.
- nanocode-jpeg's decoder runs its integer IDCT and its YCbCr-to-RGB conversion in AVX2 on x86_64 and NEON on aarch64 through nanocode-sys, the speed zune-jpeg 0.4.21 had before nanocode-jpeg replaced it, with every pixel unchanged (2026-11-13, Georgios: restore the SIMD the replacements lost, without changing an output byte). crates/core/sys/src/jpeg.rs (new, `pub mod jpeg` in lib.rs) holds safe entry points that answer whether they did the work: `inverse_dct(coefficients, output, position, stride) -> bool` and `ycbcr_to_rgb(luma, blue, red, target) -> usize` (the pixels converted, whole groups of 16). Detection lives in one private `vector_unit()` (`is_x86_feature_detected!("avx2")`, `is_aarch64_feature_detected!("neon")`, false elsewhere, so wasm32 and older x86_64 keep the scalar code); nanocode-jpeg stays forbid(unsafe_code) and keeps its scalar code as the fallback (crates/core/jpeg/src/idct.rs, color.rs, Cargo.toml now depends on nanocode-sys). The IDCT computes zune's i32 butterflies eight columns at once (AVX2 `_mm256_mullo_epi32`, NEON `vmulq_n_s32` on two halves), with wrapping adds, multiplies and shifts as the scalar release build, two 8x8 transposes, and the clamp to 0..=255 as a saturating pack followed by min/max, which equals the clamp for every i32. A block whose rows 4 to 7 or columns 4 to 7 are zero takes a variant where those inputs are the constant zero (a zero column's first pass is (0 + 512) >> 10 = 0), so LLVM drops their terms; the result is the same integers. The colour conversion computes zune's Q14 formula in i32 lanes: AVX2 with `_mm256_madd_epi16` on (Y, 1) and (Cr, Cb) pairs, which are exact because every factor fits i16, then packs that saturate to i16 and u8 (equal to clamp(0, 255)) and `_mm_shuffle_epi8` to interleave RGB; NEON with `vmlal_n_s16`, `vqshrn_n_s32`, `vqmovun_s16` and `vst3q_u8`. The decoder's DC-only test now ORs the 63 AC coefficients instead of `all(== 0)`, which stopped at the first nonzero and so ran as a 63-step scalar loop on every DC-only block (the M1 profile showed `idct::transform` at about a third of the IDCT's samples). Upsampling stays scalar: 0.5% of decode samples on x86_64 and about 1% on M1, too little to be worth a kernel. Unsafe blocks and the invariant each relies on: the calls into the `#[target_feature]` kernels (`x86::inverse_dct`, `x86::ycbcr_to_rgb`, `arm::inverse_dct`, `arm::ycbcr_to_rgb`), made only after `vector_unit()` found the feature; `_mm256_loadu_si256` from a `&[i32; 8]` coefficient row and from `&[i16; 16]` plane chunks, and `vld1q_s32` from `&[i32; 4]` and `vld1q_s16` from `&[i16; 8]` (the reference type guarantees the bytes are readable); `_mm_storeu_si128` into `&mut [i16; 8]` output rows and `&mut [u8; 16]` target chunks, `vst1q_s16` into `&mut [i16; 8]` and `vst3q_u8` into `&mut [u8; 48]` (the type guarantees the bytes are writable). Those row references are built only after `inverse_dct` asserts that position + 7 * stride + 8 fits the output and returns false for a stride under 8 (rows would overlap), and `ycbcr_to_rgb` asserts equal plane lengths and a target of three bytes per pixel. Equal: output/jpeg-simd links a copy of origin/master's nanocode-jpeg (reference-jpeg) against this one, and output/jpeg-scalar builds the same harness against a copy of nanocode-sys whose `vector_unit()` returns false. x86_64 (hosted Hand, AVX2): 2,000,000 seeded IDCT blocks (full-range i32, extremes such as i32::MIN and i32::MAX that overflow every pass, ±1024, sparse, zeroed rows 4 to 7 and columns 4 to 7, DC-only, strides 8 to 55 including ones that are not multiples of 8, offsets 0 to 19), 500,000 colour rows of 0 to 199 pixels with full-range i16 samples, the 3,825 JPEGs of the Hand's corpus (Wikimedia photos up to 8256x5504, the image-rs, libjpeg-turbo, zune-image, jpeg-decoder and Pillow test images, 3,267 Pillow-generated files) and 11,073 copies of them with random bytes overwritten or cut after the first SOS. Every pixel, ICC profile, Exif block and error is the same, with 0 differences; forced scalar gave 0 differences over 400,000 blocks, 100,000 rows, 3,825 files and 3,691 mutated files. aarch64 (gak-9, M1 Max, NEON): 4,000,000 blocks, 1,000,000 rows, the 276-file gak-9 corpus plus 8 cjpeg-made benchmark photos (284 files), 5,400 mutated files and 1,183 cjpeg files (sizes 1x1 to 1023x767, every sampling cjpeg accepts including 4x4, 3x2, 2x3 and per-component mixes, progressive, restart intervals, grayscale, optimized tables, float DCT) with 4,732 mutated copies, 0 differences; forced scalar gave 0 over the same files. Measured with output/jpeg-simd's `bench` (thread CPU time, reference and new alternating every file and round, medians) and `kernels`. x86_64, hosted Hand, load average 21 to 25 on 5 cores: decoding nine Wikimedia photos (3648x5472 and 4032x3024 4:2:0, 4000x3000 4:2:2, 3072x2304 and 8256x5504 4:4:4, 5169x6759 4:4:4 and 3363x4339 4:2:0 progressive, 1796x3767 grayscale, 3216x4288) took 1,790.1 ms before and 1,324.0 ms after (1.35x: 1.55x on 4:2:0, 1.66x on the 8256x5504 4:4:4, 1.18x and 1.22x progressive, 1.19x grayscale); IDCT 61.3 to 21.5 ns per block (2.85x), colour 2.22 to 0.33 ns per pixel (6.8x). aarch64, gak-9, load average 13 to 18 on 10 cores: eight 1744x2464 to 3072x2048 photos (4:2:0, 4:2:2, 4:4:4, progressive 4:2:0 and 4:4:4, grayscale, restart intervals) 148.1 to 129.7 ms (1.14x), the 271 corpus files 995.9 to 917.1 ms (1.09x); IDCT 30.9 to 28.0 ns per block (1.10x: LLVM already vectorizes the scalar butterflies with NEON, so only the sparse variants gain), colour 0.59 to 0.26 ns per pixel (2.3x).
