Commands: cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli, cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-http, cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-http. Packages 424 → 424.
- nanocode-compression gets a miniz_oxide-compatible DEFLATE compressor, `miniz` (2026-11-12): crates/core/compression/src/miniz/ (mod.rs: `Level`, `Format`, `Writer`, `compress`, `compress_sync_flush`; compressor.rs, dictionary.rs, block.rs, huffman.rs, bits.rs, tables.rs) writes the bytes flate2 1.1.9's write::DeflateEncoder and write::ZlibEncoder write over miniz_oxide 0.8.9, so gzip request bodies, permessage-deflate messages and PNG text chunks can leave flate2 without changing a byte. It has miniz's hash chains, probe counts per level 0 to 10 (0 stored blocks only, 1 the trigram parser, 2 and 3 greedy, 4 to 10 lazy), block splitting, Huffman construction and zlib header per level, and flate2's writer around it: a 32 KiB output buffer per call, `write_all` as repeated writes, `flush` as one sync call then draining calls, `finish` as finish calls. The buffering is part of the output: when a block does not fit the space a call has, miniz stops; level 1 then refills its 4 KiB lookahead at a different point, and a sync flush interrupted while lookahead remains never completes (flate2 then returns the stream without the trailing empty stored block), so `Writer` simulates the space of each call. The core started from psh's copy (crates/patches/psh/crates/psh-utils/src/deflate.rs: one-shot, levels 1 to 9, modelled on compress_to_vec); psh keeps it because psh is a vendored workspace of its own, and this copy adds streaming input, levels 0 and 10, sync flush and flate2's buffering. Not equal: `Level::new` refuses levels above 10 with `LevelError`, where flate2 compresses 11 to 255 as 10 and anything above 255 as 1. Equal: output/miniz-equal runs flate2 and the new code on the same operation sequences (one write, random and fixed write sizes from 1 byte, flushes between writes, ending in finish or flush; raw and zlib): 34,231 checks on seeded random inputs (9.4 GB, 0 B to 4 MiB, levels 0 to 10), 33,111 checks on 11,081 real files (3.0 GB: repository sources, /usr/bin, ~/media-corpus, serde_json and tokio sources), 72 checks on 8 to 32 MiB inputs: 0 differences, including 33 sync flushes that flate2 left incomplete. Benchmark (output/miniz-equal bench, thread CPU time, best of 9 interleaved runs on the shared Hand, flate2 → new): JSON 1 MiB level 2 387 → 375 MB/s, level 2 sync flush 367 → 363, level 6 zlib 96 → 93, level 1 795 → 713, level 9 46 → 44; Rust sources 8 MiB level 2 181 → 181, level 6 41 → 39, level 1 279 → 254, level 9 19.7 → 19.4. The dictionary tables are fixed-size boxed arrays so masked indexes need no bounds checks, and the bit writer's two argument checks are `debug_assert!`: as `assert!` they cost 3 to 20% at level 2 in the same benchmark. Commands: cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli, cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-compression (and --target wasm32-unknown-unknown), cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-compression. Packages 424 → 424 (nothing calls it yet).
- base64 0.22 (already in the tree through hyper-util and nine nanocode crates) does what base64-simd did in nanocode-image, nanocode-audio, nanocode-code-mode-engine, the Codex backend and nanocode-computer-repl, and base64-simd, vsimd and outref leave (2026-11-12). `STANDARD` is the same dialect (padding required, canonical padding only, non-zero trailing bits refused); `Uint8Array.fromBase64` in code mode decodes its already-cleaned alphabet-only input with a `GeneralPurpose` engine that allows trailing bits and missing padding, which is what `forgiving_decode_to_vec` did with it; computer-repl decodes a CUA image or audio payload once instead of `check` plus a 16-character header decode, and reads the signature from the first 12 decoded bytes, which are the same bytes. Equal: output/base64-equal (base64-simd 0.8.0 beside base64 0.22.1): 32,768 encodings (every length 0..4095, 8 seeded buffers each) byte-identical with equal encoded lengths; 9,801,520 decode checks over 3,000,000 seeded strings (alphabet, padding in any place, invalid bytes, mutated valid encodings): `STANDARD` decode result and accept/reject, `check`, the forgiving path on cleaned input and the CUA signature bytes, 0 differences (934,441 accepted). Not equal: speed. base64-simd's AVX2 paths ran 8 MiB at 3.2-12 GB/s encode and 4.9-10 GB/s decode against base64's 1.3-2.9 GB/s and 0.9-2.7 GB/s (5 interleaved rounds of 10 runs on the shared Hand, noisy); a 10 MB image data URL now costs about 6 ms more to encode, against tens of milliseconds to decode and re-encode the image, and SIMD would need unsafe intrinsics, which only nanocode-sys may hold. `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli`, `cargo clippy --locked` on the five crates, `cargo check --locked --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` for nanocode-image, nanocode-audio and nanocode-code-mode-engine. `cargo metadata` packages 427 -> 424.
- The ruff parser bounds its nesting instead of growing its stack, and parses on a long-lived parser thread with a stack sized for that bound; stacker, psm, ar_archive_writer and object leave (2026-11-12). crates/patches/rustpython-ruff_python_parser/src/parser/mod.rs: `with_recursion` (the parser's recursion points for expressions, patterns, statement blocks and format specs) counts depth against `RECURSION_DEPTH_MAX` = 20,000; the first time it is exceeded the parser records the current token's range and the number of errors so far and ends the token stream (the lexer jumps to the end of the source with no open brackets, f-strings or pending indentation, so every recursion returns at the end-of-file token), and `finish` drops the errors that recovery produced after that point and reports `ParseErrorType::NestingTooDeep`, which rustpython-compiler (`CompileError::from_nesting_too_deep`, also used by `_ast.parse`) turns into the same `RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded during compilation` its AST depth check raised for deep trees. On native targets the parse runs on a per-calling-thread worker (`thread_local!`, started on first use, jobs and replies over std mpsc channels, panics carried back and resumed) whose stack is `RECURSION_DEPTH_MAX * STACK_BYTES_PER_RECURSION_MAX` (12 KiB, from the measured maximum of 9,351 bytes per level: nested f-strings in a debug build on aarch64-apple-darwin; release needs at most 4,173), 240 MiB of reserved, lazily committed address space; a worker that cannot be started is a typed `ParserThreadUnavailable` parse error. On wasm32 the parse runs in place with the same bound, as it did under stacker, which never grows the stack there. rustpython-vm's native stack check reads the stack position from the address of a local instead of `psm::stack_pointer`. Measured on gak-9 with the bound lifted and an 8 MiB parser stack (output/stackmeasure), the deepest parse that fits per construct (debug/release): unary minus 2,786/6,319, `not` 2,785/6,319, conditional expressions 4,365/10,927, lambdas 5,238/7,493, `**` 4,224/11,160, lists 1,489/2,747, calls 916/2,776, nested `if` blocks 1,919/6,100, f-strings 896/2,009; each costs one parser level per source level. Equality: output/e2e's deep corpus (532 programs: 14 constructs at depths 50 to 100,000 in eval and exec mode plus `ast.parse`, and with recursion limits 3,000 and 20,000 at depths 2,000 to 15,000; each program in its own process), old e86dae0d8 against this change on gak-9: 529 byte-identical (including the old crash at depth 15,000 with the limit raised, which still overflows codegen's stack, and every depth-100,000 case), 1 a 166 s run that timed out under the harness's 60 s alarm on one side only (both give the same RecursionError when run alone), and 2 differ: `await` chained 100,000 deep, where old parsed it and reported `SyntaxError: await expression cannot be used here` and the parser now stops at depth 20,000 with the RecursionError. Not equal: a source nested deeper than 20,000 parser levels now raises RecursionError even when it also has a syntax error that old reported (old parsed the whole tree first), and even when `sys.setrecursionlimit` was raised above 20,000 with a thread stack big enough for codegen to walk such a tree (old accepted those); a source nested 1,000 to 20,000 deep behaves as before. Cost: compile() of a 3-line source goes from 19.4 to 33-35 us on gak-9 (two thread handoffs per parse; release, 20,000 compiles, 3 interleaved rounds), and each thread that compiles keeps one parked parser thread; spawning a thread per parse cost 73-88 us and was not kept. TigerStyle departure, bounded to the vendored parser: the worker uses std channels. `cargo metadata` and the `cargo tree -p nanocode-cli -e normal,build` counts are in the commit's check log; `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli` and `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-python --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` on Linux and `cargo check -p nanocode-python` on aarch64-apple-darwin pass.
- pyexpat parses with rustpython-stdlib's own XML pull reader, and xml 1.3.0 (xml-rs) leaves nanocode-cli and Cargo.lock (2026-11-12). crates/patches/rustpython-stdlib/src/pyexpat/reader.rs is an `EventReader` over any `Read` specialised to the one configuration pyexpat's removed `create_config` built (comments and CDATA as their own events, whitespace reported as characters, character data not coalesced, root-level whitespace dropped, several root elements allowed). It decodes one byte at a time from the source exactly as xml-rs's `CharReader` did (byte order mark sniffing for UTF-8 and UTF-16 LE/BE, the `encoding` declaration matched by common prefix against utf-8/utf8, iso-8859-1/latin1, utf-16/utf16 and ascii/us-ascii with the same conflict rules, UTF-8 errors detected only after four bytes or at the end), so the parser thread pulls the same bytes at the same moments and the `NeedMore` handoff across `Parse()` chunks, `LineTracker`'s byte indices and the synchronous backend's replay are unchanged. A lexer (markup tokens, unread characters, `]]>` and `--` handling, the DOCTYPE lexing context) feeds a state machine that splits character data at markup, expands predefined and numeric references, keeps internal DTD general and parameter entities (first definition wins, external ones empty) and re-lexes them in content and in the internal subset (depth 10, 1,000,000 pending characters), resolves namespaces (first binding per element wins, the default namespace, the xml and xmlns rules, unbound prefixes), rejects duplicate attributes, applies the XML 1.0 or 1.1 character classes and the limits xml-rs had by default (names over 256 KiB, more than 65,536 attributes, 1 GiB of text, DOCTYPE or attribute value), and keeps the 16-slot event position queue that decides `CurrentLineNumber` and `CurrentColumnNumber`. pyexpat.rs builds the reader instead of `xml::ParserConfig` (the config parameter and field are gone) and reads `TextPosition` and `QualifiedName` from it. Not equal, and not observable: pyexpat never surfaced xml-rs's errors (both backends stop dispatching at the first one), so `ReaderError` is a fieldless kind without xml-rs's message text or error position, and events no longer carry what pyexpat ignored (prefixes, the namespace map, `StartDocument` and `Doctype` fields); the point where an error stops the stream (the events before it and the bytes consumed) is equal. - jiff leaves RustPython: the time module's code for targets that are neither Unix nor Windows (wasm32) uses its own calendar and a jiff-compatible strftime, and the build script dates the commit with nanocode-platform's zone reader; jiff, jiff-core, jiff-static, jiff-tzdb, jiff-tzdb-platform, portable-atomic-util and defmt (with defmt-macros and defmt-parser) leave the lock (2026-11-12). On Linux and macOS time.localtime, gmtime, mktime, strftime, asctime, ctime, timezone, altzone, daylight and tzname never reached jiff: they go through libc in rustpython-host_env and are unchanged; jiff was compiled into nanocode-cli only because rustpython-vm depended on it unconditionally and its build script used it. crates/patches/rustpython-vm/src/stdlib/time/civil.rs (non-Unix, non-Windows only) is a civil DateTime over nanocode-platform's civil_from_days and days_from_civil (now public, and days_from_civil no longer Unix-only), with jiff 0.2.39's limits (years -9999..=9999, Unix seconds -377705023201..=253402207200, the same OverflowErrors), weekday, day of year and ISO week date, and a strftime that reproduces jiff's lenient Display: flags _ 0 - ^ #, widths up to 255 (integer padding capped at 20, the space-padded negative case uncapped), colons, %C %y %g of negative years, %c %x %X %r as jiff's locale-free "%Y M%m %-d, %a %H:%M:%S" family, %f %N %.Nf, and a directive it cannot format (%Z %z %:z %Q %s on a zone-less time, unknown letters, a dangling flag, width or colon, a width past 255) written back literally from its percent sign. The system zone on those targets is what jiff's TimeZone::system() returned on wasm32-unknown-unknown without its js feature, Etc/Unknown, which behaves as UTC with abbreviation "UTC": tm_zone "UTC", tm_gmtoff 0, mktime as UTC. The current time comes from std's SystemTime (it panics on wasm32-unknown-unknown, as jiff's Timestamp::now did with its own message; nanocode's boot.py routes time.time, localtime(), gmtime(), ctime() and strftime without a tuple through the host clock, so only asctime() without arguments reaches it) or, with the wasmbind feature, from JavaScript's Date.now as jiff's js feature did. build.rs takes nanocode-platform as a build dependency: git's commit time (or the clock) is shifted by utc_offset_seconds in the build host's zone (TZ, then /etc/localtime) and printed as "%b %e %Y" and "%H:%M:%S" by hand. nanocode-platform now parses a POSIX rule in TZ with the extended (TZif v3) syntax, rule times from -167 to 167 hours, as jiff and glibc do; before, such a TZ was refused and /etc/localtime used. What is not equal: (1) on wasm32-wasi, which nanocode does not build, jiff read a zone from TZ in the WASI environment; this code uses UTC there as on wasm32-unknown-unknown; (2) with the wasmbind feature, which nothing in nanocode enables, jiff took the browser's zone from Intl and its bundled tzdb; this code uses UTC; (3) for a TZ of the permanent-DST form DST from Jan 1 0:00 to Dec 31 25:00 (EST5EDT,0/0,J365/25), jiff 0.2.39 shows standard time in the five hours after each new year and nanocode-platform (like glibc) stays in DST, which can change the build host's date string within those hours; (4) an invalid TZ falls back to /etc/localtime's zone in nanocode-platform where jiff used UTC (the same on hosts whose /etc/localtime is UTC); (5) a now() reading outside jiff's range is an OverflowError instead of a panic. Commands: cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli, cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-python --target wasm32-unknown-unknown, cargo clippy --locked -p rustpython-vm (native and wasm32), cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-platform (native and wasm32), civil 1|2|3 20000, civil 11|12|13 200000, civil bench, zones.sh, e2e.sh.
- RustPython's derive macros carry the part of syn-ext they use, and syn-ext leaves (2026-11-12). crates/patches/rustpython-derive-impl/src/syn_ext/ is syn-ext 0.5.0's attribute.rs, generics.rs, ident.rs, item.rs, meta.rs, path.rs and punctuated.rs with its `ext` and `types` modules (`AttributeExt`, `AttributeIteratorExt`, `GetIdent`, `GetPath`, `ItemAttrExt`, `ItemLike`, `ItemModExt`, `MetaAttributeExt`, `MetaExt`, the `NestedMeta*IteratorExt` traits, `PunctuatedExt`, and the syn-1-style `Meta`/`MetaList`/`NestedMeta`/`PunctuatedNestedMeta`), with syn-ext's tests, comments and feature gates (all the gates rustpython-derive-impl enabled are on) removed, `ref`/`ref mut` bindings under default binding modes dropped for edition 2024, and `ParseStream<'_>` spelled out; the derive-impl sources import `crate::syn_ext::` instead of `syn_ext::`, and the module is public because `pyclass`, `pyexception` and `pystruct_sequence*` take `PunctuatedNestedMeta`, which rustpython-derive parses with `Punctuated::parse_terminated`. Equality: output/synext-equal (run on gak-9) links the old rustpython-derive-impl (with syn-ext 0.5.0) beside a renamed copy of the new one, collects every `#[pyclass]`, `#[pyexception]`, `#[pymodule]`, `#[pystruct_sequence]`, `#[pystruct_sequence_data]` item (958) and every derive input (1,083: `derive_from_args`, `pypayload`, `pytraverse`) from rustpython-vm, rustpython-stdlib and nanocode-python, and compares the generated token streams: 4,207 checks, 4,142 identical; the other 65 (all `#[pyclass]` on impl blocks) contain the same tokens in a different order, because derive-impl iterates a HashMap when it emits items: the old crate itself produces a different order on a second call for 60 of them. `cargo metadata` 481 to 480 packages; `cargo tree -p nanocode-cli -e normal,build` 283 to 282 (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu) and 284 to 283 (aarch64-apple-darwin). `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli` on Linux and `cargo check -p nanocode-python` on aarch64-apple-darwin pass.
- widestring is a dependency of rustpython-host_env and rustpython-vm only on Windows, and leaves nanocode-cli (2026-11-12). Every use of `widestring::WideCString`/`WideCStr` and its error types in host_env (crt_fd::wopen, fileutils' Windows stat, io::open_path, nt, overlapped, winapi, winreg, winsound, wmi, the Windows time-zone names) and vm (exceptions.rs' three `ToPyException` impls, fspath/ospath `to_wide_cstring`, nt, winreg, winsound, _winapi, os.rs' Windows environment) is already behind `cfg(windows)` (or the ctypes feature nanocode does not enable), so the dependency moves to `[target."cfg(windows)".dependencies]` in both Cargo.toml files, as rustpython-stdlib already had it; no source changes. Equality: no code compiled for Linux, macOS or wasm32 changes. `cargo tree -p nanocode-cli -e normal,build` 284 to 283 (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu) and 285 to 284 (aarch64-apple-darwin); `cargo metadata` unchanged (widestring stays in Cargo.lock for Windows). `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli` and `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-python --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` on Linux and `cargo check -p nanocode-python` on aarch64-apple-darwin pass.
- RustPython's lock types are built on rustpython-common's own port of the lock_api layer, and parking_lot, parking_lot_core and lock_api leave nanocode-cli (2026-11-12). crates/patches/rustpython-common/src/lock/api.rs carries what RustPython used of lock_api 0.4.14: the raw-lock traits (`RawMutex`, `RawRwLock` with its `is_locked_exclusive` default, `RawRwLockDowngrade`, `RawRwLockRecursive`, `RawRwLockUpgrade`, `RawRwLockUpgradeDowngrade`, `GetThreadId`), the `GuardSend`/`GuardNoSend` markers, and `Mutex`/`RwLock` with their guards, mapped guards (`map`, `try_map`), `upgradable_read`/`upgrade`, `downgrade`, `read_recursive`/`try_read_recursive`, `get_mut`, `into_inner`, `raw`, `data_ptr` and the same `Send`/`Sync` bounds and `Debug` output (`Mutex { data: .. }`, `<locked>`). Without the `threading` feature (nanocode's build) every PyMutex/PyRwLock is still the Cell-based raw lock of lock/cell_lock.rs, so locking behaves exactly as before; with `threading`, lock/parking.rs adapts parking_lot's raw locks to the new traits and parking_lot becomes an optional dependency of rustpython-vm and rustpython-stdlib that only their `threading` feature enables (it is on rustpython-host_env only for Windows). The places that took a parking_lot lock outside `threading` now use std: the csv dialect registry and field limit, the interpreter-admission gate (vm/runtime.rs, gc_state.rs) and the `_interpqueues`/`_interpchannels` registries take a `rustpython_common::lock::BlockingMutex` (a `std::sync::Mutex` whose `lock` ignores poisoning, as parking_lot has none), `_interpchannels`' blocked `send()` waits on a `std::sync::Condvar` (`wait`, and `wait_timeout` to the deadline in place of `wait_until`), host_env's `AppendLog` uses `std::sync::Mutex` the same way, hashlib's per-object state is a `PyMutex`, and `_functools`' lru_cache reentrant lock is, without `threading`, a depth counter (parking_lot's reentrant mutex on one thread only ever counted). TigerStyle departure, bounded to the vendored interpreter: these are blocking std locks and a condition variable rather than nanocode-sync primitives, because RustPython's object model hands out guards from shared references everywhere and porting it to an owner-and-mailbox design is a rewrite of the interpreter; the new lock layer uses the same unsafe as lock_api (cells handed out under a held raw lock), which the vendored crates already rely on. The `threading` feature did not build before this change either (`dyn Limiter` is not `Send + Sync` in vm/runtime.rs, _thread.rs and thread.rs, checked at e86dae0d8 on gak-9) and still does not. Equality: in nanocode's configuration the raw locks, guard order and unlock points are unchanged and nothing runs on a second thread, so lock behavior is identical; the end-to-end corpus (output/e2e) exercises every object access through these locks. `cargo metadata` 481 packages before and after (the optional dependency keeps parking_lot in Cargo.lock); `cargo tree -p nanocode-cli -e normal,build` 287 to 284 (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu) and 288 to 285 (aarch64-apple-darwin). `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli`, `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-python --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` and `cargo clippy --locked -p rustpython-common -p rustpython-host_env -p rustpython-vm -p rustpython-stdlib` on Linux and `cargo check -p nanocode-python` on aarch64-apple-darwin pass.
- rustpython-host_env loses the modules nanocode's Python never compiles a user of, and its remaining system calls go through the libc calls the crate already makes; nix, memmap2, memoffset and cfg_aliases leave (2026-11-12). nanocode builds rustpython-vm and rustpython-stdlib without their `host_env` feature, so the stdlib and vm modules that called host_env's faulthandler, grp, mmap, multiprocessing, pwd, select, shm, syslog, socket (Unix), resource, posix, posix_unix_like, fcntl and thread modules (os, posix, socket, select, mmap, fcntl, grp, pwd, resource, syslog, faulthandler, _multiprocessing, posixshmem, _thread with threading) are compiled out, as the earlier termios deletion was; those 14 host_env files are deleted, and the five `ToPyException` impls in vm/src/exceptions.rs for their error types now also require `feature = "host_env"`. `builtins.input`'s session-leader test (`getsid(0) == getpid()`) moves from host_env::posix to host_env::os unchanged. What nanocode does compile is ported: time.rs's `clock_gettime`/`clock_getres` on Unix use the libc bodies the file already had for WASI, `clock_settime` and `nanosleep` build a `libc::timespec` (seconds that do not fit `time_t` are an InvalidInput error where nix's `as` cast wrapped), fileutils' `StatStruct`/`fstat` are `libc::stat`/`libc::fstat`, io.rs's directory test is `st_mode & S_IFMT == S_IFDIR` with EISDIR, `page_size` is `sysconf(_SC_PAGESIZE)`, `set_errno` writes `__errno_location()` (Linux) or `__error()` (Apple), and `copy_file_range` (only the compiled-out os module used it) is gone. These are the same system calls nix and rustix made, through the same libc the crate already calls with unsafe elsewhere (the vendored interpreter is outside the workspace's forbid(unsafe_code)). rustix leaves rustpython-host_env (it stays in Cargo.lock for nanocode-process and nanocode-tui until those move). Not equal: the `host_env` features of the vendored vm and stdlib no longer build (nanocode never enables them); `time.sleep`'s error for a failed nanosleep other than EINTR reads `nanosleep: Invalid argument` (strerror) where nix printed `nanosleep: EINVAL: Invalid argument`, a path a valid `timespec` cannot reach. Equality: nothing that was compiled into nanocode's interpreter changed behavior besides the ports above, which call the same functions; the end-to-end corpus (output/e2e, old e86dae0d8 against the branch head) covers time.monotonic, perf_counter, process_time and clock_gettime. `cargo metadata` 484 to 481 packages; `cargo tree -p nanocode-cli -e normal,build` 291 to 287 (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu) and 292 to 288 (aarch64-apple-darwin). `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli` and `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-python --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` pass on Linux, `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-python` on aarch64-apple-darwin (gak-9).
- rustpython-vm's `eval_breaker_pending` reads the eval-breaker word itself, and the `EvalBreaker::is_empty` helper the bit-set commit added goes (2026-11-12): on wasm32 nothing calls `eval_breaker_pending`, so the helper was a new dead-code warning there that bitflagset's macro-generated method never raised. Same relaxed load, same result. `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-python --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` shows only the warnings it showed at e86dae0d8.
- nanocode-telemetry carries a server host's telemetry on nanocode-observability's own span model, batch processor, OTLP exporter and subscriber, and opentelemetry, opentelemetry_sdk, tracing-subscriber, sharded-slab, thread_local, futures-executor, rand 0.9.5, rand_chacha 0.9.0, ppv-lite86, zerocopy and zerocopy-derive leave the workspace (2026-11-12; nanocode-telemetry was their last user and is not in nanocode-cli's tree; imbl stays for nanocode-sync, nanocode-durability, code mode, subagents and the Claude backend, lazy_static for x509-parser). crates/integrations/telemetry now depends on nanocode-observability, nanocode-sync, serde_json and tracing: `GenAi<E: nanocode_observability::SpanExporter>` renames spans, adds the gen_ai.* attributes, folds content events and reports `Exported` exactly as before, with opentelemetry's `Value::as_str` reproduced (bool, i64 and f64 through Display, a string array as `["a","b"]`); `Held<P: nanocode_observability::SpanProcessor>` keeps the holding, slow/error/one_in export decision, `most` limit, expiry and `Ended` callbacks, with imbl::Vector replaced inside the same `Atom` (copy-on-write, lock-free) by nanocode-sync `Map`s keyed by (trace, position) with a per-trace length and a due queue keyed by sequence number; `Lines` and `Counters` are `subscriber::Layer`s (`Counters::layer` returns a `Filtered`), `line(event)` is unchanged, `Exports::filter` returns `filter::FilterFn`, and `METRICS_TARGET` re-exports nanocode-observability's (same value). Public API changes: nanocode-observability now exports `Event`, `KeyValue`, `Resource` (with `Resource::detected()`, the SDK's default detectors, plus `insert`/`merge`), `Scope`, `SpanContext` (public fields, `INVALID`), `SpanData`, `SpanKind`, `Status`, `Text`, `Value` with public fields, the `SpanExporter` and `SpanProcessor` traits, `BatchConfig` (SDK defaults 2,048 / 5 s / 512; `with_env()` lets set and parseable OTEL_BSP_* values win, batch size capped at the queue size as the SDK does), `BatchSpanProcessor::new(exporter, config)`, `OtlpSpanExporter::build(endpoint, &resource, &scope)`, `Tracer::new(processors)`/`shutdown_with_timeout`, `OtelLayer::new(tracer)`/`OtelSpan`; `subscriber::LAYER_SLOTS` goes from 3 to 8 and `Registry::new` takes `[Option<Filtered>; N]` for any N up to 8 (slots in a boxed slice; table entries stay 128 bytes, 8 data slots of 8 bytes). nanocode-telemetry: `GenAi::export` is synchronous; `Held` implements only `on_end` and `shutdown_with_timeout` (which still releases held traces first), so `on_start`, `force_flush` and `set_resource` go. pyramid-core's crates/kernel/src/telemetry.rs migrates as follows: `Resource::builder()` plus `with_service_name("pyramid")` becomes `Resource::detected()` merged with `Resource { attributes: vec![KeyValue::new("service.name", "pyramid")], schema_url: None }` when OTEL_SERVICE_NAME is unset; opentelemetry-otlp's `SpanExporter::builder().with_http().with_protocol(HttpBinary).build()` becomes `OtlpSpanExporter::build(&endpoint, &resource, &Scope { name: "pyramid".into(), version: None })` with endpoint OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT as given, else OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT without a trailing `/` plus `/v1/traces` (headers still from OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_HEADERS/OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS; any compression variable is refused with `OtlpError::Compression`); `GenAi::new(exporter, Some(AGENT), exported)` and `Held::new(processor, holding, ended)` keep their signatures; `BatchSpanProcessor::builder(exporter, runtime::Tokio).with_batch_config(batch_config()).build()` becomes `BatchSpanProcessor::new(exporter, BatchConfig { max_queue_size: 65_536, max_export_batch_size: 2_048, scheduled_delay: Duration::from_secs(1) }.with_env())`; `SdkTracerProvider::builder().with_resource(..).with_span_processor(held).build()` becomes `Tracer::new(vec![Box::new(held)])` (sampler and span limits still from OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER/_ARG and OTEL_SPAN_*_COUNT_LIMIT) and `Traces(Option<Tracer>)` calls `tracer.shutdown_with_timeout(Duration::from_secs(10))`; `tracing_opentelemetry::layer().with_tracer(provider.tracer("pyramid")).with_filter(exports.filter())` becomes `Filtered::new(OtelLayer::new(tracer.clone()), exports.filter())`; `tracing_subscriber::registry().with(product).with(export).with(Lines(log).with_filter(filter_fn(sqlx_warning))).with(Lines(log).with_filter(filter_fn(kernel_line))).with(Counters(..).layer()).try_init()` becomes `nanocode_observability::init(Registry::new([product, export, Some(Filtered::new(Lines(log), FilterFn(sqlx_warning))), Some(Filtered::new(Lines(log), FilterFn(kernel_line))), Some(Counters(..).layer())]))` (or `tracing::dispatcher::set_global_default(Dispatch::new(..))` to skip the log bridge `init` also installs), where the product layer implements `subscriber::Layer` and comes as an `Option<Filtered>` (an unfiltered one takes `FilterFn(|_| true)`). What is not equal: the span model has no remote-parent flag, so a request root is a Server span without a parent (opentelemetry also counted a Server span with a remote parent; neither nanocode-observability's layer nor pyramid-core creates remote parents), and attribute arrays of bool, i64 or f64 are not representable (only string arrays are); pyramid's default tracing-opentelemetry context activation has no counterpart (there is no OpenTelemetry `Context::current`; parents come from tracing's span tree, the nearest exported entered span); the batch processor exports one batch at a time with blocking reqwest on its own thread instead of the Tokio-runtime processor with 4 concurrent exports, and has no force_flush; an OTEL_BSP_* variable that is set but unparsable now keeps pyramid's value where pyramid's code kept the SDK default; only http/protobuf is sent (OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL is not read); a registry holds at most 8 layers. nanocode-cli is unchanged: its tree is 261 packages before and after (`cargo tree -p nanocode-cli -e normal,build --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`), and its install path builds the same 3-slot registry and the same batch configuration from the environment. Proven with output/telemetry-equal (old = crates/integrations/telemetry at e86dae0d8 renamed, with opentelemetry 0.32.0, opentelemetry_sdk 0.32.1, tracing-subscriber 0.3.23 and imbl 7.0.2, beside the new crate; 10 seeds): GenAi over 200,000 random batches (0 to 11 spans: model.call, tool.call, tool.execute, agent and other names, renamed and provider attributes of every value type, code.module.name and target prefixes, content events of every kind with prompts, item lists, output items, reasoning, malformed JSON and non-string content, failing and succeeding inner exporters, 4 agent settings) comparing every exported span as canonical JSON, the batch results and the Exported sequence: 1,751,776 checks, 0 differences; Held over 200,000 seeded sequences (up to 39 spans over 1 to 5 traces, Server roots and children with known, unknown and missing parents, durations around a 1 h `slow` and before start, error statuses, one_in 0, 1, 2, 3, 7, 100 and u128::MAX, most 0 to 11 and 8,192, string, number, bool and array targets against holding targets, `slow` 0 for expiry at the next span and 1 h for none, then shutdown) comparing what reaches the inner processor and the Ended callbacks: 8,007,999 checks, 0 differences; Exports::filter over 400 random configurations against 3,000 random metadata each (16 targets plus random text, 5 levels, event, span and hint kinds, content_kind field presence): 1,200,000 checks, 0 differences; Lines (sqlx and kernel filters as pyramid sets them, plus an all-pass one) and Counters in one registry each over 200,000 events from 400 callsites with spans: 223,190 lines and counters, 0 differences. output/otel-equal (old opentelemetry-based stack against a copy of this crate, `python3 drive.py 20 500 40` and `20 520 40`): 280 checks over 40 scenarios, every trace, span-header and stdout check equal, 16 differing metric files all in threaded scenarios whose gauges race (old against old on the 5 threaded scenarios of the first run differs on 8 of 35 checks). `cargo metadata --locked` 462 -> 451 packages. Checks: `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli`, `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-telemetry -p nanocode-observability` native and `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-telemetry -p nanocode-observability` (no warnings); nanocode-cli is the only other workspace crate depending on either.
- nanocode-observability formats and filters tracing with its own subscriber, and tracing-subscriber leaves it (2026-11-12). `subscriber::Registry` implements `tracing_core::Subscriber` with the three ordered filtered layer slots `install` builds (fmt, OpenTelemetry spans, metrics), reproducing `registry().with(fmt).with(otel).with(metrics)` of tracing-subscriber 0.3.23: per-layer filter bits per slot (two for the metrics layer's nested `MetricsFilter` inside `scope(otel).and(filter_fn)`) set in `enabled` and consumed by `did_enable` as `FilterState` does, the combined callsite interest and `max_level_hint` of `Layered::pick_interest`/`pick_level_hint` including the None-layer and `FilterMap::any_enabled` quirks (a callsite every filter rejects still gets interest sometimes and a span that reaches no layer), visibility of a span to a layer only when its filter enabled it (`Context::span`, `lookup_current` falling back through the thread's stack, `SpanRef::parent`, `scope`, `from_root`, `event_span`), per-thread current-span stacks with duplicate enters, reference counts with close at zero and parents closed iteratively. Spans live in a paged table of 128-byte-aligned entries reused in place (ids are generation << 32 | index + 1, free lists sharded by thread, metadata interned once per callsite, each layer's span data an Arc written once at `new_span`): a first version publishing an `Arc` per span through arc-swap measured 185 ns per insert/load/remove single-threaded and 625 ns with 4 threads, so span bookkeeping now does no arc-swap writes. `subscriber::Layer` (associated per-span `Span` type, `new_span` returning it, `on_record`/`on_follows_from`/`on_event`/`on_enter`/`on_exit`/`on_close` with `SpanRef`/`Context`, `Registry::data` for code outside the subscriber) carries the fmt layer, the OpenTelemetry span layer and the metrics layer; the span layer keeps `OtelData` and its timings behind a per-span nanocode-sync `Sequencer` turn and `Slot` (its lazy start needs exclusive mutation with a synchronous result; a contended turn parks on `Sequencer::enter`), and `span_context`/`add_link` reach it through `Dispatch::downcast_ref::<Registry>()` and `Registry::data`. `format.rs`, `pretty.rs`, `json.rs` and `style.rs` reproduce the compact (no ANSI), pretty (ANSI unless NO_COLOR is set non-empty) and JSON (span list, no current span) formats byte for byte with NEW and CLOSE span events and their `time.busy`/`time.idle`, escaping, error source lists, `r#` and `log.` field rules and the RFC 3339 timestamp from `nanocode_platform::system_time` (so a simulated host's clock shows); `filter.rs` and `env_filter.rs` port `Targets`, `EnvFilter` (its directive state machine with every quirk, dynamic span and field matching, the static-max-level warning) and `scope`; `log_bridge.rs` replaces tracing-log's `LogTracer` and `NormalizeEvent` (log records become events with the record's target, file and line); `pattern.rs` matches field-value patterns with a Pike VM over the regex syntax nanocode's regex-automata build accepts (no Unicode Perl classes or case folding there), with the DFA's unanchored leftmost-first match-at-end semantics and its `x+`/`(x+)?` compilation of repetitions. Public type change: `ObservabilityError::Filter` holds `filter::ParseError` (same Display texts) instead of tracing-subscriber's; no caller matches on it. What is not equal: span ids (opaque) are numbered differently; a directive whose untrimmed text puts a multi-byte character where tracing-subscriber's trimmed byte offsets land mid-character makes tracing-subscriber panic and us return `invalid filter directive` (3,609 and 3,502 of two runs of ~285k random filter strings); field-value patterns using flag groups, class set operations (`&&`, `--`, `~~`) or negated nested classes are rejected (`invalid field filter: error building NFA`, the text regex-automata prints for its own errors) where regex-automata accepts them, and patterns needing more than 65,536 instructions are rejected; a span whose last reference drops inside another span's `on_close` on the same thread is closed and freed here while tracing-subscriber's `CLOSE_COUNT` never frees it (nor closes its parent), and a parent is closed through this registry rather than `dispatcher::get_default`; the fmt layer's busy/idle use atomics, so a span entered on several threads at once may split an overlapping instant differently (single-threaded identical), and its debug-only assertion that a closing span is not entered is gone. Proven with output/obs-subscriber (each stack installed as the global dispatcher in its own process, old = tracing-subscriber 0.3.23 with the old install code and a FormatTime printing tracing-subscriber's own datetime.rs, new = this code with a platform host returning the same fixed time; seeded sequences over 50 event and 150 span callsites across 10 targets and 5 levels: every primitive field type, strings needing escapes, Debug, Display and error values with source chains, failing Debug, empty spans, records after creation, explicit, contextual and root parents, out-of-order exits and closes, duplicate enters, follows_from, log-crate records, 1 to 3 threads in lockstep, `Span::current`/`is_disabled` markers, random timestamps from year -95,000 to 14,000): 3,640 runs of 900 random filter strings plus DEFAULT_FILTER, `DEFAULT_FILTER,nc_metrics=info`, `trace`, `info` and the empty filter in compact, JSON, pretty and pretty with NO_COLOR, 16,064 sequences, 868,126 lines, 0 differences after replacing only busy/idle values; 1,810 runs of three recorder layers in all 8 presence combinations with random filters (two of them with a filter_fn `and`), 8,272 sequences, 420,676 lines of callbacks, visibility, parents, scopes and current spans, 0 differences; 569,730 random filter strings parsed, 0 differences in Ok or error Display beyond the panics above; 450,000 random patterns against matchers 0.2.0, 18,000,000 string and Debug matches, 0 differences; 1,500,000 timestamps identical; output/otel-equal (agent 39's end-to-end OTLP harness, old pre-OpenTelemetry-port stack against this tree): 80 scenarios, 560 checks, every trace, span-header and stdout check equal, 34 differing metric files all in threaded scenarios whose gauge values race (old against old differs on 8 of 10 of them too). Interleaved benchmark, compact layer to a discarding sink, filter `warn,nanocode=info`, median of 3 rounds, ns per op old -> new (load average ~11 on 5 cores): spans created, entered, exited and closed with the layer enabled 5,212 -> 4,401 (4 threads 9,920 -> 7,912), filtered out 456 -> 173 (819 -> 715), events in a span 1,432 -> 1,279 (2,339 -> 1,627), filtered-out events 98 -> 66 (75 -> 138; this 4-thread row moved between -22% and +85% across three runs), nested span plus event 7,600 -> 6,717 (12,425 -> 12,031). `cargo metadata --locked` 469 -> 462 packages (aho-corasick, matchers, nu-ansi-term, regex-syntax, tracing-log, tracing-serde, valuable leave; tracing-subscriber, sharded-slab, thread_local and lazy_static stay for nanocode-telemetry, regex-automata for bstr); nanocode-cli reaches 261 packages instead of 270 (`cargo tree -p nanocode-cli -e normal,build --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`: tracing-subscriber, matchers, regex-syntax, nu-ansi-term, sharded-slab, thread_local, tracing-log, tracing-serde, lazy_static leave). Checks: `cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-observability`, `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-observability` native and `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli`.
- Our own argument parser replaces clap (2026-11-12; Georgios reversed "clap stays"). crates/core/arguments (nanocode-arguments, std only, native and wasm32) declares a command line as const tables (`Command`, `Group`, `Argument`, `Choice`, `Parser`) and reproduces clap 4.6.2 as nanocode used it: lexing (long `=` values, short clusters with attached and `=` values, `--`, non-UTF-8 arguments), pending values and their resolution order, env fallbacks read when parsing (empty values included, flags take only `true`/`false`), defaults, global arguments propagated down and their values merged up (a deeper level wins ties, a command-line value beats env), required, required-unless, requires and conflicts, the help subcommand and `help <path>`, `-h` and `--help` (long help with possible-value lists and next-line layout at clap's fixed 100 columns, since wrap_help was off), `-V`, bin names from argv[0], and every error clap could produce here with its usage line (including the derive's per-struct argument groups that showed up in the `unexpected value` usage), `tip:` lines, strsim's Jaro suggestions above 0.7 and `For more information, try '--help'.`. Output is built styled with clap's ANSI styles and written as anstream did: raw when the stream is a terminal and NO_COLOR, CLICOLOR_FORCE, CLICOLOR, TERM and CI allow it, otherwise through a port of anstyle-parse's VT state machine that strips escapes (the stream variant keeps parser state across printable runs, the `Display` variant the TUI's /runner uses resets it, as anstream's two strippers do). bin/nanocode/src/cli.rs keeps every struct and enum with the same fields (so Debug is unchanged) and builds them from `Matches`; commands.rs's `RunnerCommand::try_parse_from` and app.rs's reload_args (now over `COMMAND.arguments()`) keep their shape. Downstream: `nanocode_observability::ObservabilityOutputArgs` keeps its name and `log_file`, `log_filter`, `enabled` and `builder`, and gains `ARGUMENTS` and `from_matches`; its clap `Args`/`FromArgMatches` impls are gone, so `#[command(flatten)]` over it no longer compiles; tempoxyz/pyramid and tempoxyz/pyramid-core reference neither it nor nanocode-observability (GitHub code search, default branches). `CuaCommand::BrowserHost::args` gets `#[allow(dead_code)]`: clap's generated reader was its only reader. Not equal: on Windows consoles without VT support anstream translated styles through wincon and we write ANSI; on targets other than unix and Windows a non-UTF-8 attached value (`--cd=<bytes>`) is an invalid-UTF-8 error, since std has no safe way to split such an OsStr there. Equality (output/clap-equal: clap 4.6.2 with the verbatim origin/master definitions beside the new tables, in-process): 24,806,166 checks, 0 differences over seeds 2 to 10 (1.62M argv cases from the real flag set with typos, `=`/separate values, repeats, `--`, non-UTF-8 bytes, 9 argv[0] forms and random env for all 20 env-backed arguments; each compares styled bytes, Display bytes, stream, exit code and parsed Debug, plus reload_args twice, /runner parses and errors, and 8.1M fuzzed strings through both strippers against anstream; seed 1 found the stream stripper's state carry-over, fixed); a pty harness running the old and new parsers as binaries under pty, pipes and mixed stdout/stderr with 12 env sets (NO_COLOR set/empty, CLICOLOR_FORCE=1, CLICOLOR=0/1, TERM=dumb/unset, CI, COLUMNS=40, escape bytes in env values) and 3 argv[0]: 6,480 runs (2,310 styled), run before and after rebasing, 0 differences. Commands: cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli, cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-arguments (also --target wasm32-unknown-unknown), cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-arguments, -p nanocode-observability --lib and -p nanocode-cli (clean). clap, clap_builder, clap_derive, clap_lex, anstream, anstyle, anstyle-parse, anstyle-query, anstyle-wincon, once_cell_polyfill, colorchoice, is_terminal_polyfill, utf8parse and strsim leave; heck stays for sqlx-macros-core. Packages 484 -> 471. `cargo metadata` 484 -> 471 packages at 1f10a22ea, 482 -> 469 on deps2-obs after the OpenTelemetry change (the 14 crates in the title leave, nanocode-arguments joins; heck stays for sqlx-macros-core).
- nanocode-cli keeps mimalloc and libmimalloc-sys (2026-11-12, measured for the ~0-dependencies round, left to the coordinator as asked: the system allocator is not within noise). output/alloc-bench links the nanocode crate (no default features, local-cells, as nanocode-cli does) in a release build twice, with and without `mimalloc::MiMalloc` (0.1.52, no_thp) as the global allocator, on a 4-worker Tokio runtime; medians of 7 interleaved rounds on this 5-core Linux Hand at load 12-17, system -> mimalloc: 400 Code Mode cells on each of 8 concurrent tasks (a cell builds, stringifies and parses 400 objects in djs, then the task round-trips an agent transcript item through serde_json) user CPU 1.313 -> 1.149 s (-12.5%), wall 1.743 -> 1.364 s, max RSS 11.8 -> 14.3 MB; 4 tasks serializing and parsing 200 batches of 500 transcript items each and freeing them on another task user 2.713 -> 2.025 s (-25%), wall 4.412 -> 2.770 s, max RSS 97.9 -> 93.1 MB; process start (runtime built, then exit, 140 runs) 28 ms wall and 11.3 MB for both. This agrees with the 2026-11-10 entry (20,000-agent swarm user CPU 61.3 -> 54.6 s, resident 2.6-2.9 -> 2.1-2.2 GB) and the no_thp entry's start-up numbers. Dropping it would cost 12-25% CPU on allocation-heavy agent work for 2 packages and a C build (libmimalloc-sys through cc, which ring already needs); replacing it means writing an allocator, which this round was told not to do. Commands: cd output/alloc-bench; cargo build --release (and --features mi); python3 measure.py 7.
- nanocode-observability records spans and metrics with its own OpenTelemetry model, and opentelemetry, opentelemetry_sdk and tracing-opentelemetry leave nanocode-cli (2026-11-12, Georgios: "make this ~0 deps"). What the three did for the CLI is now in crates/integrations/observability: model.rs (values, span context, status, events, resource, scope, `ExportError`), trace.rs (the tracer: ParentBased(AlwaysOn) sampling and `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER`/`_ARG`, the 128 attribute, event and link limits and their `OTEL_SPAN_*_COUNT_LIMIT` variables, span and trace ids from a per-thread xoshiro256++ seeded by `nanocode_platform::fill_random`, start, record, end and shutdown), layer.rs (the tracing layer: tracing-opentelemetry 0.33's builder-then-started span lifecycle, `otel.name`/`otel.kind`/`otel.status_code`/`otel.status_description`, location, thread and target attributes, events, error fields and exception attributes, follows_from links, busy_ns/idle_ns), metrics.rs (the `monotonic_counter.`/`counter.`/`histogram.`/`gauge.` instruments, instrument name validation, sum, last-value and explicit-bucket aggregation with the default bounds, the 2,000 attribute-set cardinality limit and its overflow set, cumulative, delta and low-memory temporality, one periodic reader thread per exporter with `OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL`) and batch.rs (the batch span processor with the `OTEL_BSP_*` variables), all lock-free (`nanocode_sync::Atom` and `Map`, atomics, channels); otlp.rs, protobuf.rs, otlp_http.rs and file.rs now encode that model (typed.rs's integer restoration moved into the HTTP exporter). Public API: `ObservabilityError::OTelSdk` carries `nanocode_observability::ExportError` (the same Display texts as `OTelSdkError`), and `SpanContext`, `span_context(&Span)` and `add_link(&Span, SpanContext)` replace `OpenTelemetrySpanExt::context`/`add_link` in bin/nanocode/src/telemetry.rs; tempoxyz/pyramid-core and tempoxyz/pyramid do not use nanocode-observability (GitHub code search). nanocode-telemetry still depends on opentelemetry and opentelemetry_sdk for its public `GenAi`/`Held` (used by pyramid-core), so both stay in Cargo.lock; tracing-subscriber stays for now (its registry holds the per-span state). bin/nanocode names futures-util's `async-await-macro` feature for `futures_util::join!`, which futures-executor under opentelemetry_sdk used to switch on by feature unification. Proven equal with output/otel-equal, which links the old crate (a copy of 1ca10117c's nanocode-observability with opentelemetry 0.32.0, opentelemetry_sdk 0.32.1, tracing-opentelemetry 0.33.0 at the locked versions) beside a copy of the new one: (1) the JSON and protobuf encoders over 40,000 seeded random batches (escapes, unicode, integer-looking strings, NaN/inf/-0.0, string arrays, events, links, every kind and status, both schema URLs): 199,414 checks, 0 differences; (2) end to end, 164 seeded scenarios each run as two processes (old, new) through `ObservabilityBuilder::install` with the local OTLP directory and a mock OTLP/HTTP collector, driving random span trees (explicit, contextual and rootless parents, records before and after a span starts, 140-event and 140-record bursts past the limits, follows_from, `span_context`/`add_link`, error fields and error values with sources, every metric prefix including invalid names, case-colliding names and u64 above i64::MAX) under 7 filters, both telemetry levels and 12 environments (limits, the samplers, OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES and OTEL_SERVICE_NAME, delta and LowMemory temporality, small batches); timestamps, busy_ns/idle_ns and process.pid normalized, ids renamed by first appearance, resource attributes and data points sorted: traces.jsonl, metrics.jsonl, the protobuf trace and metric requests and stdout all equal in every single-threaded scenario (1,148 checks), and every span equal in the scenarios with two extra threads; the metric differences left in threaded scenarios (racing gauge last values) appear at the same rate between two runs of the old stack (26 of 126 checks on the same 18 seeds, against 26 of 126 old against new). Not equal, by design: resource attributes and metric data points are written in insertion order (the old SDK iterated a HashMap, so its order changed from process to process); a data point's attributes are its first measurement's field order (the old SDK exported either that or the sorted order, whichever key its HashMap met first); metric attribute sets compare f64 values by bit pattern (old: a NaN attribute never matched itself, so each NaN measurement took a new set up to the cardinality limit, and 0.0/-0.0 hashed apart); duplicate keys in one attribute set keep the first by a stable sort (old: unstable); ids are random either way but come from a different generator; a span that follows itself is linked to itself (tracing-opentelemetry deadlocked on its own mutex; the harness avoids that case); the batch processor does not join its thread after it acknowledges shutdown; the resource still reports telemetry.sdk.name/language/version opentelemetry/rust/0.32.1 and the meter scope tracing/tracing-opentelemetry 0.33.0, so collectors see what they saw. Invalid OTEL_* values are ignored as before, because the OpenTelemetry specification requires that and the variables are shared with other programs. Hot path, release harness, 200,000 iterations, 5 interleaved rounds at load 12-14, median ns per operation old -> new: a span with a field, an event inside and a record 6,283 -> 5,071; a parent entered with a child 8,663 -> 8,127; a span and event filtered out 518 -> 535; a metrics event with a histogram and a counter 308 -> 1,022 (each measurement is a copy-on-write `Atom` update with one allocation instead of the SDK's atomic add or mutex; the CLI emits these per terminal frame and loop wakeup, about 0.1 ms a second at 60 frames). `cargo metadata` 489 -> 487 packages (tracing-opentelemetry, web-time); nanocode-cli's tree (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu and aarch64-apple-darwin) loses futures-executor, opentelemetry, opentelemetry_sdk, ppv-lite86, rand, rand_chacha, tracing-opentelemetry and zerocopy. Commands: cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli; cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-observability; cargo clippy --locked --lib -p nanocode-observability; cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-cli; in output/otel-equal: target/debug/otel-equal encode 20000 7 and 20000 99, python3 drive.py N SEED ROOTS, target/release/otel-equal bench old|new DIR 200000.
- `nanocode-turnlog` (crates/core/turnlog) and `nanocode_agent::OneLog` make one append-only log per scope, with one writer, the host's only durable store: `nanocode_log (seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, scope, body)` and `nanocode_snap (scope PRIMARY KEY, seq, body) WITHOUT ROWID` (2026-11-12). It replaces four writers on Durable Objects (the SessionLog event log, the RowStore checkpoint, the cell journal and the host's markers). A row body is JSON lines of `Record`s, and each durable point is one `INSERT ... RETURNING CAST(seq AS TEXT)` with no reads. A cold start reads one snapshot, then the tail after it. Rows are written only at A (admission), C (before a call of effect class External, through `EffectGate` for direct tools, `OneLogJournals` for Code Mode calls and `OneLog::effect` for in-object writes), F (finish, cancel or withdraw), a cancel request (committed before its acknowledgement), R (start of a turn that was unfinished at open, with its attempt and its open External calls reported as unknown), Floor (the first row of an incarnation) and Progress (a Durable checkpoint while the last row is a turn's R). Statuses, events, checkpoints (latest payload per state), tool results and cell journal updates are buffered and go into the next row. A snapshot is written when snapshot bytes plus tail bytes exceed 2 x the encoded fold. The rule "tail >= snapshot" wrote one on every new scope's first commit (1.28 rows/turn in the simulator against 0.14). `Policy.max_row_bytes` splits a row into parts that commit in the same tick, and a record that is too large alone is an error. `EffectClass::{External (default), Idempotent, None}`: `EffectClass::mcp(read_only, resumable)` derives MCP tools, read-only built-ins are None, and an undeclared tool is External. The checkpoint stays a record because a backend's `DurableState` cannot be derived from events. Event seqs: a reopen adds `EVENT_GAP` (1 << 14) to the last durable event seq, and the incarnation's first row carries `Floor`. Without the floor, the simulator reused a seq a client had seen in 54 of 5000 seeds (seed 1682): an incarnation that started idle published live events and crashed before any row. `Policy.restarts` caps consecutive R rows without log progress, and then the turn finishes Failed. Without Progress rows, 3479 of 38177 healthy turns hit the cap from restarts across the whole object, against 2468 with them. Exact attribution needs a durable "response arrived" marker and is not done. Gaps: no migration from SessionLog or RowStore data, hand tools are not declared Idempotent by default (their names come from each hand's catalog), and the event history lives in the fold, so a long session holds it in memory. Measured with output/turnlog-check (native Claude Code Mode against a scripted Messages mock, MemoryLog and SqlLog over SQLite, 10 turns): plain 2 rows (A+F), one External call 3 (A+C+F), one None call 2, and 0 warm reads. A crash while `charge` runs gives R+C+F, no second charge, 1 model call and "outcome unknown". A model that never answers with restarts = 3 gives A, R, R, R, then F Failed. Hosted on durable-cloudflare's workerd harness (`node output/sqlturn/run.mjs text|tool|reply 10`, nanocode-ts on this crate), a turn writes 2.0 rows with 3.0 statements and 3.0 event-loop commits, against 23.4/24.4/14.2 rows, 39.2/40.2/27.1 statements and 5.0/5.0/4.0 commits on 052f73db2. `npm run drill` passes. In the crash matrix, losing the commit in flight gives 0 double charges (as before). Rolling back two commits already confirmed can drop the C row after the charge ran, which workerd's output gate rules out. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-turnlog -p nanocode-tool-host -p nanocode-mcp-tools -p nanocode-agent -p nanocode`, the same with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, and `cargo clippy` with `-D warnings`.
- bin/nanocode-sim `--scenario turns` simulates a Durable Object turn host and runs a durability policy behind `TurnDurability` over a `LogHost` disk (disk.rs, one lock-free `Slot`) (2026-11-12). Each tick's appends, snapshots, workspace writes and subagent registrations commit atomically at its end. An output gate releases model requests, tool dispatches, acks and events only after that commit. A rolled-back seq is reused as SQLite's max+1 reuses it. The object crashes before commits (up to 8% per seed), after commits before output (up to 4%), at timed crashes, at deploys during long model calls, and on every attempt of a poison turn. The fault profiles add commit and read faults. The workload has multi-step scripted turns that call Read (None), Hand (Idempotent ledger), Charge (External ledger), Write (workspace) and Spawn. Clients resubmit, reconnect with after=<seq> and cancel, and client-less turns are redelivered until acked. `--policy reference` (onelog.rs) has a switch per protection (`--without admission|call_external|call_in_object|finish|progress|restart|result|snapshot`, `--live-seqs temporary|gap|reuse|floor`). `--policy turnlog` drives nanocode-turnlog through `SimHost`. tidy.rs now scans crates/core/turnlog. Invariants and canaries (`--mutation`): a charge applies at most once (`gate_releases_early`), a workspace write or spawn applies at most once (`tick_not_atomic`), every accepted turn ends durably (`recovery_skips_clientless`), a completed Idempotent call is never reported unknown (`idempotent_reported_unknown`), every event seq a client saw names that event in the durable log (`durable_seq_before_commit`, `seal_skipped`), and a turn reports one ending (`finish_before_row`). Each protection off on the reference policy (seeds 0..5000): no admission row loses turns in 4248 seeds, no C row before External calls charges twice in 1051, no C row on in-object ticks applies writes twice in 2827, no finish row fails liveness in 3780 and gives two endings in 1220, no restart row or cap crash-loops in 2133, and reused live seqs fail in 1516. Without the result row, snapshots or progress rows no invariant fails: they trade cost for fewer unknown outcomes (3667 vs 8806), cold reads (19.8 vs 25.0 rows) and fewer healthy turns capped. Results: `sweep.sh 0 100000 4 --scenario turns --policy turnlog --twice` and the same for the reference policy pass with 0 panics, and so do 20,000 seeds with `--calm` and with `--row-limit 1024`. Re-run on 2026-11-12: turnlog seeds 20000..23000 and reference 20000..22000 with `--twice` pass. Calm rows/turn are 3.11 for turnlog (A 1.00, C 1.11, F 1.00) and 3.80 for reference (with T 0.54 and S 0.14). Under faults they are 5.38 and 5.58. Turnlog writes 3.8x the bytes calm because a checkpoint rides in every row, and with no result row it reports a completed charge unknown 8987 times against 3667. Not modeled: hosts that commit each split part separately.
- smallvec leaves nanocode-types-core: `ResponseItem::AgentMessage`'s `content` is a `Vec<AgentMessageContent>` instead of a `SmallVec<[AgentMessageContent; 1]>` (2026-11-12). Both serialize as a JSON array and deserialize from one, so the wire bytes are the same; `ResponseItem` stays 184 bytes (its largest variant is another one), and a message's content now always lives on the heap instead of inline when it has one item, one allocation per agent message parsed. Public API change: the field's type; code that built the content with `smallvec!` or `SmallVec::from` builds a `Vec`, and reading it (`iter`, indexing, `len`) is unchanged; no workspace crate built one, and tempoxyz/pyramid-core and tempoxyz/pyramid do not name `ResponseItem::AgentMessage` (code search, no hits). Proven with output/types-equal, which builds nanocode-types-core as of e86dae0d8 (with smallvec 1.15.1) beside the new one: 200,000 seeded JSON documents (single items and arrays of two; `agent_message` with and without id, author and recipient, content missing, null, an object, a string, or 0 to 5 items that are input_text, encrypted_content, unknown types or missing fields, strings with escapes, surrogate pairs and non-ASCII text, extra fields), each parsed by both and compared as re-serialized bytes, error text and `serde_json::Value`: 400,000 checks, 0 differences (59,085 parsed as `AgentMessage`, the rest as errors or `Other`). `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-types-core` natively and for wasm32-unknown-unknown, `cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-types-core`, `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli`. `cargo metadata --locked` stays at 489 packages: smallvec stays in the lock through hyper, icu_normalizer, idna and parking_lot_core.
- rustix leaves the workspace's crates: nanocode-process, nanocode-tui and nanocode-sandbox make their system calls through nanocode-sys's `unix` module, and nanocode-chatgpt-extension locks with std's `File::lock` (2026-11-12). crates/core/sys/src/unix.rs holds safe libc wrappers for what rustix did: `read` (an `io::Error` from errno, so callers match `WouldBlock` and `Interrupted` where they matched `Errno::AGAIN` and `INTR`), `set_close_on_exec` (`F_SETFD` to `FD_CLOEXEC` or 0, as `fcntl_setfd`), `status_flags`/`set_status_flags` (`F_GETFL`/`F_SETFL`), `set_nonblocking` (`FIONBIO`, as `ioctl_fionbio`), `duplicate_close_on_exec` (`F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC`), `redirect_input` (`dup2` onto stdin), `inherited_descriptor` (adopts a descriptor named on the command line after `F_GETFD` confirms it is open), `reap_children` (`waitpid(-1)` until `ECHILD`), `readable_now` (a zero-timeout `poll` for `POLLIN`), `Termios` with `terminal_attributes`/`set_terminal_attributes` (`tcgetattr`, `tcsetattr(TCSANOW)`), `make_raw` (rustix's linux_raw `cfmakeraw`, the same flags written out, so no unsafe) and `end_of_file` (`VEOF`), `window_size`/`set_window_size` (`TIOCGWINSZ`/`TIOCSWINSZ`), `open_pseudoterminal` (on Linux `/dev/ptmx` opened `O_RDWR|O_NOCTTY|O_CLOEXEC` with `ENOSPC` reported as `EAGAIN`, `TIOCSPTLCK`, `TIOCGPTN` and `/dev/pts/N`, as rustix's `openpt`, `unlockpt` and `ptsname`, `grantpt` being a no-op there; on Apple `posix_openpt`, `FD_CLOEXEC`, `grantpt`, `unlockpt` and `TIOCPTYGNAME`), `lead_session` (the `pre_exec` hook: the given signals back to `SIG_DFL`, `setsid`, `TIOCSCTTY` on stdin), `open_file_limit`/`set_open_file_limit` (`RLIMIT_NOFILE`, `RLIM_INFINITY` as `None` as rustix maps it) and on Linux `send_descriptor`/`receive_descriptor` (one byte with an `SCM_RIGHTS` control message, flags 0 on send and `MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC` on receive; the first descriptor is kept and any others closed, as draining rustix's buffer did). Group and process kills use the existing `nanocode_platform::unix::signal_group`/`signal_process` with `SIGKILL` (the `killpg`/`kill` rustix made), a zero pid skipped as `Pid::from_raw` did. nanocode-process loses its `unsafe_code = "deny"` exception and takes the workspace's `forbid`: its `pre_exec` hook and `OwnedFd::from_raw_fd` moved into nanocode-sys. Unsafe code added to nanocode-sys (unix.rs), each a libc call on descriptors borrowed through `AsFd` or owned by the function: `read` into the caller's buffer with its length; `fcntl` (`F_SETFD`, `F_GETFL`, `F_SETFL`, `F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC`, `F_GETFD`), `dup2`, `ioctl` (`FIONBIO`, `TIOCGWINSZ`, `TIOCSWINSZ`, `TIOCSPTLCK`, `TIOCGPTN`, `TIOCPTYGNAME` into a 128-byte buffer, `TIOCSCTTY`) and `poll` with pointers to locals of the type each request writes; `tcgetattr` into a `MaybeUninit` read only after success and `tcsetattr` from a `termios` we hold; `waitpid` with a null status; `getrlimit`/`setrlimit` with local `rlimit`s; `open`/`posix_openpt`/`grantpt`/`unlockpt` on NUL-terminated paths; `OwnedFd::from_raw_fd` only on descriptors a successful call just returned (`open`, `F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC`, `recvmsg`'s `SCM_RIGHTS`) or that `inherited_descriptor` confirmed open and that the parent handed over on our command line (its one caller, handover.rs's reader, owns them alone); `signal`, `setsid` and `ioctl` inside `pre_exec` (async-signal-safe calls between fork and exec); and in `send_descriptor`/`receive_descriptor` a zeroed `msghdr` pointing at a local one-byte `iovec` and a `u64` control buffer of `CMSG_SPACE(4)` bytes, `CMSG_FIRSTHDR`/`CMSG_NXTHDR`/`CMSG_DATA` walked within it and the descriptors read unaligned. Not equal: `TIOCSCTTY` gets the argument 0 where rustix passed the address of a zero (which Linux reads as a nonzero steal flag), so only a privileged process taking a terminal that is already another session's controlling terminal would differ, and `lead_session` opens a fresh terminal that no session has; handover's reader skips a descriptor argument that is not open instead of adopting it, and clears `O_NONBLOCK` with the same `F_GETFL`/`F_SETFL`; sandbox's `channel` no longer has a "no room to pass a descriptor" error, since the buffer is sized for the one descriptor it sends; `open_pseudoterminal` exists for Linux and Apple only, the platforms nanocode builds for. Proven with output/sys-unix, linking rustix 1.1.4 beside nanocode-sys and running both on the hosted Hand (Linux 6.x): 200 rounds of pipe reads (empty nonblocking reads, readiness before and after data, counts and bytes), `FD_CLOEXEC`, `O_NONBLOCK` through `FIONBIO` and through `F_SETFL`, `F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC` at 50 lower bounds; 100 pseudoterminal pairs from each (descriptor and status flags, the controller's target, window sizes set and read crosswise, `tcgetattr` fields, raw mode applied and read back, restore, echo through the pair); `RLIMIT_NOFILE` read, set to four values and refused above the maximum (same errno); 200 descriptors passed over socket pairs with every mix of our and rustix's send and receive (close-on-exec set, same pipe, data through); a message without a descriptor; a child made session leader with a controlling terminal by our hook and by the rustix one; children reaped until `ECHILD`: 4,614 checks, 0 differences, in three runs. `cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-process -p nanocode-tui -p nanocode-sandbox -p nanocode-chatgpt-extension`, `cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-sys -p nanocode-process -p nanocode-tui --target aarch64-apple-darwin`, `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli`. `cargo metadata --locked` stays at 489 packages: rustix and linux-raw-sys remain in the lock through the vendored rustpython-host_env, which the python scope owns.
- arc-swap leaves the workspace: `nanocode_sync::Swap`, `SwapOption`, `Guard` and `Atom`'s storage are nanocode-sys's own lock-free Arc swap, on native and WASM alike (2026-11-12). crates/core/sys/src/swap.rs keeps arc-swap's design, a debt list: each thread claims a node (leaked, 128-byte aligned, reused after the thread exits; found in a push-only list) with 8 guard slots (arc-swap's `DEBT_SLOT_CNT`) and one transient slot for `load_full`; a load publishes the pointer it read in a free slot and confirms the storage still holds it, so a `Guard` costs no reference count; a writer that swapped a value out walks every slot, pays each debt on that value by adding a reference and marking the slot paid, and only then lets its own reference go; dropping a `Swap` pays the debts on its value (guards may outlive it), dropping an `Atom`'s `Enclosed` does not, since its `with` and `load_full` never let a debt escape (as the patched arc-swap's `Enclosed` did). Two places differ from arc-swap on purpose. (1) When the confirm fails and the debt was already paid, arc-swap keeps the paid reference as its value, but the writer that paid it may hold a different object that reused the address (even of another type, from another storage); here the payment names the paid object's type (`Releaser::<T>::RELEASE`, a `&'static` release function written into the slot), the reader gives that reference back through it and retries on (2) a pending load instead of arc-swap's generation-tagged helping slot: the reader announces the storage's address in the slot, reads the pointer and turns the announcement into a debt with one compare-exchange; a writer of that storage that meets the announcement first replaces it with a reference to a value it loads at that moment, so the reader returns a value the storage held during its call. (3) A paid slot stays paid until its guard drops, where arc-swap frees it at payment and lets a later guard's drop take over another guard's debt. `nanocode_sync`'s `Swap`/`SwapOption` keep arc-swap's API that the workspace calls (`new`, `from_pointee`, `empty`, `const_empty`, `load`, `load_full`, `store`, `swap`, `compare_and_swap` with `&Arc`, `&Option<Arc>`, `&Guard` or a raw pointer, `rcu`, `into_inner`, `Default`, `From`, `Debug`, `Display`; `Guard::into_inner`, `from_inner`, `Deref`); the WASM build drops its take-and-put wrapper (sync's swap.rs) and nanocode-types-core, nanocode-tui and the patched rustls-platform-verifier use nanocode-sys's types; crates/patches/arc-swap and its `[patch.crates-io]` entry are deleted. Public API change: `nanocode_sync::Swap`, `SwapOption` and `Guard` are `nanocode_sys::Swapped`/`Guard` instead of aliases of arc-swap's types (arc-swap's `map`, `Access`, `Cache`, strategies and weak pointers, which nothing used, are gone); tempoxyz/pyramid-core does not name them (code search for arc_swap, SwapOption, nanocode_sync::Guard: no hits) and tempoxyz/pyramid uses its own arc-swap. Unsafe code added to nanocode-sys (swap.rs): `Arc::from_raw` in `Raw::from_raw` for `Arc` (asserts non-null) and `Option<Arc>`, called by `Guard::owned`, `Swapped::{into_inner, load_full, swap}` and `Enclosed::{load_full, swap, compare_and_swap}` on a reference the caller owns (from `into_raw`, a storage's own reference, a paid debt or a load that added one); `P::from_raw` inside `ManuallyDrop` in `load_guard` for a confirmed debt, which keeps the value alive until the guard drops and is never dropped unless the debt was paid; `Arc::increment_strong_count` in `increment` (the value is kept alive by a debt or the storage's reference the caller holds); `Arc::from_raw` in `release` (the caller owns one reference); the dereference in `release_paid_debt` (slots tagged as paid debts are only written by `pay` with the address of a `&'static Release`); `ManuallyDrop::take` in `Guard::into_inner` (the guard is never dropped) and `ManuallyDrop::drop` in `Guard`'s drop (only when the guard owns its reference). Not equal: strong counts while a paid guard is alive (point 3: arc-swap's is one higher until another guard on the slot drops; final counts equal), `Debug` of a WASM `Swap` prints `ArcSwapAny(..)` as the native one did instead of `Swap(..)`, and the corner cases of points 1 and 2. Proven with output/sys-swap, linking arc-swap 1.9.2 (crates.io; the vendored copy differed only by `Enclosed`) beside nanocode-sys: 200 seeds of 20,000 random operations over three `Swap`s, two `SwapOption`s and up to 40 held guards (load, load_full, store, swap, compare_and_swap matching and not, rcu, guards dropped or turned into `Arc`s in random order) comparing every value, plus the strong count of every object whenever no guard is held and after everything is dropped: 6,616,429 checks, 0 differences; a stress run of 2, 4, 8 and 16 threads x 400,000 operations over shared storages, `Enclosed`s, short-lived `Swap`s, guards passed between threads and up to 12 guards held per thread, each value checked for a live canary on every read: 3,615,185 objects created and dropped exactly once; a monotonic run (4 readers alternating `load` and `load_full`, a writer storing 1..2,000,000 and publishing each after its store returns): no reader saw a value go back or fall below a published one; the same harness under AddressSanitizer (nightly, 541,406 objects) clean, and under Miri (weak memory, preemption rate 0.1, 20 runs: harness seeds 1 and 2 under 4 and 16 Miri scheduler seeds) with no undefined behaviour or data race. Benchmarks (release, single thread, 60 interleaved rounds of 1M operations, min/median ns on the loaded 5-core Hand): `load` and read 12.2/34.1 arc-swap against 12.1/37.5; `load_full` 26.3/69.9 against 24.9/73.4; `Atom::read`'s `with` 12.2/34.9 (arc-swap `load`) against 10.9/35.0; `store` 102.6/286.5 against 25.3/80.0; new and drop of a `Swap`'s storage 173 to 347 ns against 31 to 79 ns for `Enclosed`. `cargo check --locked --workspace`, `cargo check --locked --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p nanocode-sync -p nanocode-types-core -p nanocode-sys -p nanocode`, `cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-sys -p nanocode-sync -p nanocode-types-core -p nanocode-tui` (and the first three for wasm32), `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli`. `cargo metadata --locked`: 490 -> 489 packages (rustversion stays through encoding_rs).
- crossbeam-utils leaves nanocode-sync: `Slot`, `Mailbox`'s desk and the slow-wait holders keep their values in nanocode-sys's owned atomic pointers (2026-11-12). crates/core/sys (nanocode-sys) is new: the one workspace crate whose lints allow unsafe code (with `unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn` denied), holding only what needs it, each unsafe block minimal and behind a safe API; every other crate keeps `unsafe_code = "forbid"` (or the deny it had). Its first module, atomic.rs: `AtomicBox<T>` (an `Option<Box<T>>` in an `AtomicPtr`: `new`, `empty`, `swap`, `take`, `store`, `Sync` for `T: Send` as crossbeam's `AtomicCell` was), `AtomicArc<T>` (the same for `Option<Arc<T>>`, which the WASM `Swap` holds) and `AtomicStatic<T>` (an `Option<&'static T>`: `load`, `store`). Its unsafe code: `unsafe impl<T: Send> Sync for AtomicBox<T>` (shared access only moves whole boxes in and out and never lends a `&T`); `Box::from_raw` in `reclaim_box` and `Arc::from_raw` in `reclaim_arc` (every non-null pointer in a cell came from `Box::into_raw` or `Arc::into_raw` and is owned by the cell alone, and `swap` and `drop` take it out exactly once); `as_ref` in `AtomicStatic::load` (only null or a pointer made from a `&'static T` is ever stored). Orderings are crossbeam's for pointer-sized cells: swap `AcqRel`, load `Acquire`, store `Release`, and a store into an owning cell is a swap that drops the old value, as `AtomicCell::store` does for types that need dropping. Equal: output/sys-atomic links crossbeam-utils 0.8.22 beside nanocode-sys: 200 seeds of 50,000 random swap, take and store operations on `Option<Box<_>>` comparing every returned value and the drop counts, 200 seeds of 20,000 `&'static Location` stores and loads, and 2, 4 and 8 threads swapping 500,000 values each through either cell, where every value must come out exactly once: 23,329,284 checks, 0 differences. Benchmarks (release, interleaved, 5 rounds): take and store 10.0 to 10.5 ns with crossbeam against 9.8 to 11.0 ns; 4 threads of 2M swaps 228 to 261 ms against 234 to 276 ms. `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-sync -p nanocode-sys` natively and for wasm32-unknown-unknown, `cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-sys -p nanocode-sync` on both targets, `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli`. `cargo metadata --locked`: 489 -> 490 packages, since crossbeam-utils stays in the lock through rustpython-vm and rustpython-stdlib and nanocode-sys is a new workspace package.
- `binascii.b2a_base64` (and through it `base64.b64encode` and friends) encodes with rustpython-common's own RFC 4648 base64, and base64 0.23 leaves nanocode-cli (2026-11-12). crates/patches/rustpython-common/src/binascii.rs encodes each 3-byte group into 4 characters of the standard alphabet with `=` padding for a final group of 1 or 2 bytes into a buffer sized up front (plus the optional newline), which is what base64's `general_purpose::STANDARD.encode` produced; decoding was already the port of CPython's `a2b_base64` there. The crate's `binascii` feature no longer names `dep:base64`. base64 0.23.1 stays in Cargo.lock for other workspace crates. Equality: output/base64-equal compares base64 0.23.1 with the new function, with and without the newline, over 3,000,000 seeded inputs of 0 to 69 bytes plus one of 4,096 bytes every 1,000 rounds: 6,000,000 checks, 0 differences. `cargo metadata` 484 packages before and after; `cargo tree -p nanocode-cli -e normal,build` 292 to 291 (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu) and 293 to 292 (aarch64-apple-darwin). The three changes from here down to the bit sets were checked together with `cargo check -p nanocode-cli`, `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-python --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` and `cargo clippy --locked -p rustpython-ruff_python_ast -p rustpython-common`.
- The ruff AST's name segments keep their inline storage in a fixed array of eight `&str` with a length, and arrayvec leaves (2026-11-12). crates/patches/rustpython-ruff_python_ast/src/name.rs: `SegmentsStack` is `[&str; 8]` plus `len` (unused slots hold `""`, so no uninitialized memory and no unsafe code), with the five operations `SegmentsVec` used of `ArrayVec<&str, 8>`: `try_from_slice` (`None` past 8), `try_push` returning the rejected segment, `try_extend_from_slice` that changes nothing when the slice does not fit, `pop` and `remaining_capacity`; covariance in the lifetime, which the removed note said ruled out SmallVec, holds for the array as it did for ArrayVec. The spill rules, capacities on spilling and `Debug`, `PartialEq`, `Hash` and `Deref` are unchanged. Equality: output/ruff-equal runs the old `SegmentsVec` (with arrayvec 0.7.8) and the new one side by side through 300,000 random sequences of up to 20 pushes, pops, slice extends and iterator extends (exact and unknown size hints) from 0 to 11 initial segments, comparing contents, spilled state and `Debug` after every step, plus `From<[&str; 8]>`: 3,719,657 checks, 0 differences. `cargo metadata` 485 to 484 packages; `cargo tree -p nanocode-cli -e normal,build` 293 to 292 (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu) and 294 to 293 (aarch64-apple-darwin). `cargo check -p rustpython-ruff_python_ast` passes.
- The ruff parser's `leading_quote` picks the longest string, bytes or template prefix that starts the literal by scanning the prefix tables, and aho-corasick leaves nanocode-cli (2026-11-12). crates/patches/rustpython-ruff_python_ast/src/str.rs built an anchored leftmost-longest Aho-Corasick DFA over the 6 prefix tables at first use; an anchored leftmost-longest match is the longest pattern that is a prefix of the input, so `leading_quote` is now the maximum length over the tables' patterns that `content` starts with (the patterns are distinct), with no lazily built automaton. It is used only by `raw_contents`, not on the parse path. aho-corasick 1.1.4 stays in Cargo.lock for other workspace crates.
